title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試録序
粤稽成周賢書之貢必加禮
受三物之教必曰賔興所以
重其事而為為士者勸也其
在當時多士濟濟吉人藹藹
用致乗拱無為既醉太平之
治殆亦有由然哉洪惟我
===
朝
列聖代作
皇上一德相承科目取士尤加崇
重故自鄉舉貢春官進對
大廷
賜名進士俾得釋褐拜秩沾被
恩榮勸勵之意至矣盡矣江西文
punctuated:
江西鄉試録序

粤稽成周，賢書之貢必加禮受，三物之教必曰賔興，所以重其事而為為士者勸也。其在當時，多士濟濟，吉人藹藹，用致乗拱無為、既醉太平之治，殆亦有由然哉！洪惟我朝列聖代作，皇上一德相承，科目取士，尤加崇重。故自鄉舉貢春官，進對大廷，賜名進士，俾得釋褐拜秩，沾被恩榮，勸勵之意，至矣盡矣！江西文
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

When we examine the era of the Established Zhou, the presentation of the registers of the worthy was always received with added ritual courtesy, and the instruction in the Three Matters was always termed the "invitation and elevation of guests"; this was the means to attach great weight to the affair and to serve as an encouragement for those who were scholars. At that time, the multitude of scholars was dignified and numerous, and the virtuous men were harmonious and abundant, whereby they brought about a governance of ruling with hands folded in non-action [Note: 乗拱 is a graphic error for 垂拱] and of the Great Peace celebrated in the ode "Already Drunk" (Jizui)—surely there was a reason for this!

Reflecting on how in our August Dynasty a succession of Sacred Emperors have arisen one after another, and His Majesty the Emperor has inherited the throne with the same pure virtue, the selection of scholars through the examination categories has been held in even greater esteem and importance. Thus, from being recommended at the provincial level and presented to the Ministry of Rites, to advancing to reply at the Great Court, they are bestowed the title of metropolitan graduate (jinshi), enabling them to cast off their coarse woolens, receive official rank, and be bathed in Imperial favor and glory—the intention of encouraging and inspiring them has reached the utmost perfection! Jiangxi is a province of literary…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
肅臣藩古今名臣偉器胥此
馬出肆當大比賓興之歲時
則有若太監葉達奉
命鎮守監察御史夏塤按節分𨗳
方岳重臣秪率彝典舉行百
爾程度咸正罔缺比鎖院也
內則綜理於監察御史楊銓
===
而戒飭防範之愈嚴躬親於
左布政使黃琮按察使原傑
左參政胡淵副使張鎣而提
督監蒞之無至外則協規於
右布政使宋欽右參政楊文
琳副使章繪左參議唐宗僉
事余複程亨宋儒朱華應欽
punctuated: 肅臣藩，古今名臣偉器胥此馬出。肆當大比賓興之歲，時則有若太監葉達奉命鎮守，監察御史夏塤按節分𨗳，方岳重臣秪率彝典，舉行百爾，程度咸正罔缺。比鎖院也，內則綜理於監察御史楊銓，而戒飭防範之愈嚴；躬親於左布政使黃琮、按察使原傑、左參政胡淵、副使張鎣，而提督監蒞之無至；外則協規於右布政使宋欽、右參政楊文琳、副使章繪、左參議唐宗、僉事余複、程亨、宋儒、朱華、應欽、
translation_en: …[a province of] flourishing culture [文, from previous page] and reverent subjects, from which famous ministers and great talents of both past and present have all emerged [reading 馬 as 焉]. Now, in the year of the triennial Grand Competition and the ceremonial sending forth of worthy guests [for the examinations], there were such officials as Grand Defender Eunuch Ye Da 葉達, who by Imperial command served as Grand Defender; Investigating Censor Xia Xun 夏塤, who held his insignia of authority on a regional tour of inspection; and the senior provincial officials, who reverently followed the established statutes and carried out all matters so that every procedure and standard was proper and without deficiency. When the examination compound was locked, on the inside matters were comprehensively managed by Investigating Censor Yang Quan 楊銓, making the admonitions and security precautions all the more strict; and personally attended to by Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Huang Cong 黃琮, Surveillance Commissioner Yuan Jie 原傑, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Yuan 胡淵, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Ying 張鎣, leaving nothing undone [reading 無至 as 兼至 or 無不至 [?]] in their direction and supervision. On the outside, regulations were jointly coordinated by Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Song Qin 宋欽, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Yang Wenlin 楊文琳, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Hui 章繪, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Tang Zong 唐宗, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Yu Fu 余複, Cheng Heng 程亨, Song Ru 宋儒, Zhu Hua 朱華, Ying Qin 應欽,…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
王遴而贊相維持之益力玉
等忝竊甄別黜陟之柄尤各
凝神注思徯幾簡閱而不敢
玩視忽取是蓋同一薦賢爲
國之公心可以臨之天地而無
愧質之鬼神而無歉十有三
郡士若干輩爭執所長引觚
===
洒翰謦欬於三場角勝負
於寸晷懽聲雷動銳氣霄騰
誠太平之瑞應擴人文以宣
朗旬有餘日繼之以夜閱卷
累千而詳擇之得千百焉由
千百而精擇之得累百十焉
又累百十而益精之得數滿
punctuated: 王遴，而贊相維持之益力。玉等忝竊甄別黜陟之柄，尤各凝神注思，徯幾簡閱，而不敢玩視忽取。是蓋同一薦賢爲國之公心，可以臨之天地而無愧，質之鬼神而無歉。十有三郡士若干輩，爭執所長，引觚洒翰，謦欬於三場，角勝負於寸晷。懽聲雷動，銳氣霄騰，誠太平之瑞應，擴人文以宣朗。旬有餘日，繼之以夜，閱卷累千，而詳擇之，得千百焉；由千百而精擇之，得累百十焉；又累百十而益精之，得數滿
translation_en: … and Wang Lin 王遴, whose assistance and support became ever more strenuous. I, Yu 玉, and my colleagues, unworthily entrusted with the authority to distinguish, promote, and reject, each concentrated our minds and focused our thoughts, looking forward to carefully examining the papers and not daring to treat them lightly or make selections carelessly. In this, all shared the same impartial commitment to recommending worthies for the state—a commitment with which we could face Heaven and Earth without shame, and stand before ghosts and spirits without regret. Some thousands of scholars from the thirteen prefectures contended in displaying their strengths, taking up writing tablets and wielding their brushes, voicing their learning across the three sessions and vying for victory within brief spans of time. Joyful voices rumbled like thunder and spirited vigor soared to the skies—truly an auspicious sign of an era of great peace, expanding literary culture and making it shine forth brightly. For more than ten days, continuing on into the nights, we read papers by the thousands, and by selecting from them in detail, obtained a thousand or several hundred; from those thousand or several hundred we selected with greater refinement, obtaining several hundred or tens; and from those several hundred or tens we refined our selection still further, until the number obtained reached a full …

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
百而除五焉蓋惟解額是遵
而取之弗容過也已而第其
氏名與其文辭尤粹者録録
以傳授〔王〕序夫惟文者德之
著名者實之符群士子仰沐
聖化樂育滋久既以是德著而爲
文復以是文播而爲名又以
===
是名登貢賢之書預賓興之
列駸駸步武亨衢亦曰達矣
達而至於達也其不自茲始
乎然其達也豈徒文具名稱
云乎哉宜必激昂奮發竭知
攄忠思效多士吉人所爲于
以贊
punctuated: 百而除五焉，蓋惟解額是遵，而取之弗容過也。已而第其氏名與其文辭尤粹者，録録以傳，授〔王〕序。夫惟文者德之著，名者實之符。群士子仰沐聖化，樂育滋久，既以是德著而爲文，復以是文播而爲名，又以是名登貢賢之書，預賓興之列，駸駸步武亨衢，亦曰達矣。達而至於達也，其不自茲始乎？然其達也，豈徒文具名稱云乎哉？宜必激昂奮發，竭知攄忠，思效多士吉人所爲，于以贊
translation_en:
… one hundred less five, for this strictly adheres to the provincial quota, and in selecting them it is not permissible to exceed it. Thereafter, they ranked their names and the purest of their compositions, compiling a record to be transmitted, and entrusted it to [me, Wang,] to write a preface.

Now, literature is the manifestation of virtue, and reputation is the tally of substance. Looking up, the assembled scholars have been bathed in the sacred transformative influence and joyfully nurtured for a long time. Having already manifested this virtue as literature, and again spread this literature as reputation, they now by means of this reputation ascend into the register of tribute-worthy men of talent and join the ranks of those recommended as guests of the state. Steadily striding along the smooth thoroughfare of officialdom, they may indeed be called successful. Ascending from this success to ultimate attainment—does it not begin right here? Yet in their success, how could it be a matter of mere literary trappings and empty reputation? They ought surely to be roused and inspired, exhausting their wisdom and pouring forth their loyalty, longing to emulate the deeds of the many fine scholars and virtuous men of old, so as to assist in…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
治化而佐太平庶幾文德做濟
名實相須而
聖朝興賢勸士之效足以暴白天
下後世而於歷科前哲益有
光矣先儒恕齋王先生有言方其
取以辭章類若浮文而必實
及其臨政設施奮其事業隱
===
然爲國君臣者不可勝數玉
於是錄亦深有望於羣士子
云
天順三年八月穀旦直隸河
間府儒學教授四明邵玉序
punctuated:
治化而佐太平，庶幾文德做濟，名實相須，而聖朝興賢勸士之效，足以暴白天下後世，而於歷科前哲益有光矣。先儒恕齋王先生有言：「方其取以辭章，類若浮文而必實；及其臨政設施，奮其事業，隱然爲國君臣者，不可勝數。」玉於是錄，亦深有望於羣士子云。
天順三年八月穀旦，直隸河間府儒學教授四明邵玉序。
translation_en:
… governance and transformation and assist in bringing about Great Peace. In this way, literary virtue and practical accomplishments will complement one another [?], name and reality will correspond to each other, and the efficacy of the Sacred Dynasty in promoting the worthy and encouraging scholars will be sufficient to be made manifest to all under heaven and to future generations, adding ever greater luster to the worthy predecessors of past examinations. The former Confucian scholar Master Wang of Shuzhai once said: "When men are first selected by means of their literary compositions, it seems like mere flowery writing, yet it must be grounded in substance; when they subsequently take up governance and implement measures, exerting themselves in their achievements, those who stand as weightily reliable ministers for the state are too numerous to count." In compiling this record, I, Yu, likewise place deep hopes in all these gentlemen.

Written as a preface on an auspicious day in the eighth month of the third year of the Tianshun era (1459) by Shao Yu 邵玉 of Siming, Instructor in the Confucian School of Hejian Prefecture in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili).

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第一場
四書
夫子何哂由也曰為國以禮其言不讓是
故哂之唯求則非邦也與安見方六
七十如五六十而非邦也者唯赤則
非邦也與宗廟會同非諸侯而何赤
也為之小孰能為之大
誠者不勉而中不思而得從容中道聖人
也誠之者擇善而固執之
學
===
之審問之慎思之明辨之篤行之　有
弗學學之弗能弗措也有弗問問之
弗知弗措也有弗思思之弗得弗措
也有弗辨辨之弗明弗措也有弗行
行之弗篤弗措也人一能之己百之
人十能之己千之
雞鳴而起孳孳為善者舜之徒也
易
剛上而尚賢能止健大正也不家食吉養
punctuated:
第一場

四書

「夫子何哂由也？」曰：「為國以禮，其言不讓，是故哂之。」「唯求則非邦也與？」「安見方六七十，如五六十，而非邦也者？」「唯赤則非邦也與？」「宗廟會同，非諸侯而何？赤也為之小，孰能為之大？」

誠者，不勉而中，不思而得，從容中道，聖人也。誠之者，擇善而固執之者也。博學之，審問之，慎思之，明辨之，篤行之。有弗學，學之弗能，弗措也；有弗問，問之弗知，弗措也；有弗思，思之弗得，弗措也；有弗辨，辨之弗明，弗措也；有弗行，行之弗篤，弗措也。人一能之，己百之；人十能之，己千之。

雞鳴而起，孳孳為善者，舜之徒也。

易

剛上而尚賢，能止健，大正也。不家食吉，養
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"Master, why did you smile at You [Zilu]?" He replied: "A state is governed through ritual propriety, yet his words lacked modesty; that is why I smiled at him." "When it comes to Qiu [Ran Qiu], was it not a state that he spoke of?" "Where has one ever seen a territory of sixty or seventy li square, or fifty or sixty li square, that did not constitute a state?" "And when it comes to Chi [Gongxi Hua], was it not a state?" "Ancestral temples and diplomatic assemblies—what are these the affairs of, if not the feudal lords? If Chi were to play a minor role in them, who could play a major one?"

He who possesses sincerity hits the mark without effort and apprehends without thought; naturally and easily he abides in the Way—this is the sage. He who attains to sincerity is one who chooses the good and holds fast to it. [There seems to be an omission of "者也博" in the original print before "學":] Study it extensively [?], inquire into it accurately, think over it carefully, sift it clearly, and practice it earnestly. While there is anything not studied, or while in what he has studied he has not yet mastered it, he will not give up; while there is anything not inquired into, or while in what he has inquired into he does not yet understand it, he will not give up; while there is anything not thought over, or while in what he has thought over he has not yet apprehended it, he will not give up; while there is anything not sifted, or while in what he has sifted it is not yet clear to him, he will not give up; while there is anything not practiced, or while in what he has practiced he is not yet earnest, he will not give up. If another man succeeds by one effort, he will use a hundred efforts; if another man succeeds by ten efforts, he will use a thousand.

He who rises at cockcrow and diligently pursues goodness is a follower of Shun.

Book of Changes (Yi)

The firm ascends and honors the worthy; being able to halt strength—this is great correctness. "Not eating at home brings good fortune" means nourishing…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
賢也
上九弗損益之无咎貞吉利有攸往得臣
无家象曰弗損益之大得志也
藉用白茅无咎子曰苟錯諸地而可矣藉
之用茅何咎之有慎之至也夫茅之
為物薄而用可重也慎斯術也以往
其无所失矣勞謙君子有終吉子曰
勞而不伐有功而不德厚之至也語
以其功下人者也德言盛禮言恭謙
也者致恭以存其位者也
聖人以此洗心退藏於密吉凶與民同患
神以知來知以藏往
===
書
禹曰都帝慎乃在位帝曰俞禹曰安汝止
惟幾惟康其弼直惟動丕應徯志以
昭受上帝天其申命用休帝曰吁臣
哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞帝曰臣作
朕股肱耳目
punctuated:
賢也。
上九，弗損益之，无咎，貞吉，利有攸往，得臣无家。象曰：弗損益之，大得志也。
藉用白茅，无咎。子曰：苟錯諸地而可矣，藉之用茅，何咎之有？慎之至也。夫茅之為物薄，而用可重也。慎斯術也以往，其无所失矣。勞謙君子，有終，吉。子曰：勞而不伐，有功而不德，厚之至也。語以其功下人者也。德言盛，禮言恭。謙也者，致恭以存其位者也。
聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往。
書
禹曰：「都！帝，慎乃在位。」帝曰：「俞。」禹曰：「安汝止，惟幾惟康，其弼直，惟動丕應徯志，以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。」帝曰：「吁！臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」禹曰：「俞。」帝曰：「臣作朕股肱耳目。
translation_en:
… the worthy.”

“Top Nine: Without diminishing, one increases it. There is no blame. Constancy brings good fortune. It is favorable to have somewhere to go. One obtains servants without a private family. The Commentary on the Images says: ‘Without diminishing, one increases it’: one greatly achieves one’s will.”

“‘Placing it on a mat of white couch-grass, there is no blame.’ The Master said: ‘Simply placing it on the ground would suffice; if one places it on a mat of couch-grass, what blame could there be? It is the utmost of caution. Now, couch-grass as a thing is trifling, yet its use can be weighty. Going forward with caution according to this method, one will suffer no loss.’ ‘Toiling and yet humble, the superior man has a good end; good fortune.’ The Master said: ‘Toiling without boasting, having merit without claiming it as a virtue—this is the utmost of generosity. It speaks of one who, despite his merit, places himself below others. Virtue is spoken of in terms of fullness; ritual is spoken of in terms of reverence. Humility means utmost reverence in order to preserve one’s position.’”

“The sage uses these to cleanse his heart, retiring and storing them in secrecy, sharing the anxieties of good fortune and misfortune with the people. Spiritual, he knows what is to come; wise, he stores up what is past.”

Book of Documents (Shu)

“Yu said: ‘Oh! Emperor, be cautious regarding the position you occupy.’ The Emperor said: ‘Yes.’ Yu said: ‘Rest calmly in your proper stopping place. Attend to the subtle springs of things and to peace; let your assistants be upright. Then when you act, there will be a grand response, for they await your will, so that you manifestly receive the favor of the Lord on High, and Heaven will renew its mandate with blessings.’ The Emperor said: ‘Alas! Ministers! Associates! Associates! Ministers!’ Yu said: ‘Yes.’ The Emperor said: ‘My ministers act as my legs and arms, my ears and eyes.’”

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
岷山導江東別爲沱又東至于澧過九江
至于東陵東迆北會于匯東爲中江
入于海
乃汝盡遜曰時敘惟曰未有遜事
非佞折獄惟良折獄罔非在中察辭于差
非從惟從哀敬折獄明啓刑書胥占
咸庶中正其刑其罰其審克之
詩
既見君子庶幾說懌
===
既醉而出並受其福醉而不出是謂伐德
飲酒孔嘉維其令儀
截彼淮浦王師之所王旅嘽嘽如飛如翰
如江如漢如山之苞如川之流緜緜
翼翼不測不克濯征徐國
秋而載嘗夏而楅衡白牡騂剛犧尊將將
毛炰胾羹籩豆大房萬舞洋洋孝孫
有慶俾爾熾而昌俾爾壽而臧保彼
東方魯邦是常
punctuated:
岷山導江，東別爲沱，又東至于澧，過九江，至于東陵，東迆北，會于匯，東爲中江，入于海。
乃汝盡遜，曰時敘；惟曰未有遜事。
非佞折獄，惟良折獄，罔非在中。察辭于差，非從惟從。哀敬折獄，明啓刑書胥占，咸庶中正。其刑其罰，其審克之。

詩
既見君子，庶幾說懌。
既醉而出，並受其福；醉而不出，是謂伐德。飲酒孔嘉，維其令儀。
截彼淮浦，王師之所。王旅嘽嘽，如飛如翰，如江如漢，如山之苞，如川之流，緜緜翼翼，不測不克，濯征徐國。
秋而載嘗，夏而楅衡。白牡騂剛，犧尊將將，毛炰胾羹，籩豆大房，萬舞洋洋。孝孫有慶，俾爾熾而昌，俾爾壽而臧。保彼東方，魯邦是常。

"From Mount Min he channeled the Jiang; to the east it branched off to form the Tuo; further east it reached the Li; it passed the Nine Jiang and reached Dongling; trending east and slanting north, it joined at the confluence; to the east it became the Middle Jiang and entered the sea."
"Should they all defer to you, saying that things are thereby in order, you must say that there are as yet no deferential deeds."
"It is not the eloquent who should decide criminal cases; it is the upright who should decide criminal cases, without ever departing from impartiality. Examine discrepancies in testimony; do not blindly follow, yet follow what is right. With compassion and reverence decide criminal cases; open clearly the books of punishments and consult them together, so that all may approximate impartiality and correctness. Book of Odes (Shi):
"Having seen the noble man, / Hopeful that his heart will be pleased."
"When guests leave once they are tipsy, / Host and guests alike receive blessing; / To get drunk and not take leave / Is what is called ruining virtue. / Drinking wine is very fine, / Provided it is done with good deportment."
"Held in order were those banks of the Huai, / The station of the royal army. / The royal troops were numerous and strong, / Like creatures flying, like wings soaring, / Like the Jiang, like the Han, / Like the base of a mountain, / Like the rushing current of a river; / In continuous and orderly array, / Inscrutable and invincible, / Grandly marching against the state of Xu."
"In autumn we perform the chang sacrifice, / Having in summer fitted the crossbars to the bulls' horns. / There are the white bull and the red one, / The victim-shaped goblets in grand array, / Singed pig, sliced meat, and broth, / Bamboo and wooden vessels and the great stand, / And the wan dance in all its splendor. / The filial descendant receives blessing: / May they make you glorious and prosperous, / May they make you long-lived and good! / Protect those eastern regions, / Holding the state of Lu forever."

translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"Men of Chu made an incursion into Zheng." [2nd year of Duke Xi] "Men of Chu attacked Zheng." [3rd year of Duke Xi] "The Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Baron of Cao to make an incursion into Cai; Cai collapsed, and thereupon they attacked Chu, halting at Xing." [4th year of Duke Xi] "The Earl of Zheng fled home and did not take part in the covenant." [5th year of Duke Xi] "Men of Chu attacked Song." [26th year of Duke Xi] "Men of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song." [27th year of Duke Xi] "The Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought with men of Chu at Chengpu; the army of Chu was utterly defeated." [28th year of Duke Xi] "The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Xu, and the Viscount of Ju, and made a covenant at Jiantu." [28th year of Duke Xi]

"The Duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Baron of Cao, met the King's Heir Apparent at Shouzhi." title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
人秦人宋人陳人衛人鄭人齊人曹
人邾人薛人鄫人盟于蜀〔成公二年〕叔
孫豹會晉趙武楚屈建蔡公孫歸生
衛石惡陳孔奐鄭良霄許人曹人于
宋〔襄公二十七年〕叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公
子圍齊國弱宋向戌衛齊惡陳公子
招蔡公孫歸生鄭罕虎許人曹人于
虢〔昭公元年〕公會晉侯及吳子于黄池
〔哀公十三年〕
宋人及楚人平〔宣公十五年〕齊侯使國佐如師
〔成公二年〕吳伐我〔哀公八年〕
===
禮記
天子之五官曰司徒司馬司空司士司寇
典司五衆
是故先王之制禮也不可多也不可寡也
唯其稱也
顯揚先祖所以崇孝也身比焉順也明示
後世教也
punctuated:
人、秦人、宋人、陳人、衛人、鄭人、齊人、曹人、邾人、薛人、鄫人盟于蜀〔成公二年〕。叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚屈建、蔡公孫歸生、衛石惡、陳孔奐、鄭良霄、許人、曹人于宋〔襄公二十七年〕。叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕。公會晉侯及吳子于黄池〔哀公十三年〕。
宋人及楚人平〔宣公十五年〕。齊侯使國佐如師〔成公二年〕。吳伐我〔哀公八年〕。
禮記
天子之五官，曰司徒、司馬、司空、司士、司寇，典司五衆。
是故先王之制禮也，不可多也，不可寡也，唯其稱也。
顯揚先祖，所以崇孝也；身比焉，順也；明示後世，教也。
translation_en:
…a man of Chu, a man of Qin, a man of Song, a man of Chen, a man of Wei, a man of Zheng, a man of Qi, a man of Cao, a man of Zhu, a man of Xue, and a man of Zeng made a covenant at Shu [2nd year of Duke Cheng]. Shusun Bao met with Zhao Wu of Jin, Qu Jian of Chu, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Shi E of Wei, Kong Huan of Chen, Liang Xiao of Zheng, a man of Xu, and a man of Cao at Song [27th year of Duke Xiang]. Shusun Bao met with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, a man of Xu, and a man of Cao at Guo [1st year of Duke Zhao]. The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin and the Viscount of Wu at Huangchi [13th year of Duke Ai].
The people of Song and the people of Chu made peace [15th year of Duke Xuan]. The Marquis of Qi sent Guo Zuo to go to the army [2nd year of Duke Cheng]. Wu attacked us [8th year of Duke Ai].

Record of Rites (Liji)
The five officers of the Son of Heaven are called the Minister of Instruction (situ), the Minister of War (sima), the Minister of Works (sikong), the Director of Servitors (sishi), and the Minister of Justice (sikou); they have charge over the five multitudes.
Therefore, when the former kings instituted the rites, they could neither be made too much nor too little, but only commensurate with what is fitting.
To glorify and extol one's ancestors is the means to exalt filial piety; to associate oneself therein is compliance; to clearly display this to posterity is instruction.

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
席小卿次上卿大夫次小卿士庶子以次
就位於下獻君君舉旅行酬而后獻
卿卿舉旅行酬而后獻大夫大夫舉
旅行酬而后獻士士舉旅行酬而后
獻庶子俎豆牲體薦羞皆有等差所
以明貴賤也
第貳場
論
天下治成
===
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢擢蔡義為光祿大夫給事中詔
擬唐以宋璟為刑部尚書西京留守誥
擬宋太宗幸國子監賜直講孫奭五品服
謝表
判語〔五條〕
制書有違
漏使印信
私鑄銅錢
punctuated:
席，小卿次上卿，大夫次小卿，士、庶子以次就位於下。獻君，君舉旅行酬，而后獻卿；卿舉旅行酬，而后獻大夫；大夫舉旅行酬，而后獻士；士舉旅行酬，而后獻庶子。俎豆、牲體、薦羞，皆有等差，所以明貴賤也。

第貳場
論
天下治成
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢擢蔡義為光祿大夫給事中詔
擬唐以宋璟為刑部尚書西京留守誥
擬宋太宗幸國子監賜直講孫奭五品服謝表
判語〔五條〕
制書有違
漏使印信
私鑄銅錢
translation_en:
… seats, the junior ministers rank after the senior ministers, the grand masters rank after the junior ministers, and the servicemen and sons of concubines take their places below in order. A toast is offered to the ruler, and after the ruler raises his cup to initiate the general exchange of toasts, a toast is offered to the ministers; after the ministers raise their cups to initiate the general exchange of toasts, a toast is offered to the grand masters; after the grand masters raise their cups to initiate the general exchange of toasts, a toast is offered to the servicemen; after the servicemen raise their cups to initiate the general exchange of toasts, a toast is offered to the sons of concubines. The sacrificial stands and platters, the portions of the sacrificial victims, and the food offerings and delicacies are all graded by rank, which is the means of making clear the distinction between the noble and the base.

Second Session

Discourse:
"The Governance of All Under Heaven Is Accomplished"

Imperial Edicts, Patents of Appointment, and Memorials (candidates are examined on one of these):
Draft an imperial edict of the Han dynasty promoting Cai Yi 蔡義 to Grand Master of the Palace and Palace Steward.
Draft a patent of appointment of the Tang dynasty appointing Song Jing 宋璟 as Minister of Justice and Regent of the Western Capital.
Draft a memorial of thanks on behalf of Assistant Lecturer Sun Shi 孫奭 of the Song dynasty upon Emperor Taizong 太宗 visiting the Directorate of Education and bestowing upon him fifth-rank robes.

Legal Judgments (five items):
Violating an Imperial Decree
Omitting the Impression of an Official Seal
Privately Minting Copper Coins …

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
辨明冤枉
冒破物料
第三場
策五道
問欽惟
太祖高皇帝御製大誥三編
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝五倫書皆扶世導民之典也其立
言雖殊要皆納天下於皇極也夫建極
===
以人倫為至且以五倫言之君臣父子
兄弟夫婦朋友五者之名義可得聞歟
或謂有天屬者有人合者又謂天屬有
賴於人合者何所見歟書之所載有謂
人君躬行於上卿大夫表式於下者有
古今家識書為屏風者有田宅財物盡
與其弟者有叩頭謝罪富不易妻者有
即變姓名懷銀往贖其子者之數者可
知其人歟求其有合於三誥二書所紀
punctuated:
辨明冤枉
冒破物料

第三場
策五道

問：欽惟太祖高皇帝《御製大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，宣宗章皇帝《五倫書》，皆扶世導民之典也。其立言雖殊，要皆納天下於皇極也。夫建極以人倫為至，且以五倫言之：君臣、父子、兄弟、夫婦、朋友，五者之名義可得聞歟？或謂有天屬者，有人合者；又謂天屬有賴於人合者，何所見歟？書之所載，有謂人君躬行於上、卿大夫表式於下者，有古今家誡書為屏風者，有田宅財物盡與其弟者，有叩頭謝罪、富不易妻者，有即變姓名、懷銀往贖其子者，之數者可知其人歟？求其有合於三《誥》、二書所紀
translation_en:
Exonerating Wrongful Accusations
Fraudulently Wasting Materials

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: We reverently reflect that the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Yuzhi Dagao) personally composed by Grand Progenitor the Lofty Emperor (Taizu Gao Huangdi), the two books Secret Rewards of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Exemplars of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi) by Grand Ancestor the Cultured Emperor (Taizong Wen Huangdi), and the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) by Ancestor of Xuan the Accomplished Emperor (Xuanzong Zhang Huangdi) are all canonical works for sustaining the age and guiding the people. Although their words differ, in essence they all bring the realm into the August Ultimate (huangji). Now, in establishing the Ultimate, human relationships are paramount. Speaking in terms of the Five Relationships: may we hear an account of the names and meanings of these five—ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and friend and friend? Some say that among them are those bound by Heaven and those joined by man; others say that those bound by Heaven depend upon those joined by man—what is the basis for this view? Among the accounts recorded in the Book [of the Five Human Relationships], there is one stating that when the ruler personally practices them above, the high ministers and great officers serve as models below; there is one who inscribed ancient and modern family admonitions (jiajie [transcribed as jiashi 家識]) on a folding screen; there is one who gave all his fields, houses, and property to his younger brother; there is one who kowtowed to apologize and refused to change his wife when rich; and there is one who immediately changed his surname and given name and carried silver in his bosom to go ransom his friend's son—can the identities of these several figures be known? If we seek out how they correspond to the words and deeds recorded in the three Pronouncements and the two books…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
言行可指言與諸士子於
聖教漁汗服膺有素請詳陳之以驗貫通之學
問風俗美惡厚薄古今不同而世道之盛
衰關焉三代以前上無異政下無
異尚異情風俗之美且厚非後世所能
及果何道以致之歟周衰贏秦并六國
以有天下惟貴變詐峻刻風俗嘗趨於
薄矣炎漢肇興七制之君豈無有能變
而歸於厚者乎武帝好大喜功窮兵黷
武風俗嘗趨於虛矣繼世之君豈無有
能變而歸於實者乎魏晉以來稍慕通
達輕滅禮法風俗又趨於浮矣李唐啓
祚三宗之主亦有能變而歸於醇者乎
以至五季之衰也汴宋太祖應期受禪
奄有寰宇一變而正夷俗其視漢唐二
世風俗爲何如胡元之亡也我
===
朝
太祖高皇帝應天順人統有天下一變而復□
punctuated:
言行，可指言與？諸士子於聖教漁汗服膺有素，請詳陳之，以驗貫通之學。
問：風俗美惡厚薄，古今不同，而世道之盛衰關焉。三代以前，上無異政，下無異尚異情，風俗之美且厚，非後世所能及，果何道以致之歟？周衰，贏秦并六國以有天下，惟貴變詐峻刻，風俗嘗趨於薄矣。炎漢肇興，七制之君，豈無有能變而歸於厚者乎？武帝好大喜功，窮兵黷武，風俗嘗趨於虛矣。繼世之君，豈無有能變而歸於實者乎？魏晉以來，稍慕通達，輕滅禮法，風俗又趨於浮矣。李唐啓祚，三宗之主，亦有能變而歸於醇者乎？以至五季之衰也，汴宋太祖應期受禪，奄有寰宇，一變而正夷俗，其視漢、唐二世，風俗爲何如？胡元之亡也，我朝太祖高皇帝應天順人，統有天下，一變而復□
translation_en:
…words and deeds, can they be pointed out and discussed? You gentlemen have long been steeped in [?] and taken to heart the sagely teachings; please set them forth in detail so that we may test the thoroughness of your learning.

Question: Whether customs and morals are fine or base, generous or mean, differs between antiquity and the present, and upon this hinges the flourishing or decline of the moral order of the world. Before the Three Dynasties, those above had no divergent policies, and those below had no divergent preferences or sentiments; the beauty and generosity of their customs could not be matched by later ages. By what Way indeed was this brought about? When the Zhou declined, the Ying clan of Qin annexed the Six States to possess the empire; valuing only deceit and harsh severity, customs once tended toward meanness. When the fiery Han first rose, among the sovereigns of the Seven Institutional Reigns, could there have been none able to transform customs and return them to generosity? Emperor Wu loved grandeur and delighted in achievements, exhausting his troops in endless warfare, so that customs once tended toward emptiness. Among the sovereigns of the succeeding generations, could there have been none able to transform them and return them to substance? From the Wei and Jin onward, men increasingly admired unconstrained liberality and slighted or destroyed ritual and law, so that customs again tended toward frivolity. When the Li clan of Tang inaugurated its dynastic fortune, among the rulers of the Three Ancestors, were there also those able to transform customs and return them to purity? Down to the decline of the Five Dynasties, Taizu of the Bian Song responded to the appointed time, received the abdication, and came to possess the whole world, in a single transformation rectifying barbarian customs. Compared with the two eras of Han and Tang, how did its customs stand? With the fall of the barbarian Yuan, Emperor Taizu Gao of our Dynasty responded to Heaven and accorded with men, uniting and possessing the empire, and in a single transformation restored [?]…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
風其視唐虞三代風俗為何若諸子積
學有年襃然應舉而來宜有知其說者
願著于篇
問大學中庸聖賢傳心之閫奧也大學經
首言三綱領而申以止至善何不及明
德新民歟次言八條目而詳夫明德新
民何不及止至善歟傳釋綱領而外有
本末章何歟釋條目皆以兩事老而獨
誠意自為一章又何歟格物致知章亡
===
矣朱子取程子之意補之何不效曾子
作傳之體歟中庸首言性道教繼獨言
道何不及性教歟二十一章獨言性教
何不言道歟且兩言性教亦有分別歟
名篇之義前不之及而以性道教言之
何歟第十一章既曰此篇大旨以知仁
勇為入道之門至二十章又曰誠者實
此篇之樞紐何歟首章所謂一篇之體
要末章又謂舉一篇之要而約言之其
punctuated:
風，其視唐、虞、三代風俗為何若？諸子積學有年，襃然應舉而來，宜有知其說者，願著于篇。
問：《大學》、《中庸》，聖賢傳心之閫奧也。《大學》經首言三綱領，而申以止至善，何不及明德、新民歟？次言八條目，而詳夫明德、新民，何不及止至善歟？傳釋綱領而外，有本末章，何歟？釋條目皆以兩事老，而獨誠意自為一章，又何歟？格物、致知章亡矣，朱子取程子之意補之，何不效曾子作傳之體歟？《中庸》首言性、道、教，繼獨言道，何不及性、教歟？二十一章獨言性、教，何不言道歟？且兩言性、教，亦有分別歟？名篇之義，前不之及，而以性、道、教言之，何歟？第十一章既曰此篇大旨以知、仁、勇為入道之門，至二十章又曰誠者實此篇之樞紐，何歟？首章所謂一篇之體要，末章又謂舉一篇之要而約言之，其…
translation_en:
…customs—how did they compare to the customs of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties? You gentlemen have accumulated learning for many years and have come forward in distinction to answer the examination call; surely there are those among you who know the explanation of these matters. I wish you to set it forth in your essays.

Question: The Great Learning (Daxue) and the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) are the profound inner recesses through which the sages and worthies transmitted the mind. The classic text (jing) of the Great Learning begins by stating the Three Guiding Principles (san gangling) and then elaborates upon "resting in the highest good" (zhi zhishan); why does it not touch upon "manifesting luminous virtue" (mingde) and "renewing the people" (xinmin)? Next it states the Eight Steps (ba tiaomu), detailing the manifestation of luminous virtue and the renewal of the people; why does it not touch upon resting in the highest good? Aside from the chapters explaining the Guiding Principles, the commentary (zhuan) also has a chapter on the root and branches (benmo); why is this? The explanations of the Steps all pair two items together [?], yet "making the thoughts sincere" (chengyi) alone forms a chapter by itself; why is this as well? The chapter on "investigating things and extending knowledge" (gewu zhizhi) was lost, and Master Zhu [Zhu Xi] took the meaning of the Masters Cheng [Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi] to supplement it; why did he not imitate the style in which Master Zeng [Zengzi] composed the commentary?

The Doctrine of the Mean begins by speaking of nature (xing), the Way (dao), and instruction (jiao), and subsequently speaks solely of the Way; why does it not touch upon nature and instruction? The twenty-first chapter speaks solely of nature and instruction; why does it not speak of the Way? Moreover, between the two mentions of nature and instruction, is there also a distinction? The meaning of the title of the treatise is not mentioned at the outset, which instead speaks in terms of nature, the Way, and instruction; why is this? Under the eleventh chapter it is stated [in Zhu Xi's commentary] that the main import of this treatise takes wisdom (zhi), humanity (ren), and courage (yong) as the gateway for entering the Way, yet at the twentieth chapter it says instead that sincerity (cheng) is in fact the pivot of this treatise; why is this? What is called in the first chapter "the essential substance of the whole treatise," and what is again described in the final chapter as "raising the essentials of the whole treatise and summarizing them concisely"—what…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
何所指歟學庸二書學者所當講其究
指歸以對
問大哉宣聖道該窮壤學貫古今固非後
人敢妄議也姑以其所可疑者言之禱
於尼山事若異也何適應其生夢奠兩
楹事若幻也何即知其没道宗堯舜仕
所行之法守文武何所施之相事初攝
將焉譚之政化甫成將焉誦之軍旅之
事未之學何以拒卻萊兵雖有其德而
===
無位何以正定禮樂道大德宏胡不貸
少正卯之誅過化存神胡不免宋桓魋
之侮絕食水飲困已極矣焉得樂在其
中絕粮七日病亦甚矣奚暇絃歌不衰
四十九表超於衆何肖似夫楊虎盛德
光耀於人何見毀於州仇賢於堯舜
何其高竊比老彭何其下尼溪之封齊
貧當矣奚不可於晏嬰國政與聞魯大
治矣奚輒沮於桓子席不暇暖似乎汲
punctuated:
何所指歟？《學》、《庸》二書，學者所當講，其究指歸以對。
問：大哉宣聖！道該窮壤，學貫古今，固非後人敢妄議也。姑以其所可疑者言之：禱於尼山，事若異也，何適應其生？夢奠兩楹，事若幻也，何即知其沒？道宗堯、舜，仕所行之？法守文、武，何所施之？相事初攝，將焉譚之？政化甫成，將焉誦之？軍旅之事未之學，何以拒卻萊兵？雖有其德而無位，何以正定禮樂？道大德宏，胡不貸少正卯之誅？過化存神，胡不免宋桓魋之侮？絕食水飲，困已極矣，焉得樂在其中？絕粮七日，病亦甚矣，奚暇絃歌不衰？四十九表超於衆，何肖似夫楊虎？盛德光耀於人，何見毀於州仇？「賢於堯、舜」，何其高？「竊比老、彭」，何其下？尼溪之封，齊貧當矣，奚不可於晏嬰？國政與聞，魯大治矣，奚輒沮於桓子？席不暇暖，似乎汲…
translation_en:
…to what do they refer? The two books of the Great Learning (Daxue) and the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) are what scholars ought to study and discuss; thoroughly investigate their ultimate aims and reply.

Question: Great indeed was the Exalted Sage [Confucius]! His Way encompasses heaven and earth, and his learning penetrates antiquity and the present; truly it is not something later generations dare to presumptuously criticize. Yet let us tentatively speak of those matters that may seem open to doubt: Praying at Mount Ni seems like an extraordinary affair—how did it happen to correspond to his birth? Dreaming of funerary offerings between the two pillars seems illusory—how did he thereby immediately know of his own approaching death? He took Yao and Shun as the patriarchs of his Way—where in office [or: how, reading 何 for 仕?] did he practice it? He upheld the laws of Kings Wen and Wu—where did he apply them? When he first acted as chief minister, why was he mocked for it? When his transformative governance had barely been achieved, why was he praised in song for it? He said he had not studied military affairs—how then did he repel the troops of Lai? Though one has the virtue, if one lacks the position [one dare not make rites and music]—how then did he rectify and fix the rites and music? Since his Way was great and his virtue vast, why did he not spare Shaozheng Mao from execution? Since wherever he passed he transformed people and wherever he abided he was like a spirit, why did he not escape the insult of Huan Tui of Song? Going without food and drinking only water [?], his distress was already extreme—how could he find joy in the midst of it? Deprived of provisions for seven days, his exhaustion was also severe—how did he have the leisure to play stringed instruments and sing without flagging? His forty-nine physical features surpassed the multitude—how could he resemble Yang Hu? His abundant virtue shone brilliantly upon others—why was he slandered by Zhou Qiu [i.e.,叔孫武叔 Shusun Wushu, personal name Zhouqiu]? "Far贤於 [worthier than] Yao and Shun"—how lofty a claim is that! "I venture to compare myself to our old Peng"—how lowly is that! Regarding the enfeoffment of Nixi, Qi's reward [? 貧當, likely garbled for 賞當] was fitting—why was it deemed unacceptable by Yan Ying? When he participated in hearing state affairs, Lu achieved great order—why was he so readily obstructed by Jihuanzi? His mat never had time to get warm, which makes him seem anxiously…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
汲汲求進行不脫晁似未從容中道觀於
鄉飲何以知王道之易易射於矍相何
以致觀者之僅存過庭訓子以詩禮富
餘事皆非所可學矣回若天之喪已豈
餘子皆非所可傳顏悟篤實俱爲美質
何所喩有損益之殊剛勇柔語俱爲失
中何所答有進退之異諸君子遊學聖
門沾沐餘化其於前言往行宜必耳熟
心醉而有得也幸無靳而不與之言
===
問守法者人臣之大節持正者君子之雅
操士有不知此而可以爲士乎稽之史
傳盜遠詔旨而不重犯蹕之罰寧怫人
言而不輕受賍之典之二子皆任廷尉
而其議論爲孰優選人詐冒則奏以據
法應流郎將坐誤則奏以犯不至死之
二子皆任大理而其功業爲孰盛守潁
川而郡中清靜刺冀州而境内肅然以
何爲而致是歟遷洛陽令外戚斂手爲
punctuated:
汲汲求進；行不脫冕，似未從容中道。觀於鄉飲，何以知王道之易易？射於矍相，何以致觀者之僅存？過庭訓子以詩禮，富餘事皆非所可學？哭回若天之喪己，豈餘子皆非所可傳？穎悟篤實俱爲美質，何所喩有損益之殊？剛勇柔語俱爲失中，何所答有進退之異？諸君子遊學聖門，沾沐餘化，其於前言往行，宜必耳熟心醉而有得也，幸無靳而不與之言。

問：守法者，人臣之大節；持正者，君子之雅操。士有不知此而可以爲士乎？稽之史傳，寧違詔旨而不重犯蹕之罰，寧怫人言而不輕受賍之典，之二子皆任廷尉，而其議論爲孰優？選人詐冒則奏以據法應流，郎將坐誤則奏以犯不至死，之二子皆任大理，而其功業爲孰盛？守潁川而郡中清靜，刺冀州而境内肅然，以何爲而致是歟？遷洛陽令，外戚斂手；爲…
translation_en:
…eagerly seeking advancement; setting out without taking off his ceremonial cap [冕, transcribed 晁] seems not to be calmly hitting the mean. Watching the District Symposium, how did he know that the Kingly Way was so easy? Shooting at Juexiang, how did he cause only a few spectators to remain? When his son passed through the courtyard, he instructed him in the Odes and the Rites—was it that [豈, transcribed 富] other matters were not worth learning? He wept [哭, transcribed 矣] for Yan Hui as if Heaven had destroyed him—could it be that none of the other disciples were worthy of receiving his transmission? Quick comprehension [穎悟, transcribed 顏悟] and earnest solidity are both fine qualities; why did his analogies for them differ in terms of diminishing and increasing? Unyielding boldness and pliant timidity [柔餒, transcribed 柔語] both fail to hit the mean; why did his answers to them differ in terms of advancing and holding back? You gentlemen have studied in the school of the Sage and have been steeped in his lingering transformative influence. Regarding these words and deeds of the past, your ears must be familiar with them, your hearts captivated by them, and you must have gained insight into them. Please do not be stingy and withhold your words.

Question: Upholding the law is the great integrity of a subject; maintaining rectitude is the noble principle of a gentleman. If a scholar does not know this, how can he be called a scholar? Examining the historical records: one would rather defy an imperial decree than stiffen the penalty for violating the imperial cortege, while another would rather go against others' words than lighten the statute on accepting bribes [?]. Both of these men served as Chamberlain for Law Enforcement (Tingwei), yet whose arguments were superior? When candidates for office committed fraud, one memorialized that according to the law they should be exiled; when a Commandant of Attendants (Langjiang) was implicated for an error, another memorialized that his offense did not warrant death. Both of these men served as Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review (Dali), yet whose achievements were more flourishing? Serving as Governor of Yingchuan and making the commandery calm and quiet, or serving as Regional Inspector of Jizhou and making the region reverently orderly—by what actions did they bring this about? Promoted to Magistrate of Luoyang, the consort clans restrained their hands; serving as…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
京兆尹豪右斂跡行何政而致然歟以
至執法一心不敢惜死南山可移判不
可搖守法若此其人可得而悉指歟若
夫鄭國有火不納裨竈之說漢儲欲廢
不憚廷爭之強是皆位列大夫而稱遺
愛者誰歟鳴玉殿省不爲佞人之事須
詔開門以防不逞之徒是皆位居侍中
而著死節者誰歟任郎中而受却坐之
賞候東門而膺却輦之褒何所見而致
===
歟忠臣不私私臣不忠臣職載筆君舉
必書何所激而言歟以至遇事謇謇無
所顧憚指切時事無所回避持正若此
其人可得而悉數歟諸士子尚友於千
載究之熟矣請筆以對毋徒誦諸載籍
可考
punctuated: 京兆尹，豪右斂跡，行何政而致然歟？以至「執法一心，不敢惜死」、「南山可移，判不可搖」，守法若此，其人可得而悉指歟？若夫鄭國有火，不納裨竈之說；漢儲欲廢，不憚廷爭之強，是皆位列大夫，而稱遺愛者誰歟？鳴玉殿省，不爲佞人之事；須詔開門，以防不逞之徒，是皆位居侍中，而著死節者誰歟？任郎中而受却坐之賞，候東門而膺却輦之褒，何所見而致歟？「忠臣不私，私臣不忠」、「臣職載筆，君舉必書」，何所激而言歟？以至遇事謇謇，無所顧憚；指切時事，無所回避，持正若此，其人可得而悉數歟？諸士子尚友於千載，究之熟矣。請筆以對，毋徒誦諸載籍可考。
translation_en:
…and as Metropolitan Governor (Jingzhao yin), the powerful and influential families restrained their tracks—by practicing what governance did they bring this about? And coming down to those who said, "In upholding the law with a single mind, I dare not begrudge my life," and "Mount Nan may be moved, but this legal judgment cannot be shaken"—in maintaining the law like this, can those men all be specifically identified?

As for the one who, when the state of Zheng suffered fires, did not accept the advice of Pi Zao; and the one who, when the Han heir apparent was about to be deposed, did not shrink from fierce remonstrance at court—both of these ranked among the Grand Masters (daifu), yet which of them was praised for leaving behind a legacy of love? One sounded his jade pendants in the palace departments and refused to perform the deeds of a flatterer; another waited for an imperial decree before opening the gates so as to guard against lawless miscreants—both of these held the position of Palace Attendant (shizhong), yet which of them became renowned for dying in loyalty? One served as an Attendant Gentleman (langzhong) and received a reward for making a consort draw back from her seat; another waited at the eastern gate and won praise for making the emperor decline his hand-drawn carriage—from what insight did they bring this about? "A loyal minister has no private partiality, and a partial minister is not loyal," and "Your servant's duty is to carry the recording brush; every action of the ruler must be written down"—by what were they stirred to speak thus? And coming down to those who, when encountering affairs, were outspoken and forthright without hesitation or fear, and who pointedly criticized current affairs without evasion—in upholding rectitude like this, can those men all be enumerated?

You gentlemen have befriended the ancients across a thousand years and have investigated these matters thoroughly. Please take up your brushes to reply, and do not merely say that they can be examined in the written records.
