通暢而且推本於志定淵乎其有者
論曰脩教化而百姓大和者有之矣謂天下治成之
本不在是也務節儉而海内富庶者有之矣謂天下
治成之本亦不在是也然欲致天下之治成道豈遠
乎哉術豈多乎哉惟在於君志之定而已善乎程子
punctuated:
也、教也，一皆銘之微，而衆善之集有如此夫。大抵爲銘之道，固不可遺其善，亦不可誣其惡。苟無美而稱之，是誣也；有善而弗知，不明也；知而弗傳，不仁也。爲人子孫，不明、不仁而且誣焉，則辱莫甚矣，尚何足與言銘哉？然則爲銘者，必仁、知、誠篤然後可。

論

天下治成

陳濂
同考試官教諭楊　批：〔議論深淳，筆力雄健，非老〕於作者不能也。
考試官教諭翁　批：〔論治成原於君志之定，深得程〕子本旨。
考試官教授邵　批：〔議論天下治成，氣象宏博，文理〕通暢，而且推本於志定，淵乎其有者。

論曰：脩教化而百姓大和者有之矣，謂天下治成之本不在是也；務節儉而海内富庶者有之矣，謂天下治成之本亦不在是也。然欲致天下之治成，道豈遠乎哉？術豈多乎哉？惟在於君志之定而已。善乎程子
translation_en:
…and instruction—all of these are the subtle meanings of an inscription, and the gathering of many virtues within it is just like this. In general, the way of composing an inscription must neither omit one's ancestors' good deeds nor falsely cover over their faults. If they lack merit and yet one praises them for it, this is falsehood; if they possess goodness and one fails to recognize it, this is lack of discernment; if one recognizes it yet fails to transmit it, this is lack of benevolence. For descendants to lack discernment and benevolence and furthermore to engage in falsehood—no disgrace could be greater than this! How could such a person be worthy of discussing inscriptions? Therefore, one who composes an inscription must be benevolent, discerning, sincere, and earnest before doing so.

Discourse

"The Accomplishment of Order in All-under-Heaven"

By Chen Lian 陳濂

Associate Examiner and Instructor Yang 楊 comments: The argument is profound and pure, and the brushwork is vigorous and strong; none but a seasoned writer could achieve this.

Examiner and Instructor Weng 翁 comments: In arguing that the accomplishment of order originates in the fixing of the ruler's will, he deeply grasps Master Cheng's (Cheng Yi 程頤) fundamental intent.

Examiner and Confucianyson Director of Studies Shao 邵 comments: In discussing the accomplishment of order in All-under-Heaven, the spirit is grand and expansive, the literary structure and reasoning flow smoothly, and moreover it traces the root back to the fixing of the will—profound indeed is what he possesses!

The discourse states: There have been cases where moral transformation was cultivated and the hundred surnames lived in great harmony, yet it is said that the root of accomplishing order in All-under-Heaven does not lie in this. There have been cases where frugality was practiced and everyone within the seas became wealthy and populous, yet it is said that the root of accomplishing order in All-under-Heaven does not lie in this either. If one wishes to bring about the accomplishment of order in All-under-Heaven, how could the Way be far off? How could its methods be numerous? It lies solely in the fixing of the ruler's will, and nothing more. Admirable indeed is Master Cheng…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
論君道而有是言也何則天下之民蜂房井絡若是
其多也彙聚胣分若是其衆也誠欲以智力治之則
雖十室之邑人人提耳而教且不及況天下之大哉
是必有其要焉蓋天下必一人爲主人君以一心爲
主莫大於天下尤莫大於君之一心君心之志其可
不知所定乎是故義理不先定則多聽而易惑志意
不先定則守善而或移若典謨載籍聖人之訓所寓
也必遂稽博考精求圖治之大道而不爲後世駁雜
之政所牽帶道德齊禮先王之治可法也必以敷求祇
===
適悉遵經世之大法而不爲流俗因循之論所遷改
由是而明善惡之歸必以禮制心以義制事而得中
正之□□□□□□□□之分必任賢勿貳去邪勿疑
而得用舍之□□□□於信道如此非君志之定而何
然君志既定則揆事宰物之本立處己用人之道明
不作無益而害彼有益不狃近利而昧於遠猷斷斷
焉以天下之大聖行天下之大事殆見發號施令衆
志咸服雖疑旒負扆深居九重之上而仁化自被於
八荒□□衣拱手端處五位之尊而風教自行於四
punctuated: 論君道而有是言也。何則？天下之民，蜂房井絡若是其多也，彙聚胣分若是其衆也。誠欲以智力治之，則雖十室之邑，人人提耳而教且不及，況天下之大哉！是必有其要焉。蓋天下必一人爲主，人君以一心爲主。莫大於天下，尤莫大於君之一心，君心之志其可不知所定乎？是故義理不先定，則多聽而易惑；志意不先定，則守善而或移。若典謨載籍，聖人之訓所寓也，必遂稽博考，精求圖治之大道，而不爲後世駁雜之政所牽帶；道德齊禮，先王之治可法也，必以敷求祇適，悉遵經世之大法，而不爲流俗因循之論所遷改。由是而明善惡之歸，必以禮制心，以義制事，而得中正之□□□□□□□□之分，必任賢勿貳，去邪勿疑，而得用舍之□□□□於信道如此，非君志之定而何？然君志既定，則揆事宰物之本立，處己用人之道明。不作無益而害彼有益，不狃近利而昧於遠猷，斷斷焉以天下之大聖，行天下之大事。殆見發號施令，衆志咸服。雖疑旒負扆，深居九重之上，而仁化自被於八荒；□□衣拱手，端處五位之尊，而風教自行於四
translation_en:
…in discussing the Way of the Ruler, made this statement! Why is this so? The people of the realm, clustered like honeycombs and interlaced like a grid of wells, are so numerous; gathered into classes and divided into groups [? 胣分, for 類分], they are so multitude. If one truly wished to govern them through personal cleverness and strength, then even in a hamlet of ten households one could not reach everyone by pulling their ears to instruct them in person—how much less so across the vastness of the realm! In this, there must be an essential pivot. Now, the realm necessarily has the One Man as its master, and the ruler takes his own single mind as master. Nothing is greater than the realm, yet nothing is greater still than the single mind of the ruler; how could the resolve of the ruler's mind not know wherein it is settled?

Therefore, if moral principles are not settled beforehand, then in listening to many views one is easily confused; if one's resolve and intent are not settled beforehand, then in holding to the good one may sometimes waver. As for the canons, counsels, and written records, wherein the teachings of the sages reside: one must thoroughly investigate and broadly examine them [? 遂稽, for 邃稽],精求 [seeking with precision] the Great Way of planning for governance, without being dragged along by the impure and mixed policies of later ages. Guiding with virtue and regulating with ritual, the governance of the former kings is worthy of emulation: one must extensively seek out and reverently follow it, wholly complying with the great laws for ordering the world, without being shifted or altered by the routine and compromising arguments of vulgar custom.

From this, in clarifying the ultimate distinction between good and evil, he must regulate his mind with ritual and regulate affairs with righteousness, thereby attaining the […8 illegible characters, likely: standard of central correctness; and in clarifying the distinction between the worthy and the姦/evil…], he must employ the worthy without duplicity and cast out the wicked without doubt, thereby attaining the […4 illegible characters, likely: appropriateness of employment and dismissal;笃/devoted…] to believing in the Way like this—if this is not the settling of the ruler's resolve, what is it?

Once the ruler's resolve is settled, the foundation for measuring affairs and governing things is established, and the Way of conducting oneself and employing others becomes clear. He does not contrive what is unprofitable to the detriment of what is profitable; he does not grow accustomed to immediate advantage while remaining blind to far-reaching plans. Resolutely and wholeheartedly, as the great sage of the realm, he carries out the great affairs of the realm. One will soon see that when he issues commands and promulgates orders, the minds of the multitude all submit. Even though he stands solemn with pendant-strings hanging down and his back to theembroidered screen, dwelling deep above the ninefold gates of the palace, his benevolent transformation naturally extends over the eight荒 [eight wildernesses]; […2 illegible characters, likely: 雖垂 "even though he lets hang"] his robes and folds his hands, sitting upright in the exalted fifth [imperial] position, moral instruction naturally prevails throughout the four…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
表非假刑驅勢迫而不尊之義導之道而會其有極以歸
待教諭戶曉離之是訓是行而歸其有極焉輿圖之
大人雖有彼此也咸熙熙然於春風和氣之中幅員
之廣地雖有遠近也咸懽然於景星慶雲之下日
出而作日入而息順乎帝則之自然耕田而食鑿井
而飲不知帝力之何有於是和氣昭融休徵畢達三
光全而寒暑平山嶽奠而河海清草木光華鳥獸咸
若諸福之物可致之祥莫不畢至矣治化之隆爲何
如哉論至於是則知人君之志雖微而天下之所繫
===
甚大志定而后治成正所謂正心以正朝廷正百官
萬民遠近莫不一於正所守者至約而可以御繁所
發者至寡而可以服衆者或忽其志之近而務他道
之遠遺其志之易而圖他道之難雖欲治成其可得
乎稽之於古若克明峻德而萬邦協和帝德罔愆而
四方風動堯舜之志定而治成也允執厥中而文命
四敷懋敬厥德而萬邦惟懷禹湯之志定而治成也
緝熙敬止而脩和有夏建其有極而萬姓悅服非文
武之心定而治成乎堯舜遠矣禹湯文武往矣洪惟我
punctuated: 表。非假刑驅勢迫而不尊之義導之道，而會其有極以歸；待教諭戶曉，離之是訓是行，而歸其有極焉。輿圖之大，人雖有彼此也，咸熙熙然於春風和氣之中；幅員之廣，地雖有遠近也，咸懽然於景星慶雲之下。日出而作，日入而息，順乎帝則之自然；耕田而食，鑿井而飲，不知帝力之何有。於是和氣昭融，休徵畢達，三光全而寒暑平，山嶽奠而河海清，草木光華，鳥獸咸若，諸福之物，可致之祥，莫不畢至矣。治化之隆，爲何如哉！論至於是，則知人君之志雖微，而天下之所繫甚大。志定而后治成，正所謂正心以正朝廷、正百官、萬民，遠近莫不一於正。所守者至約而可以御繁，所發者至寡而可以服衆。苟或忽其志之近而務他道之遠，遺其志之易而圖他道之難，雖欲治成，其可得乎？稽之於古，若克明峻德而萬邦協和，帝德罔愆而四方風動，堯、舜之志定而治成也；允執厥中而文命四敷，懋敬厥德而萬邦惟懷，禹、湯之志定而治成也；緝熙敬止而脩和有夏，建其有極而萬姓悅服，非文、武之心定而治成乎？堯、舜遠矣，禹、湯、文、武往矣，洪惟我
translation_en:
… Quarters. Without relying on the compulsion of punishments or the coercion of power [?], nor waiting to instruct every household before they follow these teachings and return to the Supreme Standard [?], they converge upon the Supreme Standard and return to it. Throughout the vastness of the empire, though people differ from one another, all are joyful and harmonious within the vernal breeze and genial air; across the breadth of the realm, though lands are near or far, all rejoice beneath auspicious stars and propitious clouds. Working at sunrise and resting at sunset, they naturally follow the ruler's pattern; plowing the fields for food and digging wells for drink, they do not know what the ruler's power has to do with them. Thus, harmonious vital energy shines forth and blends, and auspicious signs all arrive: the three luminaries are complete and cold and heat are balanced, the mountains are settled and the rivers and seas run clear, plants and trees flourish brilliantly, birds and beasts are all compliant, and every blessed thing and attainable auspice arrives in full. How grand is the flourishing of such governance and transformation!

Reasoning up to this point, one knows that although the ruler's will is subtle, what depends upon it throughout the world is immense. Once the will is fixed, good governance is achieved. This is precisely what is meant by rectifying the mind in order to rectify the court, rectify the hundred officials, and rectify the myriad people, so that near and far alike are united in rectitude. What is maintained is most concise, yet it can control the complex; what is put forth is most slight, yet it can win the submission of the multitude. Should one neglect the nearness of one's will and pursue the remoteness of other ways, or abandon the ease of one's will and scheme after the difficulty of other ways, even if one wished for governance to be achieved, how could it be attained? Examining antiquity: being able to make illustrious his lofty virtue so that the myriad states were brought into harmony, and the sovereign's virtue being without fault so that the four quarters moved as if before the wind—this was the will of Yao and Shun being fixed and governance achieved; sincerely holding fast the Mean so that civilizing ordinances spread in the four directions, and earnestly revering his virtue so that the myriad states cherished him—this was the will of Yu and Tang being fixed and governance achieved; continuing in bright reverence so as to cultivate and harmonize the Xia realm, and establishing his Supreme Standard so that the myriad surnames gladly submitted—was this not the mind of King Wen and King Wu being fixed and governance achieved? Yao and Shun are distant now, and Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu have passed away; yet contemplating our great …

Our successive sacred emperors have inherited the throne one after another, their minds in harmony with the minds of the ancient sage-emperors and kings, and their Way attaining to the Way of those emperors and kings. punctuated: 剛健中正，龍行虎步，御神器於九重；魚躍鳶飛，運化機於六合。隆興學親賢之典，嚴脩身體道之誠。鑾輿始幸於橋門，衣冠增重；鳳輦再臨於璧水，俎豆生輝。詔進儒臣，祭登講席。對揚休命，陳《商書》師古之至言；如契宸衷，感傳說格心之大訓。睠惟孟品之命服，猥及一介之凡庸。寵幸自天，措躬無地。臣材猶樗櫟，學本荒蕪。摘句尋章，講論無裨於天聽；微辭奥義，指歸偶合於聖心。昔儆緇衆，恩同山嶽；〈下增〉文纊，報之涓埃。感激昌勝，揄揚莫既。伏願聖學日同羅而月同輝，皇圖天與長而地與久。臣無任瞻
translation_en:
… firm, vigorous, balanced, and upright. Striding like a dragon and pacing like a tiger, You wield the sacred regalia within the ninefold palace; while fish leap and hawks soar, You set in motion the mechanisms of transformation throughout the six directions of the universe. You exalt the rites of promoting learning and drawing close to the worthy, and strictly maintain the sincerity of cultivating the person and embodying the Way. When the Imperial Carriage first graced the bridged gates of the National University, the capped and robed scholars gained in dignity; when the Phoenix Palanquin came a second time to the Jade-ring Waters, the sacrificial vessels shone with splendor. By imperial edict You summoned the Confucian officials to ascend the lecture mat in order [?]. Responding to and extolling Your glorious mandate, I set forth the supreme words on taking antiquity as master from the Book of Shang; as though matching Your Imperial heart, You were moved by Fu Yue's great instruction on rectifying the mind.

Yet Your gracious regard, bestowing the ceremonial robes of the highest rank [?], has undeservedly reached a mere mediocrity such as myself. Favor and fortune descend from Heaven, leaving me no place to stand in my embarrassment. Your servant's talent is like that of the useless ailanthus and scrub oak, and my learning is fundamentally barren. Plucking out phrases and hunting for chapters, my lectures and discussions were of no benefit to Your Heavenly hearing; yet in subtle words and profound meanings, their general purport chanced to accord with the Sage's mind. Previously, though worn as a black robe [?], Your grace was as weighty as mountains and peaks; now, bestowed with [?] patterned silk and floss, I have not a drop of water or a speck of dust with which to repay You. Overwhelmed with gratitude beyond measure, I cannot exhaust my praise.

I humbly pray that Your Sage learning may shine together with the sun [?] and glow together with the moon, and that the Imperial rule may endure as long as Heaven and last as long as Earth. Your servant is utterly overwhelmed with gazing up…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
不群擢居首選孰敢不謹
宸翰煒煌昭回雲漢而爲萬世之典
神聖同一心
皇猷赫奕掀揭宇宙而立教之功先後同一揆欽惟
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏慮習俗之未醇人心之未淑萬
機之暇條成
大誥三編
太宗文皇帝輯寶邦家欲天下之趨善臣民之行孝
而著爲善陰隲孝順事實二書逮夫
===
宣宗章皇帝繼體守成益弘景運期臣民之克盡人
道也乃有五倫一書之頒愚嘗莊誦而知
三聖之心見於書猶化工之妙著於物
三聖之書行於世猶日月之明麗乎天迪斯民於吉
康納天下於皇極其意爲何如哉且夫建極莫
要於五倫而五倫各有名義蓋君者群也下所
歸心也臣者纏堅也志自堅固也法度教子者
謂之父孳孳無已者謂之子况父法者非兄乎
心順行篤者非弟乎至於以道扶接者謂之夫
punctuated:
不群，擢居首選，孰敢不謹？

宸翰煒煌，昭回雲漢，而爲萬世之典；神聖同一心，皇猷赫奕，掀揭宇宙，而立教之功，先後同一揆。欽惟太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，慮習俗之未醇、人心之未淑，萬機之暇，條成《大誥》三編；太宗文皇帝輯寶邦家，欲天下之趨善、臣民之行孝，而著《爲善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書；逮夫宣宗章皇帝繼體守成，益弘景運，期臣民之克盡人道也，乃有《五倫》一書之頒。愚嘗莊誦，而知三聖之心見於書，猶化工之妙著於物；三聖之書行於世，猶日月之明麗乎天。迪斯民於吉康，納天下於皇極，其意爲何如哉！且夫建極莫要於五倫，而五倫各有名義：蓋君者，群也，下所歸心也；臣者，纏堅也，志自堅固也；法度教子者謂之父，孳孳無已者謂之子；况父法者非兄乎？心順行篤者非弟乎？至於以道扶接者謂之夫，
translation_en:
…stands out above the crowd; we elevate it to first place, and who would dare not be reverent?]

Imperial brush-strokes shine resplendently, revolving brightly like the Milky Way in heaven, to become a canon for ten thousand generations; the sacred sages share a single mind, their imperial plans blaze gloriously, lifting up and illuminating the universe, and in the merit of establishing moral instruction, earlier and later rulers follow the exact same measure. Reverently I reflect that Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao (Taizu) founded the realm of China, and, concerned that customs were not yet pure and human minds not yet virtuous, in the leisure from his myriad affairs of state compiled in articles the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao); Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen (Taizong) brought harmony and cherished the state [?], and wishing the world to incline toward goodness and his subjects and people to practice filial piety, composed the two books Retribution for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Examples of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi); coming down to the time when Ancestor of Proclamation Emperor Zhang (Xuanzong) succeeded to the throne and preserved the achievements of his predecessors, further expanding the glorious destiny of the dynasty, in the hope that his subjects and people would be able to fulfill the Way of humanity to the utmost, there was the promulgation of the book On the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu). In my simplicity I have solemnly recited them, and thus I know that the minds of the Three Sages made manifest in their books are like the marvels of creative nature revealed in all things, and the books of the Three Sages circulating in the world are like the brightness of the sun and moon suspended in the heavens. Guiding these people toward auspicious peace and gathering the world into the Supreme Standard—how profound was their intention! Moreover, in establishing the Supreme Standard, nothing is more essential than the five human relationships, and each of the five relationships has its own name and meaning: "ruler" (jun) means "to group together" (qun), the one to whom those below turn their hearts; "minister" (chen) means "bound and firm" (chanjian), one whose resolve is inherently steadfast; he who instructs his children with rules and measures is called "father" (fu), and he who is tirelessly diligent without cease is called "son" (zi); is not he who exemplifies [?] the father's model the "elder brother" (xiong)? Is not he whose heart is compliant and conduct sincere the "younger brother" (di)? As for him who supports and receives according to the Way, he is called "husband" (fu)…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以禮屈服者謂之婦而朋者黨也友者有也與
不各有名義存焉若朱子謂其有天屬人合若
蓋父子兄弟二者天屬也君臣夫婦朋友三者
人合也然又謂天屬有賴於人合若蓋君臣天
屬所賴以全者也夫婦天屬所由以續者也朋
友天屬所賴以正者也書曰之所載君臣之倫若
宋儒胡寅所謂人君躬行於上卿大夫表式於
下者其與大誥君臣同心志同一氣之旨無或
殊父子之倫若唐房玄齡以古今家誡書爲屏
===
風者其與陰隲禹鈞行善義教五子之事無或
異田宅財物盡與其弟若此卜式讓產兄弟之倫
也豈不同於事實之郭全孝友乎狐頭謝罪富
不易妻者此尉遲敬德義夫婦之倫也豈不同
於陰隲之叔通娶啞乎若夫巢谷與韓存寶之
相友善存寶以銀鑄之遺其妻子谷即變姓名
懷之步往授其子則又與陰隲三郎行義同一
朋友之盡其道焉由是觀之則五倫所言衆之
三誥之旨若符節之相合五倫所載較之二書
punctuated: 以禮屈服者謂之婦，而朋者黨也，友者有也，與不各有名義存焉？若朱子謂其有天屬、人合，若蓋父子、兄弟二者，天屬也；君臣、夫婦、朋友三者，人合也。然又謂天屬有賴於人合，若蓋君臣，天屬所賴以全者也；夫婦，天屬所由以續者也；朋友，天屬所賴以正者也。書曰之所載君臣之倫，若宋儒胡寅所謂「人君躬行於上，卿大夫表式於下」者，其與《大誥》君臣同心、志同一氣之旨，無或殊。父子之倫，若唐房玄齡以古今家誡書爲屏風者，其與《陰隲》禹鈞行善、義教五子之事，無或異。田宅財物盡與其弟，若此卜式讓產，兄弟之倫也，豈不同於《事實》之郭全孝友乎？狐頭謝罪，富不易妻者，此尉遲敬德義，夫婦之倫也，豈不同於《陰隲》之叔通娶啞乎？若夫巢谷與韓存寶之相友善，存寶以銀鑄之，遺其妻子，谷即變姓名，懷之步往授其子，則又與《陰隲》三郎行義，同一朋友之盡其道焉。由是觀之，則《五倫》所言，衆之三《誥》之旨，若符節之相合；《五倫》所載，較之二書…
translation_en: …and one who submits in accordance with propriety is called a wife; whereas peng (associate) means forming a group, and you (friend) means holding in mutual possession—do not all of these [?] have their respective names and principles? As for Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) saying that among them some are bound by Heaven and some are joined by man: [?] father and son, and elder and younger brothers, are the two bound by Heaven; ruler and minister, husband and wife, and friends are the three joined by man. Yet he also said that those bound by Heaven depend upon those joined by man: [?] ruler and minister are what those bound by Heaven rely upon to be preserved whole; husband and wife are that through which those bound by Heaven are continued; and friends are what those bound by Heaven rely upon to be rectified. Regarding what is recorded in the book [?], as for the relationship of ruler and minister, such as the Song scholar Hu Yin 胡寅 saying that "the ruler personally practices it above, and the ministers and grandees serve as models below," this does not differ in the least from the purport of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) that ruler and minister share a single heart and their wills are united as one vital breath. As for the relationship of father and son, such as Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 of the Tang inscribing family admonitions past and present upon folding screens, this does not differ in the least from the matter in the Book of Secret Merits (Yinzhi shu) of Dou Yujun 竇禹鈞 performing good deeds and righteously instructing his five sons. Giving all fields, houses, and property to one's younger brother, such as Bu Shi 卜式 yielding his estate—this is the relationship of elder and younger brothers; how is it not the same as Guo Quan's 郭全 filial piety and fraternal love in the Deeds of Filial Piety and Teasurable Compassion (Xiaoci shishi)? Apologizing for an offense with a fox's head [?], and not changing one's wife when becoming rich—this is Yuchi Jingde's 尉遲敬德 righteousness in the relationship of husband and wife; how is it not the same as Shutong 叔通 marrying a mute woman in the Book of Secret Merits? And as for Chao Gu 巢谷 and Han Cunbao 韓存寶 being close friends, when Cunbao entrusted him with cast silver [?] to leave to his wife and children, Gu immediately changed his surname and given name, concealed the silver in his bosom, and traveled on foot to hand it over to Cunbao's son; this again is identical with Third Son (Sanlang 三郎) practicing righteousness in the Book of Secret Merits, both fulfilling the Way of friends. Viewed from this perspective, what is spoken of in the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), compared [?] with the purport of the three Pronouncements (Gao), matches like the halves of a tally; and what is recorded in the Book of the Five Human Relationships, compared with the two books…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之言如軌轍之相同其垂世立教之心尚何有
先後之間哉愚也樂育庠序服膺
聖訓蓋亦有年今承明問敢述以為對
第二問
彭教
同考試官教諭諸　批〔說三代風俗宛然如在目中〕
〔且文有起伏有斷制非老於筆不手皆不能〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔三代以來風俗至我〕
〔朝充盛此策善於歸美〕
===
天地之氣化有淳漓而世道之升降繫焉人君
之好尚有正否而風俗之美惡關焉粵稽諸
往古大司徒以五禮六樂陶淑人心而在上無
異教掌道王之德意志慮而在上無異政合萬
民以通其財貨同其度量而在下無異尚除其
怨惡同其好惡而在下無異情此三代以前風
俗之美且厚者由此道也迨夫王迹既熄贏秦
崛起惟貴變詐而任峻刻澆薄頑鄙之風作德
色誶語之俗興而風俗蠲於薄矣幸而炎漢肇
punctuated:
之言，如軌轍之相同。其垂世立教之心，尚何有先後之間哉？愚也樂育庠序，服膺聖訓，蓋亦有年；今承明問，敢述以為對。

第二問
彭教
同考試官教諭諸　批〔說三代風俗，宛然如在目中；〕〔且文有起伏，有斷制，非老於筆不手皆不能。〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔三代以來風俗，至我〕〔朝充盛，此策善於歸美。〕

天地之氣化有淳漓，而世道之升降繫焉；人君之好尚有正否，而風俗之美惡關焉。粵稽諸往古，大司徒以五禮、六樂陶淑人心，而在上無異教；掌道王之德意志慮，而在上無異政；合萬民以通其財貨、同其度量，而在下無異尚；除其怨惡、同其好惡，而在下無異情。此三代以前，風俗之美且厚者，由此道也。迨夫王迹既熄，贏秦崛起，惟貴變詐而任峻刻，澆薄頑鄙之風作，德色誶語之俗興，而風俗蠲於薄矣。幸而炎漢肇
translation_en:
… words of [those two books], they are as identical as carriage tracks following the same ruts. In their intention to hand down teachings for future generations, how could there be any difference between earlier and later times? Simple as I am, I have rejoiced in being nurtured in the local school and have taken the sage instructions to heart for some years now; today, having received your enlightened question, I venture to set this forth as my reply.

Second Question
Peng Jiao 彭教
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhu 諸, comments: "He discusses the customs of the Three Dynasties as vividly as if they were right before our eyes; moreover, the essay has rise and fall and decisive judgment—none but a seasoned hand at the brush [?] could achieve this."
Examiner, Instructor Weng 翁, comments: "Customs since the Three Dynasties have reached their fullest flourishing in our dynasty; this policy essay excels at attributing praise to the throne."

Thevital transformations of Heaven and Earth may be pure or thin, and the rise and decline of the Way of the world are bound up with them; the preferences of the ruler may be upright or not, and the beauty or ugliness of customs hinges upon them. Examining remote antiquity, the Minister of Education (da situ 大司徒) cultivated and refined people's minds with the Five Rites and Six Musics, so that above there were no divergent teachings; officials in charge communicated the king's virtuous intentions and thoughts, so that above there was no divergent governance; they united the myriad people so as to circulate their goods and standardize their measures, so that below there were no divergent preferences; and they removed their resentments and harmonized their likes and dislikes, so that below there were no divergent sentiments. That customs prior to and during the Three Dynasties were both admirable and generous was due to this Way. When the traces of the true kings had died out and the Ying 贏 clan of Qin 秦 rose abruptly, they valued only deceit and employed harshness and severity; a climate of superficiality, obstinacy, and vulgarity arose, habits of putting on airs of superiority over small favors and exchanging abusive words flourished, and customs degenerated [?] into thinness. Fortunately, when the fiery Han 漢 first…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
典痛革秦弊高惠寬仁文景恭儉化黎民於淳
厚致刑罰之幾措豈不變而歸於厚乎武帝繼
統解弦更張好大喜功之念萌窮兵黷武之事
舉而風俗趨於虛矣幸而孝宣中興綜核名實
吏稱其職民安其業豈不變而歸於實乎魏晉
以來稍尚通達賤守節而貴清虛蔑禮法而尚
黃老風俗又趨於浮矣向非李唐啓祚太宗力
行仁義身致太平變其浮而歸於醇則其流弊
何所不至哉柰何一盛一衰有隆有替五季之
魚爛絲紛君子所不忍言也宋太祖應期受禪
約己裕民深仁厚澤涵養數世一變而正夷俗
豈漢唐二世之可儗哉胡元之腥羶中夏君子
===
所不屑論也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝應天撫運漸仁摩義汎掃胡夷之弊習
誕回華夏之彝風自是
列聖相承克篤前烈崇詩書禮樂之教恢仁義道德
之化凡在涵煦者靡不孚顒若也是以萬方一
統六合同春人人有士君子之行比屋有可封之
punctuated: 典，痛革秦弊。高、惠寬仁，文、景恭儉，化黎民於淳厚，致刑罰之幾措，豈不變而歸於厚乎？武帝繼統，解弦更張，好大喜功之念萌，窮兵黷武之事舉，而風俗趨於虛矣。幸而孝宣中興，綜核名實，吏稱其職，民安其業，豈不變而歸於實乎？魏、晉以來，稍尚通達，賤守節而貴清虛，蔑禮法而尚黃、老，風俗又趨於浮矣。向非李唐啓祚，太宗力行仁義，身致太平，變其浮而歸於醇，則其流弊何所不至哉？柰何一盛一衰，有隆有替，五季之魚爛絲紛，君子所不忍言也。宋太祖應期受禪，約己裕民，深仁厚澤，涵養數世，一變而正夷俗，豈漢、唐二世之可儗哉？胡元之腥羶中夏，君子所不屑論也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝應天撫運，漸仁摩義，汎掃胡夷之弊習，誕回華夏之彝風。自是列聖相承，克篤前烈，崇詩書禮樂之教，恢仁義道德之化，凡在涵煦者，靡不孚顒若也。是以萬方一統，六合同春，人人有士君子之行，比屋有可封之
translation_en: … arose [reading 典 as 興] and thoroughly reformed the abuses of Qin. Emperors Gaozu and Huidi were lenient and benevolent, while Emperors Wendi and Jingdi were respectful and frugal; they transformed the common people toward simplicity and generosity, bringing punishments almost to the point of disuse—was this not a change that returned customs to generosity? When Emperor Wu succeeded to the throne, he unstrung the bow to restring it anew; thoughts of loving grandeur and delighting in exploits sprouted, enterprises of exhausting the military and engaging in wanton warfare were undertaken, and customs tended toward emptiness. Fortunately, Emperor Xiaoxuan achieved a restoration, verifying that names matched realities; officials were equal to their offices and the people were content in their occupations—was this not a change that returned customs to substance? From the Wei and Jin dynasties onward, people gradually esteemed uninhibitedness, despising the maintenance of integrity while valuing pure emptiness, and scorning ritual and law while revering Huang-Lao; thus customs once again tended toward superficiality. Had not the Li-family Tang dynasty founded its imperial line, with Emperor Taizong vigorously practicing benevolence and righteousness, personally bringing about great peace, and transforming that superficiality to return to purity, to what lengths would those flowing abuses not have reached? Yet how could it be helped that flourishing and decline alternated, and rise was followed by fall? In the Five Dynasties, the state rotted from within like a fish and became tangled like silk threads—something a gentleman cannot bear to speak of. When Emperor Taizu of the Song responded to the appointed time and received the abdication, he restrained himself to enrich the people; his deep benevolence and generous grace nurtured the realm for several generations, and at a stroke he rectified the barbarian customs—how could the two eras of Han and Tang even be compared to this? As for the barbarian Yuan befouling the central lands of Xia with their rank odor, that is something a gentleman disdains to discuss. I reflect with awe upon how our Taizu, Emperor Gao, responded to Heaven and grasped the Mandate, imbuing the people with benevolence and polishing them with righteousness, sweeping away the corrupt habits of the northern barbarians and grandly restoring the constant customs of China. Since then, the successive sage emperors have inherited the throne one after another, ably consolidating the achievements of their predecessors, exalting the teachings of the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music, and expanding the transformative influence of benevolence, righteousness, morality, and virtue, so that among all who are nurtured and warmed by them, there is none who does not respond with sincere reverence. Therefore, the myriad regions are unified as one, the six directions share in the same spring, everyone possesses the conduct of a scholar-gentleman, and side-by-side households have [customs] worthy of enfeoffment…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
俗其美且厚誠所謂周恩於世同符而媺漢魏唐宋
於下風矣天下幸甚萬世幸甚
第三問
彭教
同考試官教諭諸　批〔剖析二書之旨節節詳明其　必用功於本領而有得者〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔答此問勢如破竹迎刃而解非工　於本領之學者不能卻杯一枝非子其誰〕
二書所著之言各有不同二書立言之旨各有
===
攸在夫立言不同者由其微旨之有在也學者
徒泥其言之異而不究其指歸之當又何以得
聖賢之心法哉請因明問而條陳之昔曾子述
孔子之言而傳大學子思述所傳之意而作中
庸實聖賢傳心之閫奧也大學經文一章首言
三綱領而中以止至善不及明德新民者蓋以
至善乃明德新民之準的即二者各造其極之
謂也八條目詳夫明德新民而不及止至善者
蓋以物格知至則知止之事意誠以下則皆得
punctuated:
俗，其美且厚，誠所謂周恩於世同符，而媺漢、魏、唐、宋於下風矣。天下幸甚！萬世幸甚！

第三問
彭教
同考試官教諭諸　批：〔剖析二書之旨，節節詳明，其必用功於本領而有得者。〕
考試官教諭翁　批：〔答此問勢如破竹，迎刃而解，非工於本領之學者不能。卻杯一枝，非子其誰？〕

二書所著之言各有不同，二書立言之旨各有攸在。夫立言不同者，由其微旨之有在也。學者徒泥其言之異，而不究其指歸之當，又何以得聖賢之心法哉？請因明問而條陳之。昔曾子述孔子之言而傳《大學》，子思述所傳之意而作《中庸》，實聖賢傳心之閫奧也。《大學》經文一章，首言三綱領，而中以止至善，不及明德、新民者，蓋以至善乃明德、新民之準的，即二者各造其極之謂也。八條目詳夫明德、新民，而不及止至善者，蓋以物格、知至，則知止之事；意誠以下，則皆得
translation_en:
…customs; in their beauty and richness, they truly tally with how the Zhou dynasty extended its grace to the world, while leaving Han, Wei, Tang, and Song far behind in their wake. Most fortunate for All under Heaven! Most fortunate for ten thousand generations!

Third Question
Peng Jiao 彭教
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhu 諸, comments: [He analyzes the purport of the two books with detailed clarity at every point; he must be one who has applied his effort to the fundamental principles and gained true insight.]
Examiner, Instructor Weng 翁, comments: [He answers this question with irresistible force, like splitting bamboo that parts at the touch of the blade; none but a scholar skilled in fundamental principles could do this. As for a single branch of the cassia of郤詵 Xi Shen [? 卻杯], if not you, then who?]

The words set forth in the two books each have their differences, and the purport in establishing the words of the two books each has where it resides. Now, the reason their established words differ is that each has its own subtle purport. If scholars merely cling to the differences in their wording without investigating the fitness of their ultimate import, how then can they attain the transmission of the mind-and-heart (xinfa) of the sages and worthies? Allow me to set this forth item by item in response to the illustrious question. In antiquity, Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) recounted the words of Confucius and transmitted the Great Learning (Daxue 大學), while Zisi 子思 recounted the meaning of what had been transmitted to him and composed the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong 中庸); these are truly the innermost mysteries of the sages' and worthies' transmission of the mind-and-heart. The single chapter of the Classic text of the Great Learning first states the Three Guiding Principles (san gangling); yet in the middle it speaks of resting in the highest good without mentioning manifesting luminous virtue or renewing the people, because the highest good is the standard and target for manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people—that is, it means bringing each of the two to its ultimate perfection. The Eight Particular Steps (ba tiaomu) detail manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people without mentioning resting in the highest good, because the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge are the affair of knowing where to rest, while making the intentions sincere and the steps that follow are all…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
所止之序也其傳十章釋綱領而外有本末之
者豈非釋經文物有本末之義乎釋條目皆以
兩章相承獨誠意自爲一章者豈非以誠意爲
自脩之首乎格物致知一章亡矣朱子取程子
之意補之而不效曾子作傳之體者自謂竊嘗
效而爲之竟不能成蓋文以時異而理則一也
若夫中庸一書首言性道教繼獨言道而不及
性教者蓋以性爲道之原教爲道之用也二十
一章獨言性教而不及道者蓋以性者天之道
===
教者人之道也然先言天命之性脩道之教則
以性教之名義言之後言誠明之性明誠之教
則以聖賢之分言之二者分別可見矣首言天
命之性即未發之中率性之道即已發之中而
教者又所以裁其過與不及而歸於中名篇之
義在是矣十一章既曰此篇大旨以知仁勇爲
入道之門至二十章又曰誠者實此篇之樞紐
蓋知以知此理仁以體此理勇以强此理而誠
又所以實此知仁勇也詳言之雖有知仁勇之
punctuated: 所止之序也。其傳十章，釋綱領而外有本末之者，豈非釋經文「物有本末」之義乎？釋條目皆以兩章相承，獨誠意自爲一章者，豈非以誠意爲自脩之首乎？格物致知一章亡矣，朱子取程子之意補之，而不效曾子作傳之體者，自謂竊嘗效而爲之，竟不能成，蓋文以時異而理則一也。若夫《中庸》一書，首言性、道、教，繼獨言道而不及性、教者，蓋以性爲道之原，教爲道之用也。二十一章獨言性、教而不及道者，蓋以性者天之道，教者人之道也。然先言天命之性、脩道之教，則以性、教之名義言之；後言誠明之性、明誠之教，則以聖賢之分言之，二者分別可見矣。首言天命之性，即未發之中；率性之道，即已發之中；而教者，又所以裁其過與不及而歸於中，名篇之義在是矣。十一章既曰此篇大旨以知、仁、勇爲入道之門，至二十章又曰誠者實此篇之樞紐，蓋知以知此理，仁以體此理，勇以强此理，而誠又所以實此知、仁、勇也。詳言之，雖有知、仁、勇之
translation_en:
…the sequence of attaining the point where one abides. In its ten chapters of commentary, why is there, besides the explanations of the three guiding principles, also a chapter on the root and branches? Is it not to explain the meaning of the classical text's phrase "things have their root and their branches"? In explaining the eight specific items, the chapters are all linked in pairs, except that "making the thoughts sincere" forms a single chapter by itself; is this not because making the thoughts sincere is the starting point of self-cultivation? The chapter on the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge was lost. Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] took the ideas of the Masters Cheng [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] to supplement it, without imitating the style of Master Zeng's [Zengzi 曾子] commentary; as he himself said, he had privately tried to imitate that style in writing it, but ultimately could not succeed—for literary style varies with the times, whereas the underlying principle remains one and the same.

As for the book of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), it begins by speaking of human nature, the Way, and instruction, and then immediately goes on to speak solely of the Way without mentioning nature or instruction; this is because nature is the source of the Way, and instruction is the application of the Way. In Chapter Twenty-One, it speaks solely of nature and instruction without mentioning the Way; this is because nature is the Way of Heaven, and instruction is the Way of Man. However, when it first speaks of the nature conferred by Heaven's decree and the instruction that cultivates the Way, it is speaking in terms of the definitions of nature and instruction; when it later speaks of the nature that achieves enlightenment from sincerity and the instruction that achieves sincerity from enlightenment, it is speaking in terms of the distinction between the sage and the worthy. The difference between the two can thus be seen. At the beginning, what is called the nature conferred by Heaven's decree is equilibrium before the feelings are aroused; the Way that accords with nature is equilibrium after they are aroused; and instruction is that by which excess and deficiency are regulated so as to return to equilibrium—herein lies the meaning of the treatise's title. Under Chapter Eleven, [Master Zhu's commentary] already states that the main gist of this treatise takes wisdom, humanity, and courage as the gateway to entering the Way, and at Chapter Twenty it further states that sincerity is truly the pivot of this treatise. This is because wisdom is that by which one knows this principle, humanity is that by which one embodies this principle, courage is that by which one strives in this principle, and sincerity in turn is that by which one makes this wisdom, humanity, and courage real. Spoken of in detail, although there is the…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
分約言之不過一誠而已首章所謂一篇之體
要末章又謂舉一篇之要而約言之者蓋首章
自存養省察之功推而至於聖神功化之極末
章自下學立心之始推而極之以馴致乎篤恭
而天下平之盛亦一理而已愚也於大學中庸
二書未能造其閫奧姑述所聞以復惟執事進
而教之
第四問
彭教
===
同考試官教諭諸　批〔策場正欲觀士子學識作者往往皆鑿爲臆說殊無定見惟此策議引聖人〕
〔事實皆有證據有學有識之士也〕
同考試官學正林　批〔宣聖事實滿場答者不能〕
〔無疑惟此作詳明宜錄出之〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔條答問目略無所遺若末篇言聖〕
〔人者〕
甚矣先孔子而聖者非孔子無以明後孔子而
聖者非孔子無以法蓋道德高厚教化無窮自
punctuated:
分，約言之，不過一誠而已。首章所謂一篇之體要，末章又謂舉一篇之要而約言之者，蓋首章自存養省察之功，推而至於聖神功化之極；末章自下學立心之始，推而極之，以馴致乎篤恭而天下平之盛，亦一理而已。愚也於《大學》、《中庸》二書，未能造其閫奧，姑述所聞以復，惟執事進而教之。

第四問
彭教
同考試官教諭諸　批〔策場正欲觀士子學識，作者往往皆鑿爲臆說，殊無定見。惟此策議引聖人〕〔事實，皆有證據，有學有識之士也。〕
同考試官學正林　批〔宣聖事實，滿場答者不能〕〔無疑，惟此作詳明，宜錄出之。〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔條答問目，略無所遺，若末篇言聖〕〔人者。〕

甚矣，先孔子而聖者，非孔子無以明；後孔子而聖者，非孔子無以法。蓋道德高厚，教化無窮，自
translation_en:
…distinction [between wisdom, humanity, and courage], when stated concisely, it is nothing more than single-minded sincerity. As for why the first chapter is called the essential substance of the entire work, while the final chapter is said to take up the essentials of the entire work and summarize them: the first chapter extends from the effort of preservation, nourishment, and self-examination all the way to the ultimate transformative achievements of the sage and the spirit; the final chapter extends from the initial establishment of the mind in lower-level learning and pushes it to the extreme, gradually reaching the flourishing state where through devout reverence the whole world is brought to peace. It is all one and the same principle. In my ignorance, I have not yet been able to penetrate the inner depths of the two books, the Great Learning (Daxue) and the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong). I merely set forth what I have heard in reply, and pray that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me.

Fourth Question
Peng Jiao 彭教
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Zhu, comments: [The policy session is precisely where we wish to observe the learning and insight of the candidates, yet writers all too often force their points into mere conjecture, completely lacking settled views. Only this policy essay, in its discussion and citation of the facts concerning the Sage, has solid evidence throughout; he is a scholar of both learning and insight.]
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Lin, comments: [Regarding the facts about the Exalted Sage (Confucius), throughout the examination hall those who answered could not avoid leaving doubts; only this composition is detailed and clear, and ought to be selected for publication.]
Examiner, County Director of Studies Weng, comments: [It answers the points of the question item by item with virtually nothing omitted, especially in the final section speaking of the Sage [?].]

Indeed! The sages who came before Confucius could not have been made manifest without Confucius; the sages who came after Confucius could not have had a model to follow without Confucius. For his moral power was lofty and profound, and his transformative teaching inexhaustible; since…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
生民以來未有盛於孔子者也豈後人私心所
能窺妄議所敢加哉今因執事設疑致問而紬
繹以對且夫聖人之生也應五百年亨嘉之期
其沒也開億萬世道學之緒非偶然也則夫尼
丘之禱兩盈之夢何足疑哉序叙書斷自於唐虞
春秋致嚴於褒貶所謂道宗堯舜法守文武豈
無徵哉相事初攝而有齊魯夾谷之誘嘉於聖
人何所損政化甫成而有衮衣章甫之謗其於
聖人何所加雖云軍旅未學而拒卻萊兵蓋有
===
文事者必有武備焉有德無位而制定禮樂蓋
篤於傳述而非創始焉亂於政者誅之不爲姑
息之愛也不同道者惡之其亦自然之勢也天
理渾然至樂所寓何恤於疏食水飲之貧禮樂
之文斯須不離何有於絶糧困乏之病外貌之
異偶肖於陽虎無害於斯文也盛德之至不合
於州仇無傷於至聖也賢於堯舜者事功之著
門弟子之稱頌耳竊比老彭者傳述之事夫子
之自謙耳尼谿未就而卒沮於晏嬰魯相未幾
punctuated: 生民以來，未有盛於孔子者也。豈後人私心所能窺、妄議所敢加哉？今因執事設疑致問，而紬繹以對。且夫聖人之生也，應五百年亨嘉之期；其沒也，開億萬世道學之緒，非偶然也。則夫尼丘之禱、兩盈之夢，何足疑哉？序叙《書》斷自於唐、虞，《春秋》致嚴於褒貶，所謂道宗堯、舜，法守文、武，豈無徵哉？相事初攝，而有齊、魯夾谷之誘，嘉於聖人何所損？政化甫成，而有衮衣、章甫之謗，其於聖人何所加？雖云軍旅未學，而拒卻萊兵，蓋有文事者必有武備焉；有德無位，而制定禮樂，蓋篤於傳述而非創始焉。亂於政者誅之，不爲姑息之愛也；不同道者惡之，其亦自然之勢也。天理渾然，至樂所寓，何恤於疏食水飲之貧？禮樂之文，斯須不離，何有於絶糧困乏之病？外貌之異，偶肖於陽虎，無害於斯文也；盛德之至，不合於州仇，無傷於至聖也。賢於堯、舜者，事功之著，門弟子之稱頌耳；竊比老、彭者，傳述之事，夫子之自謙耳。尼谿未就，而卒沮於晏嬰；魯相未幾，
translation_en: … the beginning of mankind, there has never been anyone greater than Confucius. How could he be fathomed by the selfish minds of later generations, or subjected to their reckless criticisms? Now, because Your Excellency has raised doubts and posed questions, I shall draw out the threads to reply. Moreover, the birth of the Sage corresponded to the auspicious cycle of five hundred years, and his passing opened the succession of the Learning of the Way for myriads of generations—this was no mere coincidence. Why, then, should the prayer at Mount Niqiu or the dream between the two pillars [two Ying (?)] be doubted? In prefacing and arranging the Book of Documents, he began from Tang and Yu; in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he exercised strictness in praise and blame. Thus the saying that he took Yao and Shun as the ancestors of his Way and upheld the laws of King Wen and King Wu—how could it be without evidence? When he first acted as prime minister and there was the enticement between Qi and Lu at Jiagu, what loss did that bring to the Sage [reading 嘉 as 其 (?)]? When his political transformation had just been accomplished and there was the slander regarding his ceremonial robes and Zhangfu cap, what did that add to or detract from the Sage? Although he said he had not studied military affairs, he repelled the troops of Lai, for whoever has civil affairs must also have military preparations; possessing virtue without the throne, he fixed and ordered ritual and music, for he was devoted to transmitting and recounting rather than originating. Those who brought disorder to governance he executed, not indulging in tolerant affection; those who did not share his Way he disliked, which was likewise a natural course. With Heavenly Principle complete in him and supreme joy residing within, what concern had he for the poverty of coarse rice and water to drink? Not departing from the refinement of ritual and music for an instant, what to him was the distress of running out of provisions? That his outward appearance happened to resemble Yang Hu did no harm to this culture; that in the perfection of his flourishing virtue he did not get along with Zhouqiu did no injury to the Supreme Sage. That he was "worthier than Yao and Shun" referred to the manifestation of his achievements and was merely the praise of his disciples; that he "ventured to compare himself to Old Peng" referred to the work of transmitting and was merely the Master's own modesty. That the enfeoffment at Nixi was not realized and was finally thwarted by Yan Ying, and that not long after becoming acting minister of Lu…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
而終閒於女樂天之未欲平治天下也可見周
流四方而存行道濟時之心行不殺見而有見
幾明決之意聖之得乎仕止久速也可知彼其
觀於鄉飲見夫五行之俱備學未知王道之易
易乎射於矍相嚴於序點之揚言寧不致觀者
之僅存乎過庭之訓詩禮在所急也天喪之慟
乎淵道所係也賜焉惜不若已者居商焉悅賢
於己者處烏得無損益之殊由也兼勝於人求
也遜然畏縮烏得無進退之異由是觀之則聖
===
人之存沒固不偶然而聖人之言行亦豈徒然
哉是以春風壇杏萬世尊師洙泗源流百代瞻
仰不然何以被衮冕而衆無疏而王褒崇之典有
加而無替享祀之儀有腆而不薄哉
第五問
同考試官教諭諸　批〔此策學者多不能記但從舉以對不切事實惟此篇隨問隨答略〕
彭　教
無若滯且五策俱優擢之以為多士之冠
punctuated:
而終閒於女樂，天之未欲平治天下也可見；周流四方而存行道濟時之心，行不殺見而有見幾明決之意，聖之得乎仕止久速也可知。彼其觀於鄉飲，見夫五行之俱備，學未知王道之易易乎？射於矍相，嚴於序點之揚言，寧不致觀者之僅存乎？過庭之訓，《詩》《禮》在所急也；天喪之慟，乎淵道所係也。賜焉惜不若已者居，商焉悅賢於己者處，烏得無損益之殊？由也兼勝於人，求也遜然畏縮，烏得無進退之異？由是觀之，則聖人之存沒固不偶然，而聖人之言行亦豈徒然哉？是以春風壇杏，萬世尊師；洙泗源流，百代瞻仰。不然，何以被衮冕而衆，無疏而王，褒崇之典有加而無替，享祀之儀有腆而不薄哉？
第五問
彭教
同考試官教諭諸批：〔此策學者多不能記，但從舉以對，不切事實。惟此篇隨問隨答，略無若滯，且五策俱優，擢之以為多士之冠。〕
translation_en:
…and was finally estranged by the female musicians—that Heaven did not yet wish to bring peace and order to the world can thus be seen. He traveled throughout the four quarters while preserving the heart to practice the Way and rescue the age; he departed without waiting to have an audience [?], showing the resolve to perceive the subtle signs and decide clearly—that the Sage attained the right measure in taking office, stopping, tarrying, or hastening can thus be known. When he observed the district symposium, seeing that those five conducts were all complete, how could one not know [?] that the Kingly Way is so easy? When he practiced archery at Juexiang, being strict in the public declarations of Xu Dian, how could it not result in only a few spectators remaining? In the instruction given while passing through the courtyard, the Odes (Shi) and the Rites (Li) were what was urgent; in his grief crying "Heaven is destroying me!", it was because the Way rested with Yan Yuan [?]. Zigong (Si) regretted [?] dwelling with those not equal to himself, while Zixia (Shang) delighted in associating with those worthier than himself—how could there not be a difference between detriment and benefit? Zilu (You) had the energy of two men, while Ran Qiu (Qiu) modestly shrank back—how could there not be a difference in urging forward and holding back? Viewed from this perspective, the life and death of the Sage were certainly not accidental, and how could the words and deeds of the Sage be in vain? Therefore, amid the spring breeze at the Apricot Altar, ten thousand generations revere him as Teacher; from the source and stream of the Zhu and Si rivers, a hundred ages look up to him in veneration. Otherwise, why would he wear the ceremonial robes and crown of a duke [?] and become king without a fief [?], with the statutes of praise and exaltation ever increasing and never declining, and the rites of sacrifice and offering ever rich and never meager?

Fifth Policy Question
Peng Jiao
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu comments: [Most scholars could not remember the material for this policy question, and merely cited generalities in reply without fitting the actual facts. Only this essay answers each point as it is asked, with no sign of blockage or hesitation [?]; moreover, all five of his policy essays are outstanding, so we have selected him to crown the multitude of scholars.]

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭翁　批　策能知人以實守法持正之間
且歸宿正大有志之士也
嘗謂事君必先於守法修己必重於持正事君
而守法則有堅定之節修己而持正則有特立
之操節操如是不謂之君子而何式稽於古
犯蹕罪輕而不問旨以從重受贓罪重而不拘
人以從輕非張釋之狂光韶之在廷尉乎二子
議論皆當而釋之遠誅之言爲未備□以詐冒
而真選人於死不以過誤而陷郎將於刑歟
===
冑狀仁傑之在大理乎二子立心皆同而仁傑
後唐之所爲獨感何並宗顏川而首驅贓掾蘇
章刺冀州而不私故人所以成郡中清靜境內
肅然之治虞延令洛陽而巨盜伏誅何孟容尹
京兆而軍吏受繫所以致外戚歛手豪右歛迹
之功至若趙綽任刑部侍郎不奉詐卒曹之詔
李元紘爲戶參軍不改競磑之判何曾若
非守法之士乎若夫火災天數禳之何益狄子
產之拒禆竈則曰焉知天道儲副國本豈可無
punctuated:
考試官教諭翁　批：策能知人以實，守法持正之間，且歸宿正大，有志之士也。

嘗謂事君必先於守法，修己必重於持正。事君而守法，則有堅定之節；修己而持正，則有特立之操。節操如是，不謂之君子而何？式稽於古：犯蹕罪輕，而不問旨以從重；受贓罪重，而不拘人以從輕，非張釋之、狂光韶之在廷尉乎？二子議論皆當，而釋之「遠誅」之言爲未備。□以詐冒而真選人於死，不以過誤而陷郎將於刑，歟冑狀、仁傑之在大理乎？二子立心皆同，而仁傑復唐之所爲獨盛。何並宗顏川而首驅贓掾，蘇章刺冀州而不私故人，所以成郡中清靜、境內肅然之治；虞延令洛陽而巨盜伏誅，何孟容尹京兆而軍吏受繫，所以致外戚歛手、豪右歛迹之功。至若趙綽任刑部侍郎，不奉詐卒曹之詔；李元紘爲戶參軍，不改競磑之判，何曾若非守法之士乎？若夫火災天數，禳之何益？狄子產之拒禆竈，則曰「焉知天道」；儲副國本，豈可無
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Weng comments: This policy essay shows an ability to judge men by actual facts in the matters of upholding the law and maintaining rectitude, and its conclusion is upright and grand—he is a scholar of high aspirations.

It has been said that in serving one's ruler, one must first of all uphold the law, and in cultivating oneself, one must place weight on maintaining rectitude. If one upholds the law in serving the ruler, one possesses steadfast integrity; if one maintains rectitude in cultivating oneself, one possesses independent principles. With integrity and principles such as these, how could one not be called a gentleman? Let us examine antiquity: when the offense of violating an imperialprocession clearance was light, not complying with an imperial wish to impose a heavy punishment; and when the crime of taking bribes was heavy, not accommodating others to grant a light sentence—were these not Zhang Shizhi 張釋之 and Cui Guangshao 崔光韶 [transcribed 狂光韶] when they served as Chamberlain for Law Enforcement? The arguments of both men were fitting, though Shizhi's remark about "executing him on the spot" was less than sound. Refusing [?] to put a candidate for office to death for fraudulent claims, and refusing to condemn a Commandant of Escorts to punishment for an inadvertent error—were these not Dai Zhou 戴冑 [transcribed 歟冑狀] and Di Renjie 狄仁傑 when they served in the Court of Judicial Review? The intentions of both men were the same, yet Renjie's achievement in restoring the Tang was uniquely great [transcribed 後唐之所爲獨感]. He Bing 何並 governed Yingchuan 潁川 [transcribed 宗顏川] and first drove out corrupt subalterns, while Su Zhang 蘇章 served as Regional Inspector of Jizhou 冀州 and showed no partiality to an old friend; thus they achieved administrations in which the commandery was tranquil and the region was reverently orderly. Yu Yan 虞延 served as Magistrate of Luoyang 洛陽 and great bandits submitted to execution, while Xu Mengrong 許孟容 [transcribed 何孟容] served as Governor of Jingzhao 京兆 and a military subaltern was bound in fetters; thus they attained the merit of making imperial in-laws stay their hands and powerful magnates cover their tracks. As for Zhao Chuo 趙綽 serving as Vice Minister of Justice and refusing to carry out an edict to execute men of the bureau [?], and Li Yuanhong 李元紘 serving as Revenue Manager and refusing to alter his legal judgment on a disputed watermill—how could any of them not be men who upheld the law? As for fire disasters being the predetermined course of Heaven, what benefit is there in praying to avert them? Thus [transcribed 狄] Zichan 子產, in rejecting Pi Zao 裨竈, said, "How can he know the Way of Heaven?" And as the heir apparent is the foundation of the state, how can he randomly [be shaken?]…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
搖故周昌之諫高祖則曰臣不奉詔是雖均爲
大夫而稱遺愛者子產也操執絲竹則下同伶
人此稽紹之所不爲夜候開門恐變生矯詐此
謝莊之能遠慮是雖均爲侍中而著死節者稽
紹也夫盎爲郎中寵姬僭坐盎則却之而苦以
當鑒人彘郅惲爲上東城門候御輦宵還惲則
拒之而諫以當念宗社其所以致金帛之賜者
有由矣任延遷武威而光武喻以善事上官褚
遂良知起居而太宗謂其朕過亦記其所以激
===
忠讜之言有自矣至若馬知節任樞密而面詆
奸回張昇拜御史中丞而稱爲孤立何莫而非
持正之士乎吁合數子而論之守法持正不爲
阿黨之計其昭然大節毅然雅操談者固可羨
可愕殊不知由君子觀之則皆未臻成德之實
也尚友千古充當志伊尹之志學顏子之學而
後可姑以是復明問執事以爲如何
punctuated:
搖，故周昌之諫高祖則曰：「臣不奉詔。」是雖均爲大夫，而稱遺愛者，子產也。操執絲竹，則下同伶人，此稽紹之所不爲；夜候開門，恐變生矯詐，此謝莊之能遠慮。是雖均爲侍中，而著死節者，稽紹也。夫盎爲郎中，寵姬僭坐，盎則却之，而苦以當鑒「人彘」；郅惲爲上東城門候，御輦宵還，惲則拒之，而諫以當念宗社。其所以致金帛之賜者，有由矣。任延遷武威，而光武喻以善事上官；褚遂良知起居，而太宗謂其「朕過亦記」。其所以激忠讜之言，有自矣。至若馬知節任樞密，而面詆奸回；張昇拜御史中丞，而稱爲孤立：何莫而非持正之士乎！
吁！合數子而論之，守法持正，不爲阿黨之計，其昭然大節、毅然雅操，談者固可羨可愕；殊不知由君子觀之，則皆未臻成德之實也。尚友千古，充當志伊尹之志、學顏子之學而後可。姑以是復明問，執事以爲如何？
translation_en:
…be shaken? Thus when Zhou Chang 周昌 remonstrated with Emperor Gaozu 高祖, he said, "Your servant will not obey the edict." Although both were Grand Masters, the one praised for bequeathing love to the people was Zichan 子產. Holding stringed and bamboo instruments would lower oneself to the level of actors, which was something Ji Shao 稽紹 [Xi Shao 嵇紹] refused to do; waiting at night to open the city gates, fearing that rebellion might arise from forged orders, showed how Xie Zhuang 謝莊 could take long-term precautions. Although both served as Palace Attendants, the one renowned for dying for his integrity was Ji Shao. When [Yuan] Ang [袁]盎 was an Attendant Gentleman and a favored concubine presumptuously took a seat beside the emperor and empress, Ang moved her back and earnestly warned that she should take a lesson from the "human swine"; when Zhi Yun 郅惲 was Gatewaiter of the Shangdong Gate and the imperial carriage returned at night, Yun refused entry and remonstrated that the emperor ought to think of the ancestral temples and altars of the state. There was good reason why they earned rewards of gold and silk! When Ren Yan 任延 was transferred to Wuwei 武威, Emperor Guangwu 光武 instructed him to serve his superior officials well; when Chu Suiliang 褚遂良 was in charge of the Court Diaries, Emperor Taizong 太宗 asked him whether he would "also record Our faults." Their being stirred to utter loyal and honest words had its source! As for Ma Zhijie 馬知節 serving in the Bureau of Military Affairs and denouncing wicked and devious men to their faces, or Zhang Sheng 張昇 being appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and being praised as standing alone without faction—how could any of them not be gentlemen who upheld rectitude!

Alas! If we consider these several men together, they abided by the law and upheld rectitude without scheming to flatter or form cliques. Their resplendent great integrity and resolute, refined conduct are certainly enough to make those who speak of them admire and marvel. Yet they do not realize that, viewed by a true gentleman, none of them had yet attained the substance of perfected virtue. In befriending the ancients across a thousand ages, one must fulfill [?] setting one's mind on what Yi Yin 伊尹 set his mind on, and learning what Master Yan 顏子 learned, before it is sufficient. I tentatively offer this in reply to your enlightened question; what do you, sir, think of it?

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
自成周鄉舉里選之後取士
之制莫重於科目然或尚浮
華而不根藝實或行之疏數
而靡有定歲故科目雖設徒
具其名而其實不能無可議
者哉
===
朝求實設科掛酌古制三年大
比舉於鄉闈升於春官以經
義驗其實學以論策觀其底
蘊登斯選者復□於
廷奉
清問制度品式詳明盡善實有得
於成周選舉之遺意也夫成
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

自成周鄉舉里選之後，取士之制莫重於科目。然或尚浮華而不根藝實，或行之疏數而靡有定歲，故科目雖設，徒具其名，而其實不能無可議者。哉朝求實設科，掛酌古制，三年大比，舉於鄉闈，升於春官，以經義驗其實學，以論策觀其底蘊，登斯選者，復□於廷，奉清問。制度品式，詳明盡善，實有得於成周選舉之遺意也。夫成
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Since the system of recommendation by districts and selection by hamlets in the era of the Zhou at its height, no institution for selecting scholars has been more important than the examination categories. Yet at times they esteemed superficial华 [ornamentation] without being rooted in the substance of the arts [? 藝實, likely a transcription error for 其實], and at times they were held at irregular intervals without fixed years. Thus, although examination categories were established, they merely possessed the name, while their reality could not be free from points open to criticism. 

Our Dynasty [reading 哉 as 我] seeks substance in establishing the examinations, weighing and adapting ancient institutions. Every three years at the Great Comparison, candidates are recommended from the provincial examination compounds and presented to the Spring Office [Ministry of Rites]. Exposition of the Classics is used to verify their substantial learning, and discourses and policy essays are used to observe the depths of their attainment. Those who ascend through this selection are again [examined / presented □] at Court to receive the Emperor's pure inquiry. The institutional system and its regulations and forms are detailed, clear, and thoroughly perfected, truly capturing the inherited intent of selection and recommendation in the Zhou at its height. Now, in the Zhou at its height…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
周作人之實詠於詩載於書
漢唐而下顧治之君監于成
憲孰不欲鼓舞斯世網羅俊
乂得實才之用以爲之輔哉
顧以養之取之之實其道有
未盡焉爾
國朝自洪武至今百年于兹
===
列聖相承深仁厚澤典章制作盡
憲海內
皇上克篤前烈嗣位之初首條列
學政首舉德行振警士習𡚁
以踐履實蹈爲教由是髦士
攸宜俊民用章雖詩書所稱
不是過成周作人之效同休
punctuated: 周作人之實，詠於《詩》，載於《書》。漢、唐而下，顧治之君監于成憲，孰不欲鼓舞斯世，網羅俊乂，得實才之用以爲之輔哉？顧以養之、取之之實，其道有未盡焉爾。國朝自洪武至今，百年于兹，列聖相承，深仁厚澤、典章制作，盡憲海內。皇上克篤前烈，嗣位之初，首條列學政，首舉德行，振警士習𡚁，以踐履實蹈爲教。由是髦士攸宜，俊民用章，雖《詩》、《書》所稱不是過，成周作人之效，同休
translation_en:
… Zhou in cultivating men of talent is sung of in the Odes and recorded in the Documents. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, among rulers who aspired to good governance and looked to established models, who did not wish to inspire their age, gather in men of outstanding ability, and obtain the service of true talent to assist them? Yet in the substance of how they nurtured and selected them, their methods were not completely realized.

Since the Hongwu era [1368–1398], our dynasty has now endured for nearly a hundred years. A succession of sacred emperors has carried on the line; their profound benevolence, generous favor, and institutional creations have served entirely as a model for all within the seas. His Majesty has capably strengthened the achievements of his predecessors. At the very beginning of his succession to the throne, he first set forth regulations for school administration, placing foremost the promotion of moral conduct, rousing and reforming the abuses [?] in literati customs, and making practical implementation and genuine conduct the basis of instruction. Consequently, eminent scholars are well-suited to their roles, and men of outstanding talent are made manifest. Even what is praised in the Odes and the Documents does not surpass this; in the efficacy of cultivating men of talent as in the flourishing Zhou, it shares the same splendor…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
而蟣美矣江右文獻之邦素
稱多士今之得雋者覆
朝廷作養有素而興勸激昂又
有諸大臣鎮臨其地前輩舊
德為之儀刑故其文義優深
充然有得皆平日實學積於
中者所發是誠不負作育之
===
仁不負獎拔之意矣然所行
弗踐所學君子不為也由是
而顯有祿秩要必以實得於
己者推之以為德為民使勳
業有聞操履無玷卓然以成
周之士自處俾天下後世皆
稱之曰是
punctuated: 而蟣美矣。江右文獻之邦，素稱多士。今之得雋者，覆朝廷作養有素，而興勸激昂，又有諸大臣鎮臨其地，前輩舊德為之儀刑，故其文義優深，充然有得，皆平日實學積於中者所發。是誠不負作育之仁，不負獎拔之意矣。然所行弗踐所學，君子不為也。由是而顯有祿秩，要必以實得於己者，推之以為德、為民，使勳業有聞，操履無玷，卓然以成周之士自處，俾天下後世皆稱之曰：「是
translation_en:
… and matches it in beauty [? 蟣 for 媲/儷]. Jiangxi is a land of culture and worthy traditions, long renowned for its abundance of scholars. Those who have achieved distinction today not only rely on [? 覆 for 荷/賴] the Court's long-standing cultivation and nurture, which has inspired and roused them, but also have the various grand ministers governing this region and the veteran worthies of earlier generations serving as their models. Therefore, their literary compositions and grasp of meaning are refined and profound, full of genuine attainment—all bursting forth from the practical learning accumulated within them in ordinary times. This truly does not betray the benevolence that nurtured them, nor does it betray the intention behind their encouragement and selection.

Yet to fail to put into practice what one has learned is something a gentleman will not do. Rising from this to attain prominence and official emoluments and rank, they must take what they have genuinely attained within themselves and extend it to cultivate virtue and serve the people, so that their meritorious achievements become renowned and their personal conduct remains without blemish. Standing tall, they should comport themselves as scholars of the flourishing Zhou era, causing the entire realm and future generations to praise them, saying: "These are…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖朝所育之才也是某科所得之
士也則有光於文獻之邦有
光於科目之選而
皇上簡賢圖治之心庶可報稱於
萬一也故事登名有錄鋟成
序此以勸之云
直隸河間府景州吳橋縣儒
===
學教諭莆田翁淼序
alt_text:
1: 聖朝所畜之才也是其科所得之
2: 士也則有光於文獻之邦有
3: 光於科目之選而
4: 皇上簡賢圖治之心庶可報稱於
5: 萬一也故事登名有録録成
6: 序此以勸之云
7: 直隸河間府景州吳橋縣儒
8: 學教諭莆田翁淼序
聖朝所畜之才也是其科所得之
士也則有光於文獻之邦有
光於科目之選而
皇上簡賢圖治之心庶可報稱於
萬一也故事登名有録録成
序此以勸之云
直隸河間府景州吳橋縣儒
學教諭莆田翁淼序
punctuated:
聖朝所育之才也，是某科所得之士也。」則有光於文獻之邦，有光於科目之選，而皇上簡賢圖治之心，庶可報稱於萬一也。故事，登名有錄。鋟成，序此以勸之云。
直隸河間府景州吳橋縣儒學教諭莆田翁淼序。
translation_en:
… a talent nurtured by the Sacred Dynasty; this is a scholar obtained in such-and-such an examination!’ Then they will bring glory to this land of culture and learning and bring glory to the selection through the examination categories, and His Majesty’s intention of selecting the worthy and planning for good governance may perhaps be repaid in one part out of ten thousand. By precedent, there is a record registering the names of those who passed. Now that the woodblock carving is completed, I write this preface to encourage them.

Preface by Weng Miao 翁淼 of Putian 莆田, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wuqiao County 吳橋縣 in Jing Subprefecture 景州, Hejian Prefecture 河間府, in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸).

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試録序
粤稽成周賢書之貢必加禮
受三物之教必曰賓興所以
重其事而爲爲士者勸也其
在當時多士濟濟吉人藹藹
用致垂拱無爲旣醉太平之
治殆亦有由然哉洪惟我
===
朝
列聖代作
皇上一德相承科目取士尤加崇
重故自鄉舉貢春官進對
大廷
賜名進士俾得釋褐拜秩沾被
恩榮勸勵之意至矣盡矣江西文
punctuated:
江西鄉試録序

粤稽成周，賢書之貢必加禮受，三物之教必曰賓興，所以重其事而爲爲士者勸也。其在當時，多士濟濟，吉人藹藹，用致垂拱無爲、旣醉太平之治，殆亦有由然哉！洪惟我朝列聖代作，皇上一德相承，科目取士，尤加崇重。故自鄉舉貢春官，進對大廷，賜名進士，俾得釋褐拜秩，沾被恩榮，勸勵之意，至矣盡矣！江西文
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

When we examine the era of the accomplished Zhou dynasty, the tribute of the registers of the worthy was always received with ceremonial礼 (courtesy), and the instruction in the Three Matters was always referred to as raising up the worthy as guests (binxing). This was how they attached great importance to the affair and provided encouragement to those who served as scholars. At that time, the numerous scholars were dignified and abundant, and the virtuous men were harmonious andflourishing, whereby they brought about the governance of ruling with hands folded in non-action and theGreat Peace celebrated in the ode "Already Drunk" (Jizui)—surely there was a reason for this! 

Reflecting grandly upon our Dynasty, a succession of sacred emperors has arisen generation after generation, and His Majesty the Emperor has inherited their single-minded virtue, placing even greater esteem and weight on selecting scholars through the examination system. Thus, from being recommended in the local examinations and presented to the Ministry of Rites (Chunguan), they advance to reply in the Great Court and are bestowed the title of metropolitan graduate (jinshi), enabling them to cast off their coarse woolens, receive official rank, and be bathed in imperial favor and glory—the intention of encouraging and inspiring them has reached the utmost perfection! Jiangxi, a [province of] literary…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
獻臣藩古今名臣偉器胥此
焉出肆當大比賓興之歲時
則有若太監葉達奉
命鎮守監察御史夏塤按節分巡
方岳重臣秪率彝典舉行百
爾程度咸正罔缺比鎖院也
內則綜理於監察御史楊銓
===
而戒飭防範之愈嚴躬親於
左布政使黃琛按察使原傑
左參政胡淵副使張鎣而提
督監蒞之兼至外則協規於
右布政使宋欽右參政楊文
琳副使章繪左參議唐宗僉
事余復程亨宋儒朱華應欽
punctuated: 獻臣藩，古今名臣偉器胥此焉出。肆當大比賓興之歲，時則有若太監葉達奉命鎮守，監察御史夏塤按節分巡，方岳重臣秪率彝典舉行，百爾程度咸正罔缺。比鎖院也，內則綜理於監察御史楊銓，而戒飭防範之愈嚴；躬親於左布政使黃琛、按察使原傑、左參政胡淵、副使張鎣，而提督監蒞之兼至。外則協規於右布政使宋欽、右參政楊文琳、副使章繪、左參議唐宗、僉事余復、程亨、宋儒、朱華、應欽、
translation_en: …is a great province of letters and worthy exemplars, from which renowned ministers and men of great capacity, both past and present, have all emerged. Now, upon this year of the triennial examination and the presentation of worthy men as guests, there are such figures as Grand Defender Eunuch Ye Da 葉達, who by imperial command stands guard over the province, and Investigating Censor Xia Xun 夏塤, who holds his credentials on circuit inspection; together with the senior provincial officials, they respectfully follow the established statutes in carrying out the proceedings, so that every regulation and measure is upright and without deficiency. When the examination compound was locked, within, overall management was handled by Investigating Censor Yang Quan 楊銓, making the admonitions and security precautions ever stricter; personal attention was given by Left Administration Commissioner Huang Chen 黃琛, Surveillance Commissioner Yuan Jie 原傑, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Yuan 胡淵, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Ying 張鎣, bringing direction and supervision to perfection alike. Without, regulations were coordinated by Right Administration Commissioner Song Qin 宋欽, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Yang Wenlin 楊文琳, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Hui 章繪, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Tang Zong 唐宗, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Yu Fu 余復, Cheng Heng 程亨, Song Ru 宋儒, Zhu Hua 朱華, Ying Qin 應欽,…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
王廸而贊相維持之益力王
等忝竊甄别黜陟之柄尤各
凝神注思徯楚簡閱而不敢
玩視忽取是盖同一薦賢爲
國之公心可以臨之天地而無
愧質之鬼神而無歉士有三
郡士若干輩爭執所長引觚
===
灑翰聲揚蘊於三塲角勝負
於寸晷懽聲雷動鋭氣霄騰
誠太平之瑞應擴人文以宣
朗句有餘日繼之以夜閲卷
累千而詳擇之得千百焉由
千百而精擇之得累百十焉
又累百十而益精之得數滿
punctuated: 王廸，而贊相維持之益力。王等忝竊甄别黜陟之柄，尤各凝神注思，徯楚簡閱，而不敢玩視忽取。是盖同一薦賢爲國之公心，可以臨之天地而無愧，質之鬼神而無歉。士有三郡士若干輩，爭執所長，引觚灑翰，聲揚蘊於三塲，角勝負於寸晷。懽聲雷動，鋭氣霄騰，誠太平之瑞應，擴人文以宣朗。句有餘日，繼之以夜，閲卷累千而詳擇之，得千百焉；由千百而精擇之，得累百十焉；又累百十而益精之，得數滿
translation_en:
…and Wang Di 王廸, so that assistance and maintenance were exerted with all the more vigor. Wang and the other examiners, having the unworthy privilege of holding the authority to discern, select, demote, and promote, each all the more concentrated our spirits and focused our thoughts, awaiting the outstanding talents [?] as we examined and reviewed the papers, not daring to view them lightly or select them carelessly. This was indeed because all shared the same public-spirited mind of recommending the worthy for the state—an attitude with which one can face Heaven and Earth without shame, and call upon ghosts and spirits as witnesses without regret.

There were some several thousand scholars from the thirteen [?] prefectures [reading 十三郡 for 士有三郡] who vied to display their strengths, taking up writing tablets and wielding their brushes, pouring forth their stored learning [reading 罄蘊 for 聲揚蘊?] across the three sessions and contesting for victory within inches of shadow on the sundial. Joyful voices rumbled like thunder, and keen spirits soared to the skies; truly it was an auspicious sign of an era of great peace, expanding cultural refinement to shine forth brightly. For more than ten days [reading 旬 for 句], continuing through the nights, we read through thousands of papers and selected from them in detail, obtaining over a thousand; from those thousand and several hundred we made a refined selection, obtaining several hundred; and from those several hundred we refined our selection even further, obtaining a number that reached a full…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
百而除五焉盖惟解額是遵
而取之弗容過也已而第其
氏名與其文辭尤粹者鋟録
以傳授王序夫惟文者德之
著名者實之符群士子仰沐
聖化樂育滋久既以是德著而爲
文復以是文播而爲名又以
===
是名登貢賢之書賓興之
列駸駸步武亨衢亦曰逢矣
逢而至於達也其不自茲始
乎然其達也豈徒文具名稱
云乎哉宜必激昂奮發竭知
攄忠思效多士吉人所爲于
以賛
punctuated: 百而除五焉，盖惟解額是遵，而取之弗容過也。已而第其氏名，與其文辭尤粹者，鋟録以傳，授王序。夫惟文者，德之著；名者，實之符。群士子仰沐聖化，樂育滋久，既以是德著而爲文，復以是文播而爲名，又以是名登貢賢之書、賓興之列，駸駸步武亨衢，亦曰逢矣！逢而至於達也，其不自茲始乎？然其達也，豈徒文具名稱云乎哉？宜必激昂奮發，竭知攄忠，思效多士吉人所爲，于以賛
translation_en:
…a hundred less five [i.e. ninety-five], for we strictly adhered to the provincial quota and were not permitted to exceed it in our selection. Thereafter, we ranked their names and took their most refined essays to be carved onto blocks for circulation, entrusting the preface to me, Wang.

Now, literary composition is the manifestation of virtue, and reputation is the tally of substance. For a long time, the assembled scholars have looked up to and bathed in the sacred transformative influence, rejoicing in their nurturing. Having already manifested this virtue as literary composition, they have further broadcast this literary composition to become their reputation, and by means of this reputation they have ascended into the register of tribute-worthy men and the ranks of those recommended as guests of the state. Striding briskly along the open highway of official advancement, they may indeed be said to have met with auspicious opportunity! Having met with opportunity and going on to attain high station—does it not begin right here? Yet in attaining high station, how could it merely be a matter of outward literary form and titular reputation? They ought surely to be roused and inspired to exert themselves, exhausting their wisdom and pouring forth their loyalty, longing to emulate the deeds of the many fine scholars and virtuous men of old, thereby assisting…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
治化而佐太平庶幾文徳攸䝉
名實相須而
聖朝興賢勸士之效足以暴白天
下後世而於歴科前哲益有
光矣先儒志進舉有言方其
取以辭章類若浮文而夕實
及其臨㕛設施奮其事業隱
===
然爲國名臣者不可勝數玉
於是録亦深有望於群士子
云
天順三年八月穀旦直隸河
間府儒學教授四明邵玉序
punctuated:
治化而佐太平，庶幾文徳攸䝉，名實相須，而聖朝興賢勸士之效，足以暴白天下後世，而於歴科前哲益有光矣。先儒志進舉有言：「方其取以辭章，類若浮文而夕實；及其臨㕛設施，奮其事業，隱然爲國名臣者，不可勝數。」玉於是録，亦深有望於群士子云。
天順三年八月穀旦，直隸河間府儒學教授四明邵玉序。
translation_en:
… transformative governance and assist in bringing about Great Peace. In this way, literary talent and moral virtue will be mutually sustained, reputation and reality will correspond to one another, and the effectiveness of our Sacred Dynasty in promoting the worthy and encouraging scholars will suffice to be made manifest to the world and to future generations, adding ever greater luster to the worthy predecessors of past examinations. A former Confucian scholar, in writing an account of the recruitment examinations, once said: "At the moment when candidates are selected by means of their literary compositions, it seems as though there is only ornate writing and little substance [?]; yet when they come to handle practical affairs, institute measures, and exert themselves in their enterprises, those who stand out with quiet dignity as celebrated ministers of the state are too numerous to count." In compiling this record, I, Yu, likewise place this deep hope in all of you scholars.

Written as a preface on an auspicious day in the eighth month of the third year of the Tianshun era (1459) by Shao Yu 邵玉 of Siming 四明, Instructor in the Confucian School of Hejian Prefecture 河間府 in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸).

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第一場
四書
夫子何哂由也曰爲國以禮其言不讓是
故哂之唯求則非邦也與安見方六
七十如五六十而非邦也者唯赤則
非邦也與宗廟會同非諸侯而何赤
也爲之小孰能爲之大
誠者不勉而中不思而得從容中道聖人
也誠之者擇善而固執之者也博學
===
之審問之愼思之明辨之篤行之有
弗學學之弗能弗措也有弗問問之
弗知弗措也有弗思思之弗得弗措
也有弗辨辨之弗明弗措也有弗行
行之弗篤弗措也人一能之己百之
人十能之己千之
鷄鳴而起孳孳爲善者舜之徒也
易
剛上而尚賢能止健大正也不家食吉養
punctuated:
第一場
四書
「夫子何哂由也？」曰：「爲國以禮，其言不讓，是故哂之。」「唯求則非邦也與？」「安見方六七十，如五六十，而非邦也者？」「唯赤則非邦也與？」「宗廟會同，非諸侯而何？赤也爲之小，孰能爲之大？」
誠者，不勉而中，不思而得，從容中道，聖人也。誠之者，擇善而固執之者也。博學之，審問之，愼思之，明辨之，篤行之。有弗學，學之弗能，弗措也；有弗問，問之弗知，弗措也；有弗思，思之弗得，弗措也；有弗辨，辨之弗明，弗措也；有弗行，行之弗篤，弗措也。人一能之，己百之；人十能之，己千之。
鷄鳴而起，孳孳爲善者，舜之徒也。
易
剛上而尚賢，能止健，大正也。「不家食吉」，養
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"Why did you smile at You, Master?" Confucius replied, "A state is governed by ritual propriety, yet his words were lacking in modesty; that is why I smiled at him." "In the case of Qiu, was it not a state that he spoke of?" "Where has one ever seen a territory of sixty or seventy li square, or fifty or sixty li square, that was not a state?" "In the case of Chi, was it not a state that he spoke of?" "Ancestral temple rites and diplomatic meetings—what are these the affairs of if not the feudal lords? If Chi were to play only a minor part in them, who could play a major part?"

One who possesses authenticity hits the mark without effort and apprehends without deliberation, naturally and easily abiding in the Way—such is the sage. One who attains authenticity is he who chooses what is good and holds fast to it. He studies it broadly, inquires into it thoroughly, reflects on it carefully, discerns it clearly, and practices it earnestly. While there is anything he has not studied, or having studied it is not yet able to master it, he does not give up; while there is anything he has not inquired into, or having inquired into it does not yet understand it, he does not give up; while there is anything he has not reflected on, or having reflected on it has not yet grasped it, he does not give up; while there is anything he has not discerned, or having discerned it has not yet made it clear, he does not give up; while there is anything he has not practiced, or having practiced it has not yet done so earnestly, he does not give up. What others can do in one effort, he will do in a hundred; what others can do in ten efforts, he will do in a thousand.

He who rises at cockcrow and tirelessly devotes himself to doing good is a follower of Shun.

Classic of Changes (Yi)

The firm ascends and honors the worthy; being able to check strength is great rectitude. "Not eating at home brings good fortune" means nourishing…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
賢也
上九弗損益之无咎貞吉利有攸往得臣
无家象曰弗損益之大得志也
藉用白茅无咎子曰苟錯諸地而可矣藉
之用茅何咎之有慎之至也夫茅之
為物薄而用可重也慎斯術也以往
其无所失矣勞謙君子有終吉子曰
勞而不伐有功而不德厚之至也語
以其功下人者也德言盛禮言恭謙
===
也者致恭以存其位者也
聖人以此洗心退藏於密吉凶與民同患
神以知來知以藏往
書
禹曰都帝慎乃在位帝曰俞禹曰安汝止
惟幾惟康其弼直惟動丕應徯志以
昭受上帝天其申命用休帝曰吁臣
哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞帝曰臣作
朕股肱耳目
punctuated:
賢也。
上九，弗損益之，无咎，貞吉，利有攸往，得臣无家。象曰：弗損益之，大得志也。
藉用白茅，无咎。子曰：「苟錯諸地而可矣，藉之用茅，何咎之有？慎之至也。夫茅之為物薄，而用可重也。慎斯術也以往，其无所失矣。」勞謙，君子有終，吉。子曰：「勞而不伐，有功而不德，厚之至也。語以其功下人者也。德言盛，禮言恭。謙也者，致恭以存其位者也。」
聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往。

書
禹曰：「都！帝，慎乃在位。」帝曰：「俞。」禹曰：「安汝止，惟幾惟康，其弼直，惟動丕應。徯志以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。」帝曰：「吁！臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」禹曰：「俞。」帝曰：「臣作朕股肱耳目。」
translation_en:
… the worthy.”

Top Nine: Without diminishing, increasing it; no blame. Correctness brings good fortune. It is favorable to have somewhere to go. One obtains subjects without separate families. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: “Without diminishing, increasing it: one greatly achieves one’s aspirations.”

“Spreading white cogon grass beneath it: no blame.” The Master said: “If one merely placed it on the ground, it would do; yet if one spreads cogon grass beneath it, what blame could there be? This is the utmost caution. Now cogon grass as a thing is trifling, yet its use can be weighty. If one goes forward cautiously practicing this art, one will suffer no loss.” “Toiling and yet modest, the superior man has a good end: good fortune.” The Master said: “To toil and not boast, to have merit and not count it a virtue: this is the utmost generosity. It speaks of one who despite his merit places himself below others. Virtue should be abundant; ritual propriety should be reverent. Modesty is exercising reverence so as to preserve one’s position.”

By means of these the sage cleanses his heart and retires into the secret depths, sharing the anxieties of good fortune and misfortune with the common people. Through spirit he knows what is to come; through wisdom he stores up what is past.

Classic of Documents (Shu)

Yu said: “Ah! O Emperor, be cautious on your throne.” The Emperor said: “Yes.” Yu said: “Rest calmly in the point where you should abide. Attend to the subtle springs of things and to peace; let your assistants be upright, and when you move there will be a grand response. When you await their aspirations so as brilliantly to receive the mandate from the Lord on High, Heaven will renew its mandate with blessings.” The Emperor said: “Alas! Ministers! Associates! Associates! Ministers!” Yu said: “Yes.” The Emperor said: “My ministers act as my legs and arms, my ears and eyes.”

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
岷山導江東别為沱又東至于澧過九江
至于東陵東迤北會于匯東為中江
入于海
乃汝盡遜曰時叙惟曰未有遜事
非佞折獄惟良折獄罔非在中察辭于差
非從惟從哀敬折獄明啓刑書胥占
咸庶中正其刑其罰其審克之
詩
既見君子庶幾說懌
===
既醉而出並受其福醉而不出是謂伐德
飲酒孔嘉維其令儀
截彼淮浦王師之所王旅嘽嘽如飛如翰
如江如漢如山之苞如川之流緜緜
翼翼不測不克濯征徐國
秋而載嘗夏而楅衡白牡騂剛犧尊將將
毛炰胾羹籩豆大房萬舞洋洋孝孫
有慶俾爾熾而昌俾爾壽而臧保彼
東方魯邦是常
punctuated:
岷山導江，東别為沱，又東至于澧，過九江，至于東陵，東迤北，會于匯，東為中江，入于海。
乃汝盡遜，曰時叙；惟曰未有遜事。
非佞折獄，惟良折獄，罔非在中。察辭于差，非從惟從。哀敬折獄，明啓刑書胥占，咸庶中正。其刑其罰，其審克之。
詩
既見君子，庶幾說懌。
既醉而出，並受其福；醉而不出，是謂伐德。飲酒孔嘉，維其令儀。
截彼淮浦，王師之所。王旅嘽嘽，如飛如翰，如江如漢，如山之苞，如川之流，緜緜翼翼，不測不克，濯征徐國。
秋而載嘗，夏而楅衡。白牡騂剛，犧尊將將，毛炰胾羹，籩豆大房，萬舞洋洋，孝孫有慶。俾爾熾而昌，俾爾壽而臧，保彼東方，魯邦是常。
translation_en:
From Mount Min (岷山) he guided the Yangzi River (江); eastward it branched off to form the Tuo (沱); farther east it reached the Li (澧), passed the Nine Rivers (九江), and reached Dongling (東陵); slanting northeastward, it joined at the confluence (匯); eastward it became the Middle Yangzi (中江) and entered the sea.
"Wait until your ministers can all yield to one another, and then say these things are in order;only say that there is not yet any yielding in affairs."
"It is not the eloquent who should decide criminal cases, but the virtuous who should decide criminal cases; in everything they keep to the mean. Examine the discrepancies in the testimonies; do not follow your own inclinations, follow only what is right. With compassion and reverence decide criminal cases; clearly open the book of punishments and consult together, so that all may approximate impartiality and correctness. In applying punishments and fines, examine carefully and master them."

Book of Odes (詩經)
"Having seen the lord, perchance his heart is pleased and glad."
"When they are drunk and go out, both host and guests receive the blessing; when they are drunk and do not go out, this is called injuring virtue. Drinking wine is very admirable, only when done with good deportment."
"Well-guarded were those banks of the Huai (淮), the place where the royal army stood. The royal troops were numerous and strong, as if flying, as if on wings, like the Yangzi (江) and like the Han (漢), firm like the base of a mountain, rushing like the current of a river, continuous and orderly, unfathomable and invincible, grandly marching to punish the state of Xu (徐)."
"In autumn we perform the autumnal sacrifice, after in summer binding the crossbars to the horns of the bulls. With white bulls and red ones, the ox-shaped goblets grand and stately, singed pigs, sliced meat, and soups, bamboo and wooden vessels and the great stand, the Wan (萬) dance grandly performed, the filial descendant has blessing. May they make you glorious and prosperous, may they make you long-lived and good, to preserve this eastern region, holding the state of Lu (魯) forever."
