顯揚先祖，所以崇孝也；身比焉，順也；明示後世，教也。
translation_en:
… officer of Chu, an officer of Qin, an officer of Song, an officer of Chen, an officer of Wei, an officer of Zheng, an officer of Qi, an officer of Cao, an officer of Zhu, an officer of Xue, and an officer of Zeng made a covenant at Shu. [2nd year of Duke Cheng] Shusun Bao met with Zhao Wu of Jin, Qu Jian of Chu, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Shi E of Wei, Kong Huan of Chen, Liang Xiao of Zheng, an officer of Xu, and an officer of Cao at Song. [27th year of Duke Xiang] Shusun Bao met with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, an officer of Xu, and an officer of Cao at Guo. [1st year of Duke Zhao] The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin and the Viscount of Wu at Huangchi. [13th year of Duke Ai]
The people of Song and the people of Chu made peace. [15th year of Duke Xuan] The Marquis of Qi sent Guo Zuo to the army. [2nd year of Duke Cheng] Wu attacked us. [8th year of Duke Ai]

Record of Rites (Liji)
The five officers of the Son of Heaven are called the Minister of Education (Situ), the Minister of War (Sima), the Minister of Works (Sikong), the Minister of Royal Clansmen and Officers (Sishi), and the Minister of Justice (Sikou); they preside over the five multitudes.
Therefore, when the former kings instituted the rites, they could neither be made excessive nor made deficient; they simply had to be fitting.
To glorify and extol one's ancestors is the means to exalt filial piety; to associate oneself with this is compliance; to display it clearly to posterity is instruction.

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
席小卿次上卿大夫次小卿士庶子以次
就位於下獻君君舉旅行酬而后獻
卿卿舉旅行酬而后獻大夫大夫舉
旅行酬而后獻士士舉旅行酬而后
獻庶子俎豆牲體薦羞皆有等差所
以明貴賤也
第貳場
論
天下治成
===
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢擢蔡義爲光祿大夫給事中詔
擬唐以宋璟爲刑部尚書西京留守誥
擬宋太宗幸國子監賜直講孫奭五品服
謝表
判語〔五條〕
制書有違
漏使印信
私鑄銅錢
punctuated:
席，小卿次上卿，大夫次小卿，士、庶子以次就位於下。獻君，君舉旅行酬，而后獻卿；卿舉旅行酬，而后獻大夫；大夫舉旅行酬，而后獻士；士舉旅行酬，而后獻庶子。俎豆、牲體、薦羞，皆有等差，所以明貴賤也。

第貳場

論
天下治成。

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕
擬漢擢蔡義爲光祿大夫給事中詔。
擬唐以宋璟爲刑部尚書西京留守誥。
擬宋太宗幸國子監賜直講孫奭五品服謝表。

判語〔五條〕
制書有違。
漏使印信。
私鑄銅錢。
translation_en:
…mat; the Junior Ministers take their places next to the Senior Ministers, the Great Officers next to the Junior Ministers, and the Serviceable Men and Royal Scions take their places in order below. When the cup is presented to the ruler, the ruler initiates the general pledging of toasts, and only after that is a cup presented to the Ministers; the Ministers initiate the general pledging of toasts, and only after that is a cup presented to the Great Officers; the Great Officers initiate the general pledging of toasts, and only after that is a cup presented to the Serviceable Men; the Serviceable Men initiate the general pledging of toasts, and only after that is a cup presented to the Royal Scions. The sacrificial stands and vessels, the portions of the victim, and the offerings and delicacies are all graded by rank, whereby the distinction between noble and base is made clear.

Second Session

Discourse (lun)
"Order is Accomplished Throughout the Realm."

Edict (zhao), Mandate (gao), and Memorial (biao) [Examinees are tested on one of these]
Imitation of a Han edict promoting Cai Yi 蔡義 to Grand Palace Grandee (guanglu dafu) and Palace Censor (jishizhong).
Imitation of a Tang mandate appointing Song Jing 宋璟 as Minister of Justice (xingbu shangshu) and Vicegerent of the Western Capital (xijing liushou).
Imitation of a memorial of thanks on behalf of Lecturer (zhijiang) Sun Shi 孫奭 upon being bestowed fifth-rank vestments when Emperor Taizong of the Song visited the Directorate of Education (guozijian).

Legal Judgments (panyu) [Five items]
Violating an imperial decree.
Omitting to affix an official seal.
Privately minting copper coins.…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
辯明冤枉
冒破物料
第三場
策五道
問欽惟
太祖高皇帝御製大誥三編
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝五倫書皆扶世導民之典也其立
言雖殊要皆納天下於皇極也夫建極
===
以人倫為重且以五倫言之君臣父子
兄弟夫婦朋友五者之名義可得聞歟
或謂有天屬者有人合者又謂天屬有
賴於人合者何所見歟書之所載有謂
人君躬行於上卿大夫表式於下者有
古今家識書為厲風者有田宅財物盡
與其弟者有叩頭謝罪富不易妻者有
即變姓名懷銀往贖其子者之數者可
知其人歟求其有合於三誥二書所紀
punctuated:
辯明冤枉、冒破物料。

第三場

策五道

問：欽惟太祖高皇帝御製《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，宣宗章皇帝《五倫書》，皆扶世導民之典也。其立言雖殊，要皆納天下於皇極也。夫建極以人倫為重，且以五倫言之，君臣、父子、兄弟、夫婦、朋友，五者之名義可得聞歟？或謂有天屬者，有人合者；又謂天屬有賴於人合者，何所見歟？書之所載，有謂人君躬行於上，卿大夫表式於下者；有古今家識書為厲風者；有田宅財物盡與其弟者；有叩頭謝罪，富不易妻者；有即變姓名，懷銀往贖其子者。之數者，可知其人歟？求其有合於三《誥》、二書所紀
translation_en:
…Clarifying Wrongful Accusations; Fraudulent Waste of Materials.

Third Session

Five Policy Questions

Question: We reverently reflect that the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) imperially composed by Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu); the two books Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Examples of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi) by Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor (Taizong); and the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) by Emperor Zhang, the Propagating Ancestor (Xuanzong), are all canons for supporting the world and guiding the people. Although their expressions differ, in essence they all bring the realm into the August Ultimate. Now, establishing the Ultimate takes human relationships as paramount. Speaking specifically of the Five Relationships—ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and friends—may we hear an account of the names and meanings of these five? Some say that among them there are those bound by heaven and those joined by man, and further say that those bound by heaven depend upon those joined by man; on what is this view based? Among the accounts recorded in the Book [of the Five Human Relationships], there is mention of the ruler personally practicing virtue above while high ministers and great officers serve as models below; there is one in which family instructions [?] of ancient and modern times were written onto a screen; there is one who gave all his fields, houses, and property to his younger brother; there is one who knocked his head on the ground to apologize and refused to change his wife when rich; and there is one who immediately changed his surname and given name and carried silver in his bosom to go and ransom his friend's son. For these several cases, can the persons involved be identified? If we seek how they correspond to the words and deeds recorded in the three Pronouncements and the two books…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
言行可指諸言與諸士子於
聖教涣汗服膺有素請詳陳之以驗貫通之學
問風俗美惡厚薄古今不同而世道之盛
衰關焉三代以前上無異政下無
異尚異情風俗之美且厚非後世所能
及果何道以致之歟周衰嬴秦并六國
以有天下惟貴變詐峻刻風俗嘗趨於
薄矣漢肇興七制之君豈無有能變
而歸於厚者乎武帝好大喜功窮兵黷
===
武風俗嘗趨於虛矣繼世之君豈無有
能變而歸於實者乎魏晉以來稍慕通
達輕滅禮法風俗又趨於浮矣李唐啓
祚三宗之主亦有能變而歸於醇者乎
以至五季之衰也汴宋太祖應期受禪
奄有寰宇一變而正夷俗其視漢唐二
世風俗爲何如胡元之亡也我
朝
太祖高皇帝應天順人統有天下一變而復□□
punctuated:
言行，可指諸言與？諸士子於聖教涣汗，服膺有素，請詳陳之，以驗貫通之學。

問：風俗美惡厚薄，古今不同，而世道之盛衰關焉。三代以前，上無異政，下無異尚、異情，風俗之美且厚，非後世所能及，果何道以致之歟？周衰，嬴秦并六國以有天下，惟貴變詐峻刻，風俗嘗趨於薄矣。漢肇興，七制之君豈無有能變而歸於厚者乎？武帝好大喜功，窮兵黷武，風俗嘗趨於虛矣；繼世之君豈無有能變而歸於實者乎？魏晉以來，稍慕通達，輕滅禮法，風俗又趨於浮矣。李唐啓祚，三宗之主亦有能變而歸於醇者乎？以至五季之衰也，汴宋太祖應期受禪，奄有寰宇，一變而正夷俗，其視漢、唐二世風俗爲何如？胡元之亡也，我朝太祖高皇帝應天順人，統有天下，一變而復□□
translation_en:
… words and deeds—can these be pointed out and discussed? You scholars have long taken to heart the imperial teachings proclaimed abroad; please set them forth in detail so that we may test your comprehensive learning.

Question: The beauty or ugliness, richness or meagerness of customs and mores have differed between antiquity and the present, and the flourishing or decline of the way of the world hinges upon them. Before the Three Dynasties, those above had no divergent policies, and those below had no divergent preferences or sentiments; the beauty and richness of their customs could not be matched by later ages. By what way indeed was this brought about? When the Zhou declined, the Ying clan of Qin annexed the six states to possess All under Heaven, valuing only deceit and harshness, and customs once tended toward meagerness. When the Han first rose, among the sovereigns of the seven reigns of institutional founders, was there none able to transform customs and return them to richness? Emperor Wu loved grandeur and delighted in exploits, exhausting his troops and abusing military force, and customs once tended toward hollowness; among the sovereigns who succeeded him, was there none able to transform them and return them to substance? From the Wei and Jin onward, people increasingly admired uninhibitedness and slighted or cast aside ritual and law, so that customs again tended toward frivolity. When the Li clan of Tang inaugurated its imperial line, among the rulers of the Three Ancestors, was there also one able to transform customs and return them to purity? Down to the decline of the Five Dynasties, Taizu of the Bian Song responded to the appointed time, received the abdication, and came to possess the entire realm, transforming and rectifying barbarian customs at a stroke; how did this compare with the customs of the two ages of Han and Tang? With the fall of the barbarian Yuan, Emperor Gao, Taizu of our Dynasty, responded to Heaven and accorded with men to unify and possess All under Heaven, transforming them at a stroke and restoring [□□] …

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
風其視唐虞三代風俗為何若諸子積
學有年襟懷鼎盛來宜有知其說者
願著于篇
問大學中庸聖賢傳心之閫奧也大學經
首言三綱領而申以止至善何不及明
德新民歟次言八條目而詳夫明德新
民何不及止至善歟傳釋綱領而外有
本末章何歟釋條目皆以兩事指序獨
誠意自為一章又何歟格物致知章亡
===
矣朱子取程子之意補之何不效曾子
作傳之體歟中庸首言性道教繼獨言
道何不及性教歟二十一章獨言性教
何不言道歟且兩言性教亦有分別歟
名篇之義首不之及而以性道教言之
何歟第十一章既曰此篇大旨以知仁
勇為入道之門至二十章又曰誠者實
此篇之樞紐何歟首章所謂一篇之體
要末章又謂舉一篇之要而約言之果
punctuated:
風，其視唐、虞、三代風俗為何若？諸子積學有年，襟懷鼎盛，來宜有知其說者，願著于篇。

問：《大學》、《中庸》，聖賢傳心之閫奧也。《大學》經首言三綱領，而申以止至善，何不及明德、新民歟？次言八條目，而詳夫明德、新民，何不及止至善歟？傳釋綱領而外有本末章，何歟？釋條目皆以兩事指序，獨誠意自為一章，又何歟？格物致知章亡矣，朱子取程子之意補之，何不效曾子作傳之體歟？《中庸》首言性、道、教，繼獨言道，何不及性、教歟？二十一章獨言性、教，何不言道歟？且兩言性、教，亦有分別歟？名篇之義，首不之及，而以性、道、教言之，何歟？第十一章既曰此篇大旨以知、仁、勇為入道之門，至二十章又曰誠者實此篇之樞紐，何歟？首章所謂「一篇之體要」，末章又謂「舉一篇之要而約言之」，果…
translation_en:
…customs—how does that compare with the customs of the eras of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties? You gentlemen have accumulated learning for many years, and the aspirations in your breasts are at their prime; coming here, there must be those among you who know the explanation of these matters, so I wish you to set them forth in your essays.

Question: The Great Learning (Daxue) and the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) are the inner sanctum of the sages' and worthies' transmission of the mind. In the Great Learning, the Classic text (jing) first states the Three Guiding Principles (san gangling) and elaborates on "resting in the highest good" (zhi zhishan); why does it not touch upon "manifesting luminous virtue" (mingde) and "renewing the people" (xinmin)? Next it states the Eight Steps (ba tiaomu) and gives details regarding manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people; why does it not touch upon resting in the highest good? Outside of explaining the Guiding Principles, why do the Commentaries (zhuan) have a chapter on the root and branches (benmo)? In explaining the Steps, each links two matters in sequence; why again does "making the thoughts sincere" (chengyi) alone form a chapter by itself? The chapter on "investigating things and extending knowledge" (gewu zhizhi) was lost; when Master Zhu [Xi] took the meaning of the Masters Cheng to supplement it, why did he not imitate the style in which Master Zeng composed the Commentaries? The Doctrine of the Mean begins by speaking of nature (xing), the Way (dao), and instruction (jiao), and then continues by speaking solely of the Way; why does it not touch upon nature and instruction? The twenty-first chapter speaks solely of nature and instruction; why does it not speak of the Way? Moreover, in speaking twice of nature and instruction, is there also a distinction between them? Why is the meaning of the title of the treatise not mentioned at the beginning, which instead speaks of nature, the Way, and instruction? Under the eleventh chapter [in the commentary] it is already said that the main purport of this treatise takes wisdom (zhi), humanity (ren), and courage (yong) as the gateway for entering the Way, yet at the twentieth chapter it says again that sincerity (cheng) is in fact the pivot of this treatise—why is this? What the commentary on the first chapter calls "the essential substance of the whole treatise," and what the commentary on the final chapter calls "taking up the essentials of the whole treatise and summarizing them"—what indeed…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
何所指歟學庸二書學者所當講其究
指歸以對
問大哉宣聖道該穹壤學貫古今固非後
人敢妄議也姑以其所可疑者言之禱
祈尼山事若異也何適應其生夢奠兩
楹事若幻也何即知其没道宗堯舜修
所行之法守文武何所施之相事初攝
將焉誅之政化甫成將焉誦之軍旅之
事未之學何以拒却萊兵雖有其德而
===
無位何以正定禮樂道大德宏胡不貸
少正卯之誅過化存神胡不免宋桓魋
之傷疏食水飲困已極矣焉得樂在其
中絶粮七日病亦甚矣奚暇絃歌不衰
四十九衰超於衆何肖似夫楊虎盛德
光輝接於人何見毁於州仇賢於堯舜
何其高竊比老彭何其下尼溪之封齊
景當矣奚不可於晏嬰國政與聞魯大
治矣奚輙沮於桓子席不暇暖似乎汲
punctuated:
何所指歟？《學》、《庸》二書，學者所當講，其究指歸以對。

問：大哉宣聖！道該穹壤，學貫古今，固非後人敢妄議也。姑以其所可疑者言之：禱祈尼山，事若異也，何適應其生？夢奠兩楹，事若幻也，何即知其没？道宗堯、舜，修所行之；法守文、武，何所施之？相事初攝，將焉誅之？政化甫成，將焉誦之？軍旅之事未之學，何以拒却萊兵？雖有其德而無位，何以正定禮樂？道大德宏，胡不貸少正卯之誅？過化存神，胡不免宋桓魋之傷？疏食水飲，困已極矣，焉得樂在其中？絶粮七日，病亦甚矣，奚暇絃歌不衰？四十九衰超於衆，何肖似夫楊虎？盛德光輝接於人，何見毁於州仇？賢於堯、舜，何其高？竊比老彭，何其下？尼溪之封，齊景當矣，奚不可於晏嬰？國政與聞，魯大治矣，奚輙沮於桓子？席不暇暖，似乎汲…
translation_en:
…to what do they actually refer? The two books, the Great Learning (Daxue) and the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), are works that scholars ought to study thoroughly; investigate their ultimate aims and present your reply.

Question: Great indeed was the Exalted Sage [Confucius]! His Way encompasses heaven and earth, and his learning penetrates antiquity and the present; truly it is not something later generations dare to rashly dispute. Yet let us speak tentatively of those points that may raise doubts: The prayer at Mount Ni seems like a strange affair—how did it happen to correspond with his birth? Dreaming of funerary offerings between the two pillars seems illusory—how did he thereby immediately know of his own approaching death? He took Yao and Shun as the ancestors of his Way—how did he cultivate and practice it [?]? He upheld the laws of Kings Wen and Wu—where did he put them into effect? When he first acted as chief minister, whom was he going to execute? When his political transformation had barely been achieved, how was he already praised in song? He said he had never studied military affairs—how then did he repel the troops of Lai? Although he possessed virtue without holding a ruler's position—by what authority did he rectify and fix the rites and music? Since his Way was great and his virtue vast, why did he not pardon Shaozheng Mao from execution? Since wherever he passed he transformed people and wherever he abided his spirit worked wonders, why did he not escape harm from Huan Tui of Song? With coarse rice to eat and water to drink, his privation had reached the extreme—how could he find joy in the midst of it? Deprived of provisions for seven days, his distress was severe indeed—how did he have the leisure to play the stringed instruments and sing without flagging? His forty-nine remarkable physical features [?] surpassed those of the multitude—why did he resemble Yang Hu? The splendid brilliance of his flourishing virtue touched all who met him—why was he slandered by Shusun Wuji (Zhouqiu)? To be called worthier than Yao and Shun—how lofty is that! To secretly compare himself to Lao Peng—how humble is that! As for the enfeoffment at Nixi, Duke Jing of Qi acted appropriately—why was it deemed unacceptable by Yan Ying? When he participated in hearing the governance of the state, Lu achieved great order—why was he so readily thwarted by季 Huanzi? His mat never had time to get warm, which makes it seem as though he were anxiously…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
汲求進行不脫晃似未從容也道觀於
鄉飲何以知王道之易易射於矍相何
以致觀者之堵存過庭訓子以詩禮豈
餘事皆非所可學與回若天之喪已豈
餘子皆非所可傳穎悟篤實俱爲美質
何所喻有損益之殊剛勇柔懦俱爲失
中何所咨有進退之異諸君子遊學聖
門沾沐餘化其於前言往行宜必耳熟
心醉而有得也幸無靳而不與之言
===
問守法者人臣之大節持正者君子之雅
操士有不知此而可以爲士乎稽之史
傳盜逃詔旨而不重犯蹕之罰當哮人
言而不輕受贓之典之二子皆任廷尉
而其議論爲孰優選人詐冒則奏以據
法應流郎將坐誤則奏以犯不至死之
二子皆任大理而其功業爲孰盛守穎
川而郡中清靜刺冀州而境內肅然以
何爲而致是穀遷洛陽令外戚斂手爲
punctuated:
汲求進；行不脫晃，似未從容也道。觀於鄉飲，何以知王道之易易？射於矍相，何以致觀者之堵存？過庭訓子以《詩》、《禮》，豈餘事皆非所可學？與回若天之喪已，豈餘子皆非所可傳？穎悟、篤實俱爲美質，何所喻有損益之殊？剛勇、柔懦俱爲失中，何所咨有進退之異？諸君子遊學聖門，沾沐餘化，其於前言往行，宜必耳熟心醉而有得也，幸無靳而不與之言。

問：守法者，人臣之大節；持正者，君子之雅操。士有不知此，而可以爲士乎？稽之史傳：盜逃詔旨，而不重犯蹕之罰；當哮人言，而不輕受贓之典。之二子皆任廷尉，而其議論爲孰優？選人詐冒，則奏以據法應流；郎將坐誤，則奏以犯不至死。之二子皆任大理，而其功業爲孰盛？守穎川而郡中清靜，刺冀州而境內肅然，以何爲而致是穀？遷洛陽令，外戚斂手；爲
translation_en:
…eagerly seeking advancement; and departing without taking off his ceremonial cap [?晃 for 冕] seems as though he did not proceed leisurely along the Way [?也道 for 中道]. Watching the district symposium, how did he know that the Kingly Way is so easy? Shooting arrows at Juexiang, how did he cause the spectators to stand like a wall? When his son passed through the courtyard, he instructed him in the Odes (Shi) and the Rites (Li)—could it be that all other matters were unworthy of study? Toward Yan Hui, he mourned as if Heaven were destroying him—could it be that none of the other disciples were worthy of transmitting his teachings? Quick comprehension and steadfast sincerity are both fine qualities—by what analogy did he distinguish between diminishing and increasing them? Brash courage and timid weakness both miss the Mean—upon what inquiry did he differentiate between urging forward and holding back? You gentlemen have studied in the school of the Sage and been bathed in his lingering transformative influence. Regarding the words and deeds of antiquity, your ears must be familiar and your hearts entranced, having gained true insight into them. Pray do not be stingy and withhold your words.

Question: Upholding the law is the great integrity of a minister; maintaining rectitude is the noble principle of a gentleman. Can a scholar who does not know this be considered a true scholar? Examining the historical records: one [Zhang Shizhi 張釋之] defied an imperial decree [?盜逃詔旨] and refused to stiffen the penalty for violating the imperial cortege; another [Yu Dingguo 于定國] countered the clamor of accusers [?當哮人言] and did not lightly apply the statutes on bribery. Both of these men served as Chamberlain for Law Enforcement (tingwei), yet whose deliberations were superior? When candidates for office committed fraud and impersonation, one [Dai Zhou 戴胄] memorialized that according to the law they should be exiled; when a Commandant of Attendants (langjiang) was implicated for an error, another [Tang Lin 唐臨 / Xu Yougong 徐有功] memorialized that his offense did not warrant death. Both of these men served as Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review (dali), yet whose achievements were more flourishing? One governed Yingchuan Commandery and the district became pure and tranquil; another served as Regional Inspector of Jizhou and the territory became reverently orderly—by what actions did they bring this about [?穀 for 歟]? One was promoted to Magistrate of Luoyang and the imperial consort clan restrained their hands; another served as…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
京兆尹豪右斂跡行何政而致然歟以
至執法一心不敢惜死南山可移判不
可搖守法若此其人可得而悉指歟若
夫鄭國有火不納禆竈之說漢儲欲廢
不憚廷爭之強是皆位列大夫而稱遺
愛者誰歟鳴玉殿省不爲伶人之事須
詔開門以防不逞之徒是皆位居侍中
而著死節者誰歟任郎中而受却坐之
賞侯東門而膺却輦之襃何所見而致
===
歟忠臣不私私臣不忠臣職載筆君舉
必書何所激而言歟以至遇事謇謇無
所顧憚指切時事無所回避持正若此
其人可得而悉數歟諸士子尚友於千
載究之熟矣請筆以對毋徒誦諸載籍
可考
punctuated: 京兆尹，豪右斂跡，行何政而致然歟？以至執法一心，不敢惜死，南山可移，判不可搖，守法若此，其人可得而悉指歟？若夫鄭國有火，不納禆竈之說；漢儲欲廢，不憚廷爭之強。是皆位列大夫，而稱遺愛者誰歟？鳴玉殿省，不爲伶人之事；須詔開門，以防不逞之徒。是皆位居侍中，而著死節者誰歟？任郎中而受却坐之賞，侯東門而膺却輦之襃，何所見而致歟？「忠臣不私，私臣不忠」，「臣職載筆，君舉必書」，何所激而言歟？以至遇事謇謇，無所顧憚，指切時事，無所回避，持正若此，其人可得而悉數歟？諸士子尚友於千載，究之熟矣，請筆以對，毋徒誦諸載籍可考。
translation_en:
… became Governor of the Capital (Jingzhao Yin), the powerful and privileged families curbed their tracks—what policies were practiced to bring this about? And furthermore, those who upheld the law with a single mind and did not dare to begrudge death, and those who declared that the Southern Mountains might be moved, yet a legal judgment could not be shaken—when it comes to upholding the law like this, can those men all be specifically pointed out?

Now as for the one who, when the state of Zheng suffered fires, refused to accept the advice of Pi Zao, and the one who, when the Han heir apparent was about to be deposed, did not shrink from fierce contention at court—both of these ranked as Grand Masters (dafu), yet which of them was praised for leaving behind a legacy of benevolent affection? As for the one who wore tinkling jades in the palace ministries and refused to perform the business of actors, and the one who insisted on waiting for an imperial edict to open the city gates so as to guard against lawless malcontents—both of these held the post of Palace Attendant (shizhong), yet which of them became renowned for dying in loyalty? As for the one who served as Attendant Gentleman (langzhong) and received a reward for declining to sit with a consort, and the one who waited at the eastern gate and won praise for turning back the imperial hand-carriage—what insight led them to bring this about? As for the sayings, "A loyal minister has no private partiality; a minister with private partiality is not loyal," and "Your servant's duty is to wield the brush; every move of the ruler must be recorded"—what stirred them to speak thus? And furthermore, those who were outspoken and forthright when encountering affairs, without regard or fear, and who pointedly criticized current events without any evasion—when it comes to maintaining rectitude like this, can those men all be enumerated?

You gentlemen have befriended the ancients across a thousand years and have investigated these matters thoroughly. Please take up your brushes to reply, and do not merely say that they can be examined in the historical records.
