title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
四書
夫子何哂由也曰爲國以禮其言不讓是故哂
之唯求則非邦也與安見方六七十如五六十
而非邦也者唯赤則非邦也與宗廟會同非諸
侯而何赤也爲之小孰能爲之大
李斌
同考試官學正林　批〔此題問答有三諸作皆無發越獨此卷發明詳盡辭理簡當可式〕
〔中之錚錚者髙薦何忝〕
===
考試官教諭翁　批〔聖賢問答之意盡於言表非他卷所及〕
考試官教授鄧　批〔此篇文辭優柔不迫寫出孔門師弟子問答之意居然可見非涵養於聖賢者不能也〕
賢者以同列見哂爲問聖人荅之有其致賢者以同
列言志爲疑聖人荅之無所貶蓋三子之志皆欲得
國而治者也賢者因仲由見哂而不及求赤故屢致
其問聖人安得不明言以告之哉昔者曾晳子路冉
有公西華各言已志聖人獨哂仲由故曾晳疑而問
punctuated:
四書

「夫子何哂由也？」曰：「爲國以禮，其言不讓，是故哂之。」「唯求則非邦也與？」「安見方六七十，如五六十，而非邦也者？」「唯赤則非邦也與？」「宗廟會同，非諸侯而何？赤也爲之小，孰能爲之大？」

李斌

同考試官學正林　批〔此題問答有三，諸作皆無發越，獨此卷發明詳盡，辭理簡當，可式。〕〔中之錚錚者，髙薦何忝？〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔聖賢問答之意，盡於言表，非他卷所及。〕
考試官教授鄧　批〔此篇文辭優柔不迫，寫出孔門師弟子問答之意，居然可見，非涵養於聖賢者不能也。〕

賢者以同列見哂爲問，聖人荅之有其致；賢者以同列言志爲疑，聖人荅之無所貶。蓋三子之志，皆欲得國而治者也。賢者因仲由見哂而不及求、赤，故屢致其問，聖人安得不明言以告之哉？昔者曾晳、子路、冉有、公西華各言已志，聖人獨哂仲由，故曾晳疑而問…
translation_en:
Four Books

["The Master asked,] 'Master, why did you smile at You [Zilu]?' He replied, 'A state is governed by ritual propriety, yet his words lacked modesty; that is why I smiled at him.' 'Could it be that what Qiu [Ran You] spoke of is not a state?' 'Where has one ever seen a territory of sixty or seventy li square, or fifty or sixty, that is not a state?' 'Could it be that what Chi [Gongxi Hua] spoke of is not a state?' 'Ancestral temples and diplomatic assemblies—what are these the affairs of if not the feudal lords? If Chi were to play only a minor part in them, who could play a major one?'" [Analects 11.26]

Li Bin 李斌

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Lin comments: [This topic contains three exchanges of questions and answers. None of the other compositions achieved any real breakthrough, whereas this paper alone elucidates the meaning thoroughly, with concise and fitting diction and reasoning; it may serve as a model.] [An outstanding piece among those selected—how could a high recommendation be undeserved?]
Examiner and County Instructor (jiaoyu) Weng comments: [The intent of the questions and answers between the Sage and the worthy is fully brought out beyond the literal words; it is something the other papers do not reach.]
Examiner and Prefectural Instructor (jiaoshou) Deng comments: [The phrasing of this essay is gentle and unhurried, depicting the spirit of the dialogue between Master and disciple in the Confucian school so vividly that it can be clearly seen; none who had not cultivated themselves in the teachings of the sages and worthies could have written it.]

The worthy [Zeng Xi] asked why his fellow disciple was smiled at, and the Sage answered him by giving the reason; the worthy then expressed doubt about the ambitions stated by his other fellow disciples, and the Sage answered him without any disparagement of them. For the ambitions of all three disciples were alike aimed at obtaining a state and governing it. Because Zhong You [Zilu] was smiled at while [Ran] Qiu and [Gongxi] Chi were not, the worthy repeatedly posed his questions—how could the Sage not speak plainly to inform him? In former times, when Zeng Xi, Zilu, Ran You, and Gongxi Hua each stated his own ambition, the Sage smiled at Zhong You alone; therefore Zeng Xi felt doubt and asked…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之若曰爲國治民之事由也所優爲矣夫子果何爲
而哂之乎化民向義之事亦由也所優爲矣夫子又
何爲而哂之乎夫子告以爲國之道以禮遜爲本今
由也言之無所退遜此吾所以哂也治國之要以禮
讓爲先由也言之無所謙讓此吾所以哂也然曾晳
既聞仲由之事矣其意以爲求之言志非爲邦之謂
歟夫子以冉求所言方六七十國之小者也如五六
十國之又小者也求雖退遜而以近小之國自居安
見小國而非爲邦之事乎曾晳既聞冉求之志矣又
===
以爲赤之言志非爲邦之謂歟夫子以赤所言宗廟
祭祀此諸侯之事也朝見會同亦諸侯之事也赤雖
謙讓而以擯相之末自任然在人又孰能有出其右
者哉此夫子於求赤之志答無貶詞蓋亦許之也吁
仲由冉求公西赤之志皆欲得國而治以事功言也
若曾晳之志則欲即其所居之位樂其日用之常與
物各得其所以理趣言也然事功固不若理趣之高
理趣又不若事功之實觀此則四子之優劣可見矣
學者知之
punctuated: 之，若曰：爲國治民之事，由也所優爲矣，夫子果何爲而哂之乎？化民向義之事，亦由也所優爲矣，夫子又何爲而哂之乎？夫子告以爲國之道，以禮遜爲本，今由也言之無所退遜，此吾所以哂也；治國之要，以禮讓爲先，由也言之無所謙讓，此吾所以哂也。然曾晳既聞仲由之事矣，其意以爲求之言志，非爲邦之謂歟？夫子以冉求所言，方六七十，國之小者也；如五六十，國之又小者也。求雖退遜，而以近小之國自居，安見小國而非爲邦之事乎？曾晳既聞冉求之志矣，又以爲赤之言志，非爲邦之謂歟？夫子以赤所言，宗廟祭祀，此諸侯之事也；朝見會同，亦諸侯之事也。赤雖謙讓，而以擯相之末自任，然在人又孰能有出其右者哉？此夫子於求、赤之志，答無貶詞，蓋亦許之也。吁！仲由、冉求、公西赤之志，皆欲得國而治，以事功言也；若曾晳之志，則欲即其所居之位，樂其日用之常，與物各得其所，以理趣言也。然事功固不若理趣之高，理趣又不若事功之實。觀此則四子之優劣可見矣，學者知之。
translation_en: … him, as if to say: "Administering a state and governing the people are things that You [Zhong You 仲由, i.e., Zilu 子路] is more than capable of doing; why then did you, Master, smile at him? Transforming the people and directing them toward righteousness are also things that You is more than capable of doing; why again did you, Master, smile at him?" The Master told him that the Way of administering a state takes ritual deference as its foundation, and since You spoke without any modesty or deference, that was why he smiled; and that the essential point in governing a state puts ritual yielding first, and since You spoke without any humility or yielding, that was why he smiled. Yet once Zeng Xi 曾晳 had heard about the matter of Zhong You, his thought was: "In stating his ambition, was Qiu [Ran Qiu 冉求] not speaking of administering a state?" The Master replied that what Ran Qiu spoke of—a territory of sixty or seventy li square—is a small state, and one of fifty or sixty li square is an even smaller state. Although Qiu was deferential and content to place himself in charge of a small state, how could one see a small state as not being a matter of administering a state? Once Zeng Xi had heard about the ambition of Ran Qiu, he further thought: "In stating his ambition, was Chi [Gongxi Chi 公西赤] not speaking of administering a state?" The Master replied that what Chi spoke of—ancestral temples and sacrifices—are the affairs of feudal lords, and audiences and diplomatic gatherings are likewise the affairs of feudal lords. Although Chi was humble and yielding, taking upon himself only the minor role of a ceremonial assistant, among other men who could possibly surpass him? Thus, in replying about the ambitions of Qiu and Chi, the Master used no words of disparagement, for he indeed approved of them as well. Ah! The ambitions of Zhong You, Ran Qiu, and Gongxi Chi all lay in wishing to obtain a state and govern it, speaking in terms of practical achievements. As for the ambition of Zeng Xi, he wished to remain in the station he occupied, taking joy in the ordinary affairs of daily life, with all things each finding their proper place, speaking in terms of the flavor of moral principle. Yet while practical achievements are certainly not as lofty as the flavor of moral principle, the flavor of moral principle is in turn not as substantial as practical achievements. Observing this, the relative merits of the four disciples can be seen; let scholars take note of it.

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
誠者不勉而中不思而得從容中道聖人也誠
之者擇善而固執之者也博學之審問之愼思
之明辨之篤行之有弗學學之弗能弗措也有
弗問問之弗知弗措也有弗思思之弗得弗措
也有弗辨辨之弗明弗措也有弗行行之弗篤
弗措也人一能之己百之人十能之己千之
謝諒
同考試官學正鄭　批〔此題當以生知安行學知利行困知勉行爲三節場中作者往往得此失彼惟此作敘理明白遣詞簡當〕
===
考試官教諭翁　批〔中庸作此講究明白必熟於性理之學者〕
考試官教授邵　批〔此題三節頭緒頗多而能約而爲文理意俱到非有學之士不能也〕
全夫實德者知行有自然之妙欲實其德者知行加
勉然之功夫聖人之德無不實故知行皆出於自然
也則夫賢人以下欲實其德者可不勉焉以盡知行
punctuated:
「誠者，不勉而中，不思而得，從容中道，聖人也。誠之者，擇善而固執之者也。博學之，審問之，愼思之，明辨之，篤行之。有弗學，學之弗能，弗措也；有弗問，問之弗知，弗措也；有弗思，思之弗得，弗措也；有弗辨，辨之弗明，弗措也；有弗行，行之弗篤，弗措也。人一能之，己百之；人十能之，己千之。」
謝諒
同考試官學正鄭　批〔此題當以生知安行、學知利行、困知勉行爲三節，場中作者往往得此失彼，惟此作敘理明白，遣詞簡當。〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔《中庸》作此，講究明白，必熟於性理之學者。〕
考試官教授邵　批〔此題三節，頭緒頗多，而能約而爲文，理意俱到，非有學之士不能也。〕
全夫實德者，知行有自然之妙；欲實其德者，知行加勉然之功。夫聖人之德無不實，故知行皆出於自然也。則夫賢人以下欲實其德者，可不勉焉以盡知行
translation_en:
"Authenticity is hitting the mark without effort, apprehending without thought, and naturally and easily embodying the Way—this is the sage. Attaining authenticity is choosing what is good and holding fast to it. Study it extensively, inquire into it accurately, think over it carefully, sift it clearly, and practice it earnestly. While there is anything not studied, or while in what one has studied one is not yet capable, do not give up. While there is anything not inquired into, or while in what one has inquired into one does not yet know, do not give up. While there is anything not thought over, or while in what one has thought over one has not yet apprehended it, do not give up. While there is anything not sifted, or while in what one has sifted it is not yet clear, do not give up. While there is anything not practiced, or while in what one has practiced one is not yet earnest, do not give up. If another man succeeds by one effort, oneself will use a hundred efforts. If another man succeeds by ten efforts, oneself will use a thousand."

Xie Liang 謝諒

Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Zheng comments: [This topic should be divided into three sections corresponding to knowing by birth and practicing with ease, knowing through study and practicing for advantage, and knowing after painful feeling of ignorance and practicing with strenuous effort. Writers in the examination hall often grasp one aspect while losing sight of another; only this essay expounds the principles clearly and employs phrasing that is concise and fitting.]

Examiner, District Instructor (jiaoyu) Weng comments: [Composing an essay on the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) like this, with such clear investigation and elucidation, must be the work of a scholar thoroughly versed in the learning of human nature and principle.]

Examiner, Prefectural Instructor (jiaoshou) Shao comments: [The three sections of this topic have rather numerous threads, yet the author is able to synthesize them concisely into an essay where both principle and meaning are fully realized. None but a scholar of true learning could achieve this.]

He who wholly possesses real virtue has a natural wondrousness in his knowledge and action; he who desires to make his virtue real applies the effort of strenuous exertion to his knowledge and action. Now, the virtue of the sage is never unreal, and therefore his knowledge and action both issue from what is natural. As for those from the worthies on down who desire to make their virtue real, how can they not exert themselves to exhaust the…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之功哉且夫誠者真實無妄之謂聖人之德渾然實
理其行安行不待勉强而後中其知生知不待思慮
而後得無所矯揉從容中道此生知安行聖人之德
也若夫誠之者未至於聖而其爲德不能皆實故未
能不思而得則必擇善而後可以明善未能不勉而
中則必固執而後可以誠身然誠之之事必有其目
是故博學審問而取於人者詳愼思明辨而求於心
者精所以擇善而爲知由是而加篤行之功使學問
之所得者踐其實思辨之所得者體諸身所以固執
===
而爲仁此學知利行賢人之學也然知以知之仁以
體之使非勇以强之又何以要其成哉故弗學弗問
則已學之不能問之不知弗措也弗思弗辨則已思
之不得辨之不明弗措也以至弗行則已行而不篤
又豈可止乎故他人以一而能之我則倍之以百而
必底于成人以十而能之我則倍之以千而必造其
極此困而知勉而行勇之事也子思子引孔子之論
誠其所以發明知仁勇之事無餘藴矣嗟夫人性無
不善而氣稟有不同故以其等言之雖有生知學知
punctuated: 之功哉？且夫「誠」者，真實無妄之謂。聖人之德，渾然實理：其行安行，不待勉强而後中；其知生知，不待思慮而後得。無所矯揉，從容中道，此生知安行，聖人之德也。若夫「誠之」者，未至於聖，而其爲德不能皆實。故未能不思而得，則必擇善而後可以明善；未能不勉而中，則必固執而後可以誠身。然誠之之事，必有其目。是故博學、審問，而取於人者詳；愼思、明辨，而求於心者精，所以擇善而爲知。由是而加篤行之功，使學、問之所得者踐其實，思、辨之所得者體諸身，所以固執而爲仁。此學知利行，賢人之學也。然知以知之，仁以體之，使非勇以强之，又何以要其成哉？故弗學、弗問則已，學之不能、問之不知，弗措也；弗思、弗辨則已，思之不得、辨之不明，弗措也；以至弗行則已，行而不篤，又豈可止乎？故他人以一而能之，我則倍之以百，而必底于成；人以十而能之，我則倍之以千，而必造其極。此困而知、勉而行，勇之事也。子思子引孔子之論誠，其所以發明知、仁、勇之事，無餘藴矣。嗟夫！人性無不善，而氣稟有不同。故以其等言之，雖有生知、學知、
translation_en:
…the effort of [knowledge and action]?

Moreover, "authenticity" (cheng) means being true, real, and free from falsehood. The virtue of the sage is wholly real principle: his action is practiced with ease, hitting the mark without waiting upon forced effort; his knowledge is born within him, grasping the truth without waiting upon deliberation. Without any artificial contrivance, he leisurely and naturally hits the Way—this is knowing by birth and practicing with ease, the virtue of the sage.

As for "attaining authenticity," one has not yet reached sagehood, and one's virtue cannot be entirely real. Therefore, being unable to grasp the truth without thinking, one must choose what is good before one can understand the good; being unable to hit the mark without effort, one must hold fast to it before one can make one's person authentic. Yet the work of attaining authenticity must have its specific steps. Therefore, through studying extensively and inquiring accurately, what one takes from others is thorough; through thinking carefully and sifting clearly, what one seeks within one's own mind is refined—this is how one chooses the good and achieves wisdom. From this, one adds the effort of earnest practice, causing what has been gained through study and inquiry to be fulfilled in reality, and what has been gained through thought and sifting to be embodied in one's own person—this is how one holds fast and achieves humanity. This is knowing through learning and practicing for its benefit, the learning of the worthy.

Yet while wisdom is wherewith one knows it, and humanity is wherewith one embodies it, if there is not courage wherewith to press it forward, how could one ensure its completion? Thus, if one does not study or inquire, so be it; but if one studies it and still cannot do it, or inquires of it and still does not understand it, one does not give up. If one does not think or sift, so be it; but if one thinks of it and still does not grasp it, or sifts it and still is not clear about it, one does not give up. Coming down to action: if one does not practice it, so be it; but if one practices it and is not earnest, how could one ever stop? Therefore, what others are able to do with one effort, I will multiply by a hundred, and will certainly carry it through to completion; what others are able to do with ten efforts, I will multiply by a thousand, and will certainly reach the utmost limit. This is knowing through hard toil and practicing through forced effort, the work of courage.

Master Zisi 子思子 cited Confucius's discourse on authenticity, and thereby elucidated the work of wisdom, humanity, and courage with nothing left unexpressed. Alas! Human nature is never not good, yet the endowments of vital force (qibing) differ. Therefore, speaking in terms of their grades, although there are the distinctions between knowing by birth, knowing through learning,…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
困知之殊安行利行勉行之異然能自強不息則由
勉然而馴至於自然矣孰謂誠者聖人終不可以學
而至哉故先儒有曰所入之途雖異所至之域則同
雞鳴而起孳孳爲善者舜之徒也
姚駿
同考試官訓導許　批〔此題本平易但塲中作者或主未接物或主已接物間有兼動靜說者紛紛不決殊失本旨惟此篇專主勤於爲善深得孟子本意且措辭簡當可取可取〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔辭理簡切初學得之可以起人爲善之心宜中優選〕
考試官教授邵　批〔發明孟子之意透徹無遺讀〕
===
能夙興而勉於善者斯亦聖人之徒也蓋樂於爲善
莫舜若也人能夙興而勉於善又豈非舜之徒也哉
宜乎孟子言之以勉人也且夫善者天下之公理人
心所固有不以聖人而豐不以衆人而嗇但汨於物
欲而失之尔今有人焉雞鳴之時惕然而起而能孳
孳焉於性分之所固有者爲之不敢有毫髮之少怠
punctuated:
困知之殊，安行、利行、勉行之異，然能自強不息，則由勉然而馴至於自然矣。孰謂誠者聖人，終不可以學而至哉？故先儒有曰：「所入之途雖異，所至之域則同。」

「雞鳴而起，孳孳爲善者，舜之徒也。」
姚駿
同考試官訓導許　批〔此題本平易，但塲中作者或主未接物，或主已接物，間有兼動靜說者，紛紛不決，殊失本旨。惟此篇專主勤於爲善，深得孟子本意，且措辭簡當，可取，可取。〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔辭理簡切，初學得之，可以起人爲善之心，宜中優選。〕
考試官教授邵　批〔發明孟子之意，透徹無遺。讀〕

能夙興而勉於善者，斯亦聖人之徒也。蓋樂於爲善，莫舜若也；人能夙興而勉於善，又豈非舜之徒也哉？宜乎孟子言之以勉人也。且夫善者，天下之公理，人心所固有，不以聖人而豐，不以衆人而嗇，但汨於物欲而失之尔。今有人焉，雞鳴之時，惕然而起，而能孳孳焉於性分之所固有者爲之，不敢有毫髮之少怠，
translation_en:
… those who know only after painful difficulty, as well as the distinctions between practicing with ease, practicing for advantage, and practicing by strenuous effort; yet if one can strengthen oneself ceaselessly, one will gradually advance from strenuous effort to natural ease. Who would say that the sincerity of the sage can never be reached through learning? Therefore a former Confucian scholar said: "Though the paths by which they enter are different, the realm at which they arrive is the same."

"He who rises at cockcrow and diligently does good is a follower of Shun."
Yao Jun 姚駿
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu 許 comments: [This topic is inherently straightforward, yet writers in the examination hall either argued that it refers to the state before engaging with external things, or argued that it refers to the state after engaging with things, while some spoke of combining activity and tranquility—arguing back and forth without resolution and completely missing the essential purport. Only this essay focuses exclusively on diligence in doing good, deeply grasping Mencius's original intent; moreover, its wording is concise and fitting. Commendable, commendable!]
Examiner and Instructor Weng 翁 comments: [Both language and principle are concise and to the point. If beginning students obtain this, it can inspire in people the determination to do good. It deserves to be placed among the top selections.]
Examiner and Instructor Shao 邵 comments: [It elucidates Mencius's meaning thoroughly, leaving nothing out. Reading …]

One who can rise early in the morning and strive at goodness is indeed a follower of the sage. For in delighting to do good, no one surpassed Shun; if a person can rise early and strive at goodness, how could he not be a follower of Shun? Fittingly did Mencius speak these words to encourage people. Moreover, goodness is the universal principle of the world, inherent in the human mind; it is neither abundant in sages nor scanty in ordinary people, though ordinary people become submerged in material desires and lose it. Suppose there is a person who rises vigilantly at cockcrow and is able to practice diligently what is inherent in his allotted nature, not daring to slacken by even a hair's breadth …

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
則爲善之心可謂勤矣夙興而能孳孳焉於職
分之所當爲者爲之不敢有須刻之少忽則爲善之
心可謂篤矣夫旣勤於爲善吾知是人也雖未能如
舜之舍己從人然所趨者正而無偏陂反側之非亦
是舜之徒也雖未能如舜之由仁義行然所向者善
而無放僻邪侈之失亦是舜之徒矣孟子言此其勉
人爲善之意何其切哉大抵戰國之時天下之人惟
利是求而不知善之當爲故孟子於此旣言孳孳爲
善爲舜之徒矣下文又言孳孳爲利者爲蹠之徒無
非所以勉人爲善戒人爲利是皆遏人欲而擴天理
也學者不可不察
易
===
剛上而尚賢能止健大正也不家食吉養賢也
謝諒
同考試官學正鄭　批〔此題本以卦變卦體及取尚賢之象以釋利貞不家食吉之辭但作者每昧之每〕
往往誤認以止健爲卦德及至措辭又多冗雜令人厭
觀忽得是作認得傳註直指卦體爲言且行文條暢
punctuated:
則爲善之心，可謂勤矣；夙興而能孳孳焉於職分之所當爲者爲之，不敢有須刻之少忽，則爲善之心，可謂篤矣。夫旣勤於爲善，吾知是人也，雖未能如舜之舍己從人，然所趨者正，而無偏陂反側之非，亦是舜之徒也；雖未能如舜之由仁義行，然所向者善，而無放僻邪侈之失，亦是舜之徒矣。孟子言此，其勉人爲善之意，何其切哉！大抵戰國之時，天下之人惟利是求，而不知善之當爲。故孟子於此旣言孳孳爲善爲舜之徒矣，下文又言孳孳爲利者爲蹠之徒，無非所以勉人爲善、戒人爲利，是皆遏人欲而擴天理也，學者不可不察。

《易》
「剛上而尚賢。能止健，大正也。不家食吉，養賢也。」
謝諒
同考試官學正鄭　批〔此題本以卦變、卦體，及取尚賢之象，以釋「利貞，不家食吉」之辭，但作者每昧之。每〕往往誤認以「止健」爲卦德，及至措辭，又多冗雜，令人厭觀。忽得是作，認得傳註直指卦體爲言，且行文條暢，
translation_en:
… then his heart in doing good may truly be called diligent! If, rising early, he can tirelessly practice what is required by his allotted duty without daring to neglect it for even a moment, then his heart in doing good may truly be called steadfast! Now, since he is diligent in doing good, I know that although such a person may not yet be able, like Shun, to set aside his own views and follow others, nevertheless what he pursues is upright and free from the wrongs of partiality, obliquity, or perversity—and so he too is a follower of Shun. And although he may not yet be able, like Shun, to act straight from benevolence and righteousness, nevertheless what he aims at is good and free from the failings of license, depravity, wickedness, or extravagance—and so he too is a follower of Shun. When Mencius spoke thus, how earnest was his intention to encourage people to do good! On the whole, during the Warring States period, people in the world sought only after profit and did not know that they ought to do good. Therefore, having stated here that he who tirelessly does good is a follower of Shun, Mencius goes on in the passage below to state that he who tirelessly seeks profit is a follower of Robber Zhi. All of this was simply meant to encourage people to do good and warn them against seeking profit—in every case curbing human desires and expanding the Principle of Heaven. Scholars must not fail to examine this carefully.

Classic of Changes (Yi)
"The firm ascends, and the worthy are honored. Being able to restrain strength—this is great correctness. 'Not eating at home brings good fortune'—this means nourishing the worthy."
By Xie Liang 謝諒
Associate Examiner Zheng, Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng), comments: 〔This topic originally uses the hexagram's line-transformation (guabian), its constituent trigrams (guati), and the image derived from honoring the worthy to explain the hexagram statement "advantageous to be firm and correct; not eating at home brings good fortune." Yet writers regularly fail to grasp this. Every [?]〕 All too often they mistakenly take "restraining strength" to refer to the hexagram's virtues (guade), and when it comes to their phrasing, it is mostly verbose and muddled, making it tiresome to read. Suddenly coming upon this composition, I found that the writer recognized that the commentary and notes speak directly of the constituent trigrams; moreover, the style flows smoothly and clearly, …

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
理亦精純錄之無恭
考試官教諭翁　批〔發揮彖辭明白醇正可取〕
考試官教授邵　批〔聖人彖易之旨發明殆盡允宜中選〕
人君尊賢以畜健本於正賢者仕進獲善有其由此聖
人明大畜之卦辭也蓋非大正之道則不能尊賢而
畜健非人君之養食賢又何以致賢者之仕進而不家
食哉且大畜之卦合乾艮而成體以卦變而言自需
而來九之陽剛本居於五今也變而居上則是六五
之君尊尚上九之賢所以有尚賢之義焉以卦體而
===
言艮為止而居上乾為健而居下則是以艮之止而
止乎乾之健所以有止健之義也唯其尚賢則必去
讒而遠色唯其止健則能制之而不肆欲是皆非已
之大正不能此吾夫子所以言尚賢止健皆必本於
大正也夫人君唯以賢而是尚則賢者又豈不食祿
於朝而食於家哉必也推其窮之所畜而為達之所
施如施其所畜於一國則食於國而吉矣施其所畜
於天下則食於天下而吉矣而其所以然者良由六
五之君能於乎尚而尊有德也使非待之誠而養之
punctuated:
理亦精純，錄之無恭。
考試官教諭翁　批〔發揮彖辭，明白醇正，可取。〕
考試官教授邵　批〔聖人彖《易》之旨，發明殆盡，允宜中選。〕

人君尊賢以畜健本於正，賢者仕進獲善有其由，此聖人明《大畜》之卦辭也。蓋非大正之道，則不能尊賢而畜健；非人君之養食賢，又何以致賢者之仕進而不家食哉？且《大畜》之卦，合《乾》、《艮》而成體。以卦變而言，自《需》而來，九之陽剛本居於五，今也變而居上，則是六五之君尊尚上九之賢，所以有尚賢之義焉。以卦體而言，《艮》為止而居上，《乾》為健而居下，則是以《艮》之止而止乎《乾》之健，所以有止健之義也。唯其尚賢，則必去讒而遠色；唯其止健，則能制之而不肆欲。是皆非已之大正不能，此吾夫子所以言尚賢、止健皆必本於大正也。夫人君唯以賢而是尚，則賢者又豈不食祿於朝而食於家哉？必也推其窮之所畜，而為達之所施。如施其所畜於一國，則食於國而吉矣；施其所畜於天下，則食於天下而吉矣。而其所以然者，良由六五之君能於乎尚而尊有德也。使非待之誠而養之
translation_en:
…and its reasoning is also refined and pure; we record it without reservation [?].
Examiner Weng, Instructor, comments: 〔Its elucidation of the Judgment (Tuan) is clear, pure, and orthodox; it is worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Shao, Professor, comments: 〔The import of the Sage's Judgment on the Changes (Yi) is elucidated almost completely; it truly deserves to be chosen.〕

That a ruler honors the worthy and restrains strength is rooted in rectitude, and that the worthy enter office and attain good fortune has its cause—this is how the Sage clarifies the hexagram statement of Great Taming (Daxu). For without the way of great rectitude, one cannot honor the worthy and restrain strength; and without the ruler's nourishing of the worthy, how could one bring the worthy to enter office and not eat at home? Moveover, the hexagram Great Taming combines the trigrams Qian and Gen to form its structure. Speaking in terms of hexagram transformation, it comes from Waiting (Xu): the yang firmness of the Nine originally occupied the fifth place, and now it has changed to occupy the topmost place; thus the ruler at the Six in the fifth place honors and exalts the worthy at the Nine at the top, which is why it has the meaning of exalting the worthy. Speaking in terms of the hexagram's constituent trigrams, Gen represents stopping and occupies the upper position, while Qian represents strength and occupies the lower position; thus it uses the stopping of Gen to restrain the strength of Qian, which is why it has the meaning of restraining strength. Only because he exalts the worthy will he surely dismiss slanderers and keep sensual beauty at a distance; only because he restrains strength is he able to control it and not indulge his desires. None of these is possible without great rectitude in oneself [?]; this is why our Master (Confucius) says that exalting the worthy and restraining strength must both be rooted in great rectitude. Now, since the ruler exalts only the worthy, how could the worthy not eat a stipend at court rather than eating at home? Surely they will extend what they have accumulated in obscurity and put it into practice in prominence. If they apply what they have accumulated to a single state, they will eat in that state and have good fortune; if they apply what they have accumulated to all under Heaven, they will eat in all under Heaven and have good fortune. And the reason it is so is truly because the ruler at the Six in the fifth place is able to exalt [?] and honor the virtuous. If he did not treat them with sincerity and nourish them with…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
尊則賢者皆高尚其事嘉遯貞吉矣何以不家食吉哉
此吾夫子所以明不家食而必由於君之養賢也䟽
抑又論之尊尚賢德能止至健皆大正之道也而賢
者之得禄亦必以大正焉夫尚賢非大正則好賢之
不篤止健非大正則多慾而不剛食禄非大正難逃
枉尺而直尋屈己而狗人者矣然則體大畜之君子
其可不以正乎
聖人以此洗心退藏於密吉凶與民同患神以
知來知以藏往
===
□□□□
李勳
同考試官學正鄭　批〔此篇說出聖人即易之妙蘊真知易〕〔者也是宜錄出以冠本經〕
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
考試官教諭翁　批〔易理具於聖人此篇能發明親〕〔切佳作也〕
考試官教授鄧　批〔聖人具理於心而妙於用講究詳〕〔明高中擬奉〕
知聖人具易書之理於一心當知聖人妙易書之用
punctuated:
尊，則賢者皆高尚其事，嘉遯貞吉矣，何以不家食吉哉？此吾夫子所以明不家食，而必由於君之養賢也。䟽抑又論之，尊尚賢德、能止至健，皆大正之道也；而賢者之得禄，亦必以大正焉。夫尚賢非大正，則好賢之不篤；止健非大正，則多慾而不剛；食禄非大正，難逃枉尺而直尋、屈己而狗人者矣。然則體《大畜》之君子，其可不以正乎？

「聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往。」
□□□□
李勳
同考試官學正鄭　批〔此篇說出聖人即易之妙蘊，真知易〕〔者也，是宜錄出以冠本經。〕
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
考試官教諭翁　批〔易理具於聖人，此篇能發明親〕〔切，佳作也。〕
考試官教授鄧　批〔聖人具理於心而妙於用，講究詳〕〔明，高中擬奉。〕

知聖人具《易》書之理於一心，當知聖人妙《易》書之用
translation_en:
…honor, then the worthy would all hold their own pursuits lofty and find good fortune in admirable retirement and firm correctness—how could there be the good fortune of not eating at home? This is why our Master made clear that not eating at home must stem from the ruler's nourishing of the worthy.

To discuss it further [?]: honoring and prizing worthy virtue and being able to restrain the utmost vigor are both the way of great rectitude; and when the worthy obtain official emoluments, it must also be through great rectitude. Now, if prizing the worthy is not done with great rectitude, then one's fondness for the worthy will not be sincere; if restraining vigor is not done with great rectitude, then one will have many desires and lack firmness; if partaking of official emoluments is not done with great rectitude, one can hardly escape bending a foot to straighten eight feet, or bending oneself to accommodate [狗 for 徇] others. This being so, how could a gentleman who embodies the hexagram "Great Accumulation" (Daxu) fail to abide by rectitude?

"The sage uses these to cleanse his heart, retires and conceals them in secrecy, and shares the anxieties of good and ill fortune with the people. Through numinousness he knows the future; through wisdom he stores the past."

[4 illegible characters]
By Li Xun 李勳.
Associate Examiner Zheng 鄭, Subprefectural Instructor, comments: [This essay brings out the subtle profundity that the sage himself is the Book of Changes (Yi). He is one who truly understands the Changes; it is fitting to record and publish this to head the essays on this Classic.]
[16 illegible characters]
Examiner Weng 翁, County Instructor, comments: [The principles of the Changes are complete within the sage; this essay is able to elucidate this intimately and切ly—a fine piece of work.]
Examiner Deng 鄧, Prefectural Instructor, comments: [The sage embodies the principles in his heart and is wondrous in their application. The exposition is detailed and clear; I propose presenting it for a high ranking.]

When one knows that the sage embodies the principles of the Book of Changes within his single heart, one ought to know how the sage wondrously applies the Book of Changes…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以應變者蓋聖人之心一易書之理也然其具於心者
既不外易之理而其所以應變者又豈能外是理哉
且夫圓神方知之德者易書之理也六爻之義易以
貢者亦易書之理也聖人體具三者之理以此洗心
而湛然純一退藏於密而寂然不動心之所有者即
圓神方知之德之所在心之所具者即變易以貢之
義之所存至精至密而無一隙之可窺至虛至明而
無一塵之或累茲非聖人具易書之理於一心乎然
理之具於心者無事之時也及其用也則感而遂通
===
故事之吉者慮人之不知趨則使之趨之而無疑是
與民同患於吉事之凶者慮人之不知避則使人避之
而無害是與民同患於凶吉凶之未兆至難知也而
吾心之神皆有以察其未然之機得失之報為易見
也而吾心之知皆有以具其已然之迹又非聖人妙
易書之用以應變乎雖然大傳是節乃言聖人備易
之理而具夫體用未至於用夫易也下文明於天之
道而察於民之故是興神物以前民用則言作易之
事至於聖人以此齊戒以神明其德乃言用易之事
punctuated: 以應變者，蓋聖人之心，一易書之理也。然其具於心者，既不外易之理，而其所以應變者，又豈能外是理哉？且夫圓神、方知之德者，易書之理也；六爻之義易以貢者，亦易書之理也。聖人體具三者之理，以此洗心而湛然純一，退藏於密而寂然不動。心之所有者，即圓神、方知之德之所在；心之所具者，即變易以貢之義之所存。至精至密，而無一隙之可窺；至虛至明，而無一塵之或累。茲非聖人具易書之理於一心乎？然理之具於心者，無事之時也；及其用也，則感而遂通。故事之吉者，慮人之不知趨，則使之趨之而無疑，是與民同患於吉；事之凶者，慮人之不知避，則使人避之而無害，是與民同患於凶。吉凶之未兆，至難知也，而吾心之神，皆有以察其未然之機；得失之報，為易見也，而吾心之知，皆有以具其已然之迹。又非聖人妙易書之用以應變乎？雖然，《大傳》是節，乃言聖人備易之理而具夫體用，未至於用夫易也。下文「明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用」，則言作易之事；至於「聖人以此齊戒，以神明其德」，乃言用易之事…
translation_en: …so as to respond to changes, for the mind of the sage is wholly one with the principle of the Book of Changes. Yet since what is embodied in his mind is nothing outside the principle of the Changes, how could the means by which he responds to changes lie outside this principle? Moreover, the virtues of the round and spiritual, and the square and wise, are the principle of the Book of Changes; and the meanings of the six lines, shifting in order to inform, are likewise the principle of the Book of Changes. The sage in his person embodies the principles of these three; with them he cleanses his mind so that it is limpid and purely one, withdrawing and storing them in secrecy so that he remains still and unmoved. Whatever is present in his mind is precisely where the virtues of the round and spiritual, and the square and wise, reside; whatever is contained in his mind is precisely where the meaning of shifting in order to inform is preserved. Utmost in subtlety and utmost in closeness, without a single crevice that can be spied into; utmost in emptiness and utmost in brightness, without a single speck of dust to encumber it—is this not the sage embodying the principle of the Book of Changes within his single mind? Yet the principle's being embodied in the mind pertains to when nothing is happening; when it comes to its functioning, upon being stirred it immediately penetrates. Therefore, in affairs that are auspicious, fearing that people do not know to pursue them, he causes them to pursue them without doubt—this is sharing the concerns of the people regarding good fortune; in affairs that are inauspicious, fearing that people do not know to avoid them, he causes people to avoid them without harm—this is sharing the concerns of the people regarding misfortune. Before good fortune and misfortune have given a sign, they are most difficult to know, yet the spirit of his mind is in every case able to discern the incipient springs of what has not yet come to pass; the requitals of gain and loss are easy to see, and the wisdom of his mind is in every case able to encompass the traces of what has already come to pass. Is this, again, not the sage marvelously exercising the function of the Book of Changes so as to respond to changes? Even so, this section of the Great Commentary (Dazhuan) speaks of the sage's being fully endowed with the principle of the Changes and possessing both substance and function, without yet coming to the actual use of the Changes. The following passage—"illuminating the Way of Heaven and discerning the conditions of the people, he thus instituted the spiritual things to anticipate the people's needs"—speaks of the making of the Changes; as for "the sage with these fasts and purifies himself, to render spiritual and bright his virtue," that speaks of the matter of using the Changes…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
也吁□亡用行是以當之者其唯古之聰明叡知神
武而不殺者夫
書
禹曰都帝愼乃在位帝曰俞禹曰安汝止惟幾
惟康其弼直惟動丕應徯志以昭受上帝天其
申命用休帝曰吁臣哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞
帝曰臣作朕股肱耳目
李　斌
同考試官教諭諸　批〔作此題者多冗泛一□令人〕
厭觀惟此篇講有發明文亦整飭佳作也
===
同考試官學正林　批〔此題場中作者往往以弼直〕
爲臣職之備而不知爲君德備於外曉得此卷辭
瞻理明寫出舜禹都俞氣象宛然在目兄非雜筆
所能到
考試官教諭翁　批〔措辭簡潔得舜禹告戒微旨當〕
是作者
考試官教授鄧　批〔說出舜禹弼直臣鄰之意殆無〕
餘蘊可嘉
punctuated:
也。吁！□亡用行，是以當之者，其唯古之聰明叡知、神武而不殺者夫！

《書》：「禹曰：『都！帝，愼乃在位。』帝曰：『俞。』禹曰：『安汝止，惟幾惟康，其弼直；惟動丕應徯志，以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。』帝曰：『吁！臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！』禹曰：『俞。』帝曰：『臣作朕股肱耳目。』」
李　斌
同考試官教諭諸　批：〔作此題者，多冗泛一□，令人〕厭觀。惟此篇講有發明，文亦整飭，佳作也。
同考試官學正林　批：〔此題場中作者，往往以「弼直」〕爲臣職之備，而不知爲君德備於外。曉得此卷辭瞻理明，寫出舜、禹都俞氣象，宛然在目，兄非雜筆所能到。
考試官教諭翁　批：〔措辭簡潔，得舜、禹告戒微旨，當〕是作者。
考試官教授鄧　批：〔說出舜、禹弼直、臣鄰之意，殆無〕餘蘊，可嘉。
translation_en:
… Alas! To have both [substance and] function put into practice [?]—is not the only one equal to this the ancient sage who possessed keenness of hearing and sight, far-reaching intelligence, and divine martial valor without resorting to killing?

Book of Documents (Shu):
"Yu said, 'Oh! Emperor, be cautious in the throne you occupy.' The Emperor said, 'Yes.' Yu said, 'Abide calmly in the point where you should rest; attend to the subtle springs of things and to what brings peace, and let your assistants be upright. Then when you move, there will be a grand response, as if the people had been waiting for your will; thus you will brightly receive the favor of the Supreme Lord, and Heaven will renew its mandate with blessings.' The Emperor said, 'Alas! Ministers, my associates! Associates, my ministers!' Yu said, 'Yes.' The Emperor said, 'My ministers act as my legs and arms, my ears and eyes.'"

By Li Bin 李斌.

Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu 諸 comments: "Those who wrote on this topic were mostly verbose, superficial, and uniform [?], making one weary of reading them. Only this essay brings out new insights in its exposition, and its prose is also well-ordered and disciplined—an excellent piece."

Associate Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Lin 林 comments: "Candidates in the examination hall writing on this topic frequently took 'having upright assistants' (bi zhi 弼直) as the perfection of ministerial duty, not realizing that it refers to the ruler's virtue being perfected externally. Upon reading [?] this paper, its diction is rich and its reasoning clear; it depicts the spirit of harmonious deliberation (du yu 都俞) between Shun and Yu as vividly as if it were right before one's eyes. Truly [?] it is beyond what an ordinary brush could achieve."

Examiner Instructor Weng 翁 comments: "Its phrasing is concise and succinct, grasping the subtle purport of Shun and Yu's mutual admonitions. Truly the work of an accomplished writer."

Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Deng 鄧 comments: "It sets forth the meaning of Shun and Yu's words on 'upright assistants' and 'ministers and associates' leaving almost nothing unexpressed. Commendable."

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
大臣謹位之言契乎君而推夫交儆之效聖君臣鄰
之嘆契乎臣而資以同體之義蓋君位固所當謹而
臣職尤所當儆今也大臣戒君而推所以謹位之意
聖君安得不反復咏嘆而資以同體之義哉昔者大
禹告舜既嘆美以發其端復稱帝以起其聽謂夫天
位惟艱帝不可不致其謹也故舜深然其言而禹則
推言其意以為人君之於心也必當順適乎道心之
正使不陷於人欲之危人君之於事也必當謹幾以
審其事之發惟康以省其事之安則君德備於內矣
===
至於左右輔弼之臣皆盡其繩愆糾謬之職前後有
位之士咸盡其責難陳善之恭則君德備於外矣由
是不動則已動則丕應徯志人之應我為何如以是
昭受上帝天其申命用休天之應我又何如帝舜在
此遂深感弼直之義而致咏嘆之辭謂之臣哉鄰哉
者言人臣當盡輔弼之職也謂之鄰哉臣哉者言盡
職乃所以為臣也於是禹即然其言而舜復推其義
以為臣之於君非徒與之共天位也作吾之股肱而
翼為之助在是矣非徒與之食天祿也作吾之耳目
punctuated: 大臣謹位之言契乎君，而推夫交儆之效；聖君臣鄰之嘆契乎臣，而資以同體之義。蓋君位固所當謹，而臣職尤所當儆。今也大臣戒君，而推所以謹位之意，聖君安得不反復咏嘆，而資以同體之義哉？昔者大禹告舜，既嘆美以發其端，復稱帝以起其聽，謂夫天位惟艱，帝不可不致其謹也。故舜深然其言，而禹則推言其意，以為人君之於心也，必當順適乎道心之正，使不陷於人欲之危；人君之於事也，必當謹幾以審其事之發，惟康以省其事之安，則君德備於內矣。至於左右輔弼之臣，皆盡其繩愆糾謬之職；前後有位之士，咸盡其責難陳善之恭，則君德備於外矣。由是不動則已，動則丕應徯志，人之應我為何如？以是昭受上帝，天其申命用休，天之應我又何如？帝舜在此，遂深感弼直之義，而致咏嘆之辭。謂之「臣哉鄰哉」者，言人臣當盡輔弼之職也；謂之「鄰哉臣哉」者，言盡職乃所以為臣也。於是禹即然其言，而舜復推其義，以為臣之於君，非徒與之共天位也，作吾之股肱，而翼為之助在是矣；非徒與之食天祿也，作吾之耳目，
translation_en:
The great minister’s words on being cautious in the sovereign’s position resonated with the ruler, and he extended them to the efficacy of mutual admonition; the sage ruler’s exclamation over his ministers and close associates resonated with the minister, and he relied upon the principle of sharing a single body. Indeed, the ruler’s position is certainly something that must be treated with caution, while the minister’s duty is especially something that requires vigilance. Now, when the great minister admonishes the ruler and elaborates on the meaning of being cautious in his position, how could the sage ruler not repeatedly chant and sigh in admiration, relying upon the principle of sharing a single body?

In antiquity, when Great Yu addressed Shun, having first sighed in praise to open his remarks, he again addressed him as Emperor to arouse his attention, saying that the Heaven-conferred position is truly arduous and the Emperor cannot fail to exercise his utmost caution. Therefore Shun deeply agreed with his words, and Yu then elaborated on their meaning, holding that with regard to his mind, a ruler of men must conform to the correctness of the moral mind so that it does not sink into the peril of human desires; and with regard to affairs, a ruler of men must be cautious about the subtleincipient springs in order to examine how affairs arise, and be mindful of stability in order to inspect how affairs are settled—then the ruler’s virtue is made complete within. As for the assisting and rectifying ministers on the left and right, when all fulfill their duties of correcting faults and impeaching errors, and the gentlemen holding office in front and behind all fulfill the reverence of demanding difficult achievements and setting forth what is good—then the ruler’s virtue is made complete without. From this, if he does not make a move, nothing more need be said; if he does move, there will be a grand response as if awaiting his will—how great then is humanity’s response to him! By this he brightly receives the favor of the Lord on High, and Heaven renews its mandate with blessings—how great too is Heaven’s response to him!

At this point Emperor Shun was deeply moved by the principle of assisting uprightness, and gave voice to words of chanting and admiration. Calling out, “Ministers indeed! Close associates indeed!” meant that a minister ought to fulfill his duty of assisting and rectifying; calling out, “Close associates indeed! Ministers indeed!” meant that fulfilling this duty is precisely what makes one a minister. Thereupon Yu immediately agreed with his words, and Shun again elaborated on their meaning, holding that in a minister’s relation to his ruler, he does not merely share the Heaven-conferred position with him—he acts as my legs and arms, and the aid of sheltering and acting lies therein; he does not merely consume the Heaven-conferred emoluments with him—he acts as my ears and eyes, …

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
而明聰之助在是矣其言臣□所以爲鄰之義何其至
哉吁帝舜之聖非不能盡謹位之實也大禹之賢非
不能盡臣鄰之職也今大禹不以其君之聖而忘責
難之恭帝舜不以其臣之賢而忘資助之意都俞吁
咈交相勸勉此有虞所以致雍熙泰和之治也歟
非佞折獄惟良折獄罔非在中察辭于差非從
惟從哀敬折獄明啓刑書胥占咸庶中正其刑
其罰其審克之
彭敎
===
同考試官敎諭諸　批〔作此題者講擇人處多矣之累講盡心處又多支泛殊無可觀求其不失〕
句擯而不失於理者此作得之
同考試官學正林　批〔此題頭緒雖多其要在乎擇人盡心而已然作者往往牽引題語爲講殊〕
無文采可觀獨此作能以註意組織成文非熟於
經者不能也
考試官敎諭翁　批〔以擇人盡心二者該括本題深合〕
傳旨
punctuated:
而明聰之助在是矣。其言臣□所以爲鄰之義，何其至哉！吁！帝舜之聖，非不能盡謹位之實也；大禹之賢，非不能盡臣鄰之職也。今大禹不以其君之聖而忘責難之恭，帝舜不以其臣之賢而忘資助之意，都俞吁咈，交相勸勉，此有虞所以致雍熙泰和之治也歟！

「非佞折獄，惟良折獄，罔非在中。察辭于差，非從惟從。哀敬折獄，明啓刑書胥占，咸庶中正。其刑其罰，其審克之。」
彭敎
同考試官敎諭諸　批：〔作此題者，講擇人處多矣之累，講盡心處又多支泛，殊無可觀。求其不失句擯而不失於理者，此作得之。〕
同考試官學正林　批：〔此題頭緒雖多，其要在乎擇人、盡心而已。然作者往往牽引題語爲講，殊無文采可觀。獨此作能以註意組織成文，非熟於經者不能也。〕
考試官敎諭翁　批：〔以擇人、盡心二者該括本題，深合傳旨。〕
translation_en:
…and the assistance of seeing and hearing clearly lies right here. How supreme is his explanation of the meaning of how a minister [?] acts as a close associate! Ah! With the sageliness of Emperor Shun, it was not that he was incapable of fulfilling the reality of being cautious on the throne; with the worthiness of the Great Yu, it was not that he was incapable of fulfilling the duty of a ministerial associate. Now, the Great Yu did not forget the reverence of urging difficult achievements upon his sovereign because of his ruler's sageliness, and Emperor Shun did not forget the intention of relying on assistance because of his minister's worthiness. Expressing agreement and voicing caution ("du, yu, xu, fu"), they mutually encouraged and exhorted one another—was this not how the虞 (Yu) dynasty achieved a governance of harmonious prosperity and supreme peace?

"It is not the artful-tongued who should decide criminal cases, but the truly good who should decide criminal cases; in nothing will they fail to hit the due mean. Examine the discrepancy in pleadings; do not follow what is false, but follow what is true. With compassion and reverence decide criminal cases; clearly open the law books and deliberate together, so that all may approximate the due mean and correctness. Whether imposing punishments or fines, examine them carefully and master them." [Book of Documents, "Punishments of Lü" (Lü xing)]

Peng Jiao 彭敎

Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhu commented: [Those who write on this topic mostly suffer from tediousness [?] when explaining the selection of men, and are mostly digressive and vague when explaining the exhaustion of the mind, offering nothing worth reading. If one seeks an essay that does not lose the structure of the sentences [?] and does not stray from principle, this piece has achieved it.]

Associate Examiner Director of Studies (xuezheng) Lin commented: [Although this topic has many threads, its essentials lie simply in selecting the right men and exhausting one's mind. Yet writers often merely drag in the words of the prompt to make their explanation, with no literary brilliance worth admiring at all. This piece alone is able to weave the meaning of the commentary into a coherent essay; no one who is not thoroughly familiar with the Classic could do this.]

Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Weng commented: [Encompassing this topic through the two aspects of selecting men and exhausting the mind, it deeply accords with the purport of the commentary.]

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授鄧　批〔經旨既明文亦典雅初考得之〕
賢王告諸侯以典獄既欲擇其人又欲盡其心也蓋
刑獄之重不擇其人則無敬忌之心不盡其心則有
怠忽之患穆王曁是爲諸侯告其善於訓刑者矣且
夫叅錯訊鞫極天下之勞者莫若獄也聽之甚可易
其人耶是故口才辯給變幻是非此便佞之人也以
是人典獄則愛憎徇己不出於公取舍任情不循乎
正豈可以折獄焉慈祥愷悌視民如傷此溫良長者
也以是人治獄則輕所當輕不失於縱重所當重不
===
傷於刻而無不在中焉此非聽獄者當擇其人乎然
聽獄之要在於察辭辭非情實終必有差故必於其
差而察之也察辭不可偏主必不然而然所以審輕
重而取中也既察其辭必惻怛敬畏推鞫以求其情
既得其情必詳明法律占度以同乎衆如此則皆庶
幾其無過咸矣於是重者刑之又當察之而盡其能
輕者罰之亦必審之而盡其力務使刑罰之各得乎
中正可也此非聽獄者當盡其心乎抑考呂刑一書
訓刑詳盡然大本則在敬與中也故既曰惟敬五刑
punctuated:
考試官教授鄧　批〔經旨既明，文亦典雅，初考得之。〕

賢王告諸侯以典獄，既欲擇其人，又欲盡其心也。蓋刑獄之重，不擇其人，則無敬忌之心；不盡其心，則有怠忽之患。穆王曁是爲諸侯告，其善於訓刑者矣。且夫叅錯訊鞫，極天下之勞者莫若獄也，聽之甚可易其人耶？是故口才辯給，變幻是非，此便佞之人也；以是人典獄，則愛憎徇己，不出於公，取舍任情，不循乎正，豈可以折獄焉？慈祥愷悌，視民如傷，此溫良長者也；以是人治獄，則輕所當輕，不失於縱，重所當重，不傷於刻，而無不在中焉。此非聽獄者當擇其人乎？然聽獄之要在於察辭。辭非情實，終必有差，故必於其差而察之也。察辭不可偏主，必不然而然，所以審輕重而取中也。既察其辭，必惻怛敬畏，推鞫以求其情；既得其情，必詳明法律，占度以同乎衆，如此則皆庶幾其無過咸矣。於是重者刑之，又當察之而盡其能；輕者罰之，亦必審之而盡其力，務使刑罰之各得乎中正可也。此非聽獄者當盡其心乎？抑考《呂刑》一書，訓刑詳盡，然大本則在敬與中也。故既曰「惟敬五刑」、
translation_en:
Examiner Deng, Confucian Instructor, comments: [Both the meaning of the Classic is clear and the prose is refined and elegant; it was selected at the first reading.]

When the worthy king instructed the feudal lords on administering judicial cases, he wished them both to select the right men and to exhaust their minds in the task. For given the gravity of punishments and litigation, if one does not select the right men, there will be no heart of reverence and caution; and if they do not exhaust their minds, there will be the danger of negligence and carelessness. When King Mu went on to announce this to the feudal lords, how skilled he was at giving instruction on punishments! Moreover, in cross-examining and interrogating, nothing in the world is more exhausting than judicial cases; in hearing them, how could one treat the choice of men lightly [?]? Therefore, those who are glib of tongue and artfully distort right and wrong are specious flatterers; if one uses such men to administer judicial cases, their likes and dislikes will follow selfish interest rather than public impartiality, and their acceptances and rejections will indulge personal whim rather than adhere to rectitude—how can they decide judicial cases? Those who are kind, benevolent, and easygoing, looking upon the people as if they were wounded, are gentle and virtuous elders; if one uses such men to govern judicial cases, they will mitigate what ought to be mitigated without erring into laxity, and penalize severely what ought to be penalized severely without erring into harshness, so that nothing fails to hit the mean. Is this not why those who hear judicial cases must select the right men? Yet the essential point in hearing judicial cases lies in examining the pleadings. If the pleadings do not reflect the true facts, in the end there will inevitably be discrepancies, and therefore one must examine them by means of those discrepancies. In examining the pleadings, one must not hold a preconceived bias, but must consider what seems not so as possibly so, thereby weighing gravity and lightness so as to grasp the mean. Having examined their pleadings, one must interrogate with compassion and reverent awe in order to seek out the true circumstances; having obtained the true circumstances, one must be clear and thorough regarding the laws and statutes, deliberating and measuring so as to accord with the consensus of the multitude; if one proceeds thus, all will come close to being entirely free of fault [?]. Thereupon, when subjecting grave offenses to corporal punishment, one must again examine them and exhaust one's ability; when subjecting light offenses to fines, one must likewise investigate them and exhaust one's strength, striving to ensure that punishments and fines each attain due centrality and uprightness. Is this not why those who hear judicial cases must exhaust their minds? Furthermore, if we examine the chapter "Punishments of Lü" (Lü xing), its instructions on punishments are detailed and exhaustive, yet its great foundation lies in reverence and the mean. Thus, having said "Reverently attend to the Five Punishments" and…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
朕敬于刑必又曰哀敬折獄用心以敬也旣曰觀于
五刑之中此又曰罔非在中蓋庶中正用法以中也
心與法而並用敬與中而兩存若穆王者其知所本
者歟
詩
旣醉而出並受其福醉而不出是謂伐德飲酒
孔嘉維其令儀
同考試官訓導許　批〔此篇理明文順識出武公自悔之意甚當〕　姚駿
===
考試官教諭翁　批〔形容飲酒得出而歸出不至伐德由可嘉可法〕
考試官教授邵　批〔此篇形容旣出不出者發伐德之意明白通暢可取〕
節於飲者全其譽過於飲者失其德此燕飲所以貴
乎儀之善也蓋燕飲惟在有其節而善其儀也使飲
不能節而儀有未善焉又何以全賓主之與譽而不失
在己之德哉昔是詩衛武公飲酒悔過而作此章上文
punctuated:
「朕敬于刑」，必又曰：「哀敬折獄」，用心以敬也。旣曰：「觀于五刑之中」，此又曰：「罔非在中」、「蓋庶中正」，用法以中也。心與法而並用，敬與中而兩存，若穆王者，其知所本者歟？

詩
「旣醉而出，並受其福。醉而不出，是謂伐德。飲酒孔嘉，維其令儀。」
同考試官訓導許　批〔此篇理明文順，識出武公自悔之意，甚當。〕　姚駿
考試官教諭翁　批〔形容飲酒得出而歸，出不至伐德，由可嘉可法。〕
考試官教授邵　批〔此篇形容旣出、不出者，發伐德之意，明白通暢，可取。〕

節於飲者全其譽，過於飲者失其德，此燕飲所以貴乎儀之善也。蓋燕飲惟在有其節而善其儀也，使飲不能節而儀有未善焉，又何以全賓主之與譽，而不失在己之德哉？昔是詩衛武公飲酒悔過而作，此章上文
translation_en:
… "We are reverent toward punishments," it must further say, "With compassion and reverence settle criminal cases," which is to apply one's mind with reverence. Having said, "Observe the mean in the five punishments," here it further says, "None are not in accordance with the mean" and "May they approximate the mean and correctness," which is to apply the law with the mean. Mind and law are employed together; reverence and the mean are both preserved. Someone like King Mu (Mu wang 穆王)—did he not understand what is fundamental?

Classic of Poetry (Shi 詩)
"When one leaves after becoming drunk, both host and guest receive the blessing. To get drunk and not leave—this is called ruining one's virtue. Drinking wine is very fine, provided one maintains good deportment."
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu 許 comments: 〔This essay is clear in reasoning and smooth in style; its identification of Duke Wu's (Wu gong 武公) sense of self-repentance is most fitting.〕 Yao Jun 姚駿
Examiner and Instructor Weng 翁 comments: 〔It describes drinking wine and knowing when to leave and return home, so that leaving prevents the ruining of one's virtue [?]; this is praiseworthy and worthy of emulation.〕
Examiner and Confucianyson Instructor (教授) Shao 邵 comments: 〔This essay describes both the one who leaves and the one who does not leave, bringing out the meaning of ruining one's virtue; it is clear, fluent, and worthy of selection.〕

He who is moderate in drinking preserves his reputation; he who is excessive in drinking loses his virtue. This is why, in banquet drinking, excellence of deportment is valued. Indeed, banquet drinking consists solely in maintaining moderation and perfecting one's deportment. If one cannot be moderate in drinking and one's deportment is less than good, how then can one preserve the mutual reputation of guest and host without losing the virtue within oneself? In ancient times, this ode was composed by Duke Wu of Wei (Wei Wu gong 衛武公) in repentance for his faults in drinking wine. After the preceding lines of this stanza …

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
既言其威儀之失至此復申其悔之之詞謂夫肆筵
設席之初沉爵奠斝之際所飲酒孔偕而禮意之周洽
獻酬交錯而情義之相孚于斯時也曰既醉止乎爲以
出庶不盡人之懽而能節之以禮矣賓主豈不並受
其福乎既醉以酒乎焉而退庶不虛人之賜而能將
之以德矣彼此豈不俱有美譽乎使或醉而不出湛
樂是從則必至於舍其坐遷而威儀幡幡矣寧乎不自
伐其德乎抑或迷而忘返沉湎是務則必至於亂我
籩豆而屢舞僛僛矣寧乎不自戕其性乎然亢恐誨爾
===
諄諄聽我藐藐也故復言之以爲人之飲酒所以孔
嘉者以其威儀抑抑德音秩秩而不至於有愆耳蘇
飲所以甚美者以其禮儀卒度笑語卒獲而弗罹乎
咎爾君子其可不致謹於此乎武公自悔而言及此
則其有文章而能以禮自防也爲何如哉不特此爾
武公進脩則見於衛風淇澳之篇自警則有大雅抑
戒之什此則有飲酒悔過之詩其作聖之功可謂至
矣宜乎生而稱爲有斐君子沒而謚爲睿聖武公也
punctuated: 既言其威儀之失，至此復申其悔之之詞。謂夫肆筵設席之初，沉爵奠斝之際，所飲酒孔偕而禮意之周洽，獻酬交錯而情義之相孚。于斯時也，曰既醉止乎，爲以出，庶不盡人之懽，而能節之以禮矣，賓主豈不並受其福乎？既醉以酒乎，焉而退，庶不虛人之賜，而能將之以德矣，彼此豈不俱有美譽乎？使或醉而不出，湛樂是從，則必至於舍其坐遷，而威儀幡幡矣，寧乎不自伐其德乎？抑或迷而忘返，沉湎是務，則必至於亂我籩豆，而屢舞僛僛矣，寧乎不自戕其性乎？然亢恐誨爾諄諄，聽我藐藐也，故復言之，以爲人之飲酒所以孔嘉者，以其威儀抑抑，德音秩秩，而不至於有愆耳；蘇飲所以甚美者，以其禮儀卒度，笑語卒獲，而弗罹乎咎爾。君子其可不致謹於此乎？武公自悔而言及此，則其有文章而能以禮自防也，爲何如哉！不特此爾，武公進脩則見於《衛風·淇澳》之篇，自警則有《大雅·抑》戒之什，此則有飲酒悔過之詩，其作聖之功可謂至矣。宜乎生而稱爲有斐君子，沒而謚爲睿聖武公也。
translation_en: …having already spoken of the loss of dignified demeanor, at this point reiterates the words of his remorse. He says that when the mats and seats are first spread out, and as the goblets are rinsed and the jade cups set down, the wine drunk is in complete harmony and the ritual intent is thorough and congenial; toasts and pledges are exchanged back and forth, and feelings and righteousness are in mutual accord. At such a time, if when already drunk one thereupon withdraws [?], one will nearly avoid exhausting others' goodwill and will be able to regulate it with ritual propriety—would not guest and host both receive blessings? When already drunk with wine, if one thereupon retires, one will nearly avoid rendering others' gifts in vain and will be able to sustain it with virtue—would not both parties alike enjoy a fine reputation? Suppose, however, that one gets drunk and does not leave, giving oneself over to indulgent pleasure; then it will inevitably come to abandoning one's seat and moving about, one's dignified demeanor becoming light and frivolous—how would this not be ruining one's own virtue? Or suppose one becomes befuddled and forgets to return home, making a business of wallowing in drink; then it will inevitably come to throwing the bamboo and wooden vessels into disorder and dancing about unsteadily time and again—how would this not be injuring one's own nature? Yet he still fears [?] that though he instructs you earnestly, you listen to him with disdainful indifference. Therefore he speaks of it again, holding that the reason a person's drinking of wine is so admirable is simply that his dignified demeanor is cautious and his virtuous words are orderly, so that he does not come to commit faults; and the reason banquet [?] drinking is so fine is simply that the ritual ceremonies are wholly according to measure and the laughing and talking are wholly appropriate, so that he does not incur blame. How could a gentleman not exercise the utmost caution in this? That Duke Wu (Wu gong 武公), in repenting of himself, spoke to this effect—how great indeed was his possession of refined accomplishment and his ability to guard himself through ritual propriety! And not only this: Duke Wu's cultivation and self-improvement are seen in the ode "Qi Ao" (淇澳, Cove of the Qi) in the Airs of Wei (Wei feng 衛風); for his self-admonition there is the piece of warning "Yi" (抑) in the Greater Odes (Da ya 大雅); and here there is this poem of repenting faults in drinking wine. His efforts at becoming a sage may truly be called supreme! Rightly indeed was he praised in life as an accomplished gentleman, and given in death the posthumous title of the Perspicacious and Sage Duke Wu (Ruisheng Wu gong 睿聖武公).

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
截彼淮浦王師之所王旅嘽嘽如飛如翰如江
如漢如山之苞如川之流緜緜翼翼不測不克
濯征徐國
王鏞
同考試官訓導許　批〔此題作者多以王師服淮浦遠人自服且措詞簡古必有□□〕〔王旅服徐方殊失本旨惟此作歸美宣王盛而〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔説王師敵愾之義□□中□〕〔死發揮見宣王中興之氣象〕
===
考試官教授邵　批〔發明王者之師有征無戰〕〔諸卷皆不及宜表出之以冠本經〕
王師至而有以威乎遠王師盛而足以伐乎遠夫遠
人未易威而伐之也今王師臨其地而有制勝之威
極其盛而有必勝之勢非中興仁義之師其能然哉
昔者宣王自將以伐淮北之夷而詩人美之謂夫淮
浦之地密邇徐方王化不沾也遠矣兵威不加也久
矣一旦宣王者出奮赫赫業業之威震如霆如雷之
怒進厥虎臣而戰陳於其所未敢輕而不妄動也然
punctuated:
「截彼淮浦，王師之所。王旅嘽嘽，如飛如翰，如江如漢，如山之苞，如川之流，緜緜翼翼，不測不克，濯征徐國。」
王鏞
同考試官訓導許批：〔此題作者多以王師服淮浦，遠人自服，且措詞簡古，必有□□〕〔王旅服徐方，殊失本旨。惟此作歸美宣王盛而〕
考試官教諭翁批：〔説王師敵愾之義，□□中□〕〔死，發揮見宣王中興之氣象。〕
考試官教授邵批：〔發明王者之師有征無戰，〕〔諸卷皆不及，宜表出之以冠本經。〕
王師至而有以威乎遠，王師盛而足以伐乎遠。夫遠人未易威而伐之也，今王師臨其地而有制勝之威，極其盛而有必勝之勢，非中興仁義之師，其能然哉？昔者宣王自將以伐淮北之夷，而詩人美之，謂夫淮浦之地，密邇徐方，王化不沾也遠矣，兵威不加也久矣。一旦宣王者出，奮赫赫業業之威，震如霆如雷之怒，進厥虎臣，而戰陳於其所，未敢輕而不妄動也。然
translation_en:
"Strictly in order along those banks of the Huai, the station of the King's army. The King's legions are numerous and grand, as if flying, as if winged, like the Jiang and like the Han, like the firm base of a mountain, like the rushing current of a river, continuous and orderly, unfathomable and invincible, marching in bright array against the state of Xu." [Classic of Poetry, Major Odes, "Changwu"]

By Wang Yong 王鏞

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu comments: [Note: Note lines are swapped across the double column] "On this topic, most writers take 'the King's army' as subjugating the banks of the Huai and 'the King's legions' as subjugating the region of Xu, thereby missing the fundamental meaning. Only this essay attributes the praise to King Xuan's flourishing virtue, whereby distant peoples submit of their own accord; moreover, its phrasing is concise and archaic, surely possessing […]."

Examiner and Instructor Weng comments: "It explains the righteous indignation of the King's army against the enemy, […] [?] and brings out the spirit of King Xuan's dynastic revival."

Examiner and Professor Shao comments: "It elucidates how a true king's army conducts punitive expeditions without needing to fight. None of the other papers match it; it should be singled out to head the essays on this Classic."

When the King's army arrives, it possesses the means to overawe those afar; when the King's army is in full force, it suffices to chastise those afar. Now, distant peoples are not easily overawed and chastised. Yet here, when the King's army approaches their territory, it possesses the majesty that commands victory, and at the height of its strength, it holds the momentum of certain triumph. Were it not the benevolent and righteous army of a dynastic revival, how could it be thus?

In antiquity, King Xuan personally led an expedition to chastise the Yi tribes north of the Huai River, and the poet praised him. He meant that those banks of the Huai lay in close proximity to the region of Xu; they had long been untouched by royal moral transformation, and for a long time military might had not been brought to bear upon them. Once King Xuan arose, he roused his awe-inspiring and formidable majesty and unleashed his thunderous wrath. Sending forth his tiger-like stalwart ministers, he arrayed his battle lines in that place, never daring to act lightly or make reckless moves. Yet…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
其兵威截然齊一自有以聳服其心而不敢犯焉時
維鷹揚鋪師旅於其地未嘗能掠而肆暴也然其軍
容肅然整齊自有以震驚其衆而不敢肖焉夫王師
截彼淮浦而能以制勝者如此則夫王旅嘽嘽之衆
而大爲征伐之舉也宜何如哉殆見如飛如翰而其
行爲甚疾如江如漢而其衆爲甚盛其靜也則如山
之苞而不可撼焉其動也則如川之流而不可禦焉
以至其屬則綿綿連絡而不絕其整則翼翼嚴肅而
不紊謀之深也孰得而測之氣之銳也孰得而克之
===
夫王者兵威氣勢之盛如此于焉濯征徐國以正其
不庭之罪而非掩襲而取也于焉肆伐徐方以示夫
天討之公而非窮兵黷武也卒之徐方來庭而四方
既平豈特兵威然哉亦惟王者之師有征無戰也抑
考宣王以義興師而征伐有功也匪直淮夷爲然觀
其北伐獫狁而獫狁于夷南征蠻荊而蠻荊來威西
伐羌戎而羌戎以定宜詩人有以播諸歌咏而著其
中興之大業於無窮也猗歟盛哉
春秋
punctuated:
其兵威截然齊一，自有以聳服其心，而不敢犯焉。時維鷹揚，鋪師旅於其地，未嘗能掠而肆暴也；然其軍容肅然整齊，自有以震驚其衆，而不敢肖焉。夫王師「截彼淮浦」而能以制勝者如此，則夫「王旅嘽嘽」之衆，而大爲征伐之舉也，宜何如哉？殆見「如飛如翰」，而其行爲甚疾；「如江如漢」，而其衆爲甚盛。其靜也，則「如山之苞」，而不可撼焉；其動也，則「如川之流」，而不可禦焉。以至其屬則「綿綿」連絡而不絕，其整則「翼翼」嚴肅而不紊。謀之深也，孰得而測之？氣之銳也，孰得而克之？夫王者兵威氣勢之盛如此，于焉濯征徐國，以正其不庭之罪，而非掩襲而取也；于焉肆伐徐方，以示夫天討之公，而非窮兵黷武也。卒之徐方來庭，而四方既平，豈特兵威然哉？亦惟王者之師，有征無戰也。抑考宣王以義興師，而征伐有功也，匪直淮夷爲然。觀其北伐獫狁，而獫狁于夷；南征蠻荊，而蠻荊來威；西伐羌戎，而羌戎以定。宜詩人有以播諸歌咏，而著其中興之大業於無窮也。猗歟盛哉！

春秋
translation_en:
…their military might was sharply uniform, naturally striking awe and submission into the enemy's hearts so that they did not dare to offend. At that time, soaring like eagles, they deployed their troops and brigades across that territory, yet never engaged in plundering or rampant violence; nevertheless, their martial array was solemnly orderly, naturally terrifying the enemy host so that they did not dare to contend [?]. Now, since the royal army in "bringing order to those banks of the Huai" was able to secure victory in this manner, then when "the royal brigades were numerous and mighty" and undertook a grand campaign of punitive expedition, what must that have been like? One would see them "like flying birds, like soaring wings," their march being exceedingly swift; "like the Yangzi, like the Han," their multitude being exceedingly grand. In their stillness, they were "like the base of a mountain," impossible to shake; in their movement, they were "like the flow of a river," impossible to withstand. Moreover, in their continuity they were "unbroken," linked together without interruption; in their orderliness they were "disciplined," solemn and without confusion. In the depth of their counsel, who could fathom them? In the sharpness of their spirit, who could overcome them? Now, such was the grandeur of the true king's military might and momentum; thereupon he grandly marched on the state of Xu to rectify its crime of failing to attend court, rather than taking it by surprise attack; thereupon he broadly struck the region of Xu to display the impartiality of Heaven's punishment, rather than exhausting the military in wanton aggression. In the end, the region of Xu came to court and the four quarters were pacified—how could this have been achieved by military might alone? It was simply because the army of a true king conducts punitive expeditions without needing pitched battles. Furthermore, if we examine how King Xuan raised armies in accordance with righteousness and achieved merit in his campaigns, it was not only the case with the Huai Yi. Looking at how in the north he struck the Xianyun and the Xianyun were pacified, in the south he marched on the Man of Jing and the Man of Jing came in awe, and in the west he struck the Qiang Rong and the Qiang Rong were thereby settled, it is fitting that the poet broadcast these deeds in song and verse, making manifest the great enterprise of his restoration for all eternity. Oh, how glorious!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
楚人侵鄭〔僖公二年〕楚人伐鄭〔僖公三年〕公會齊侯
宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐
楚次于陘〔僖公四年〕鄭伯逃歸不盟〔僖公五年〕楚人
伐宋〔僖公十六年〕楚人陳侯蔡侯鄭伯許男圍宋
〔僖公二十七年〕晉侯齊師宋師秦師及楚人戰于城
濮楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡
侯鄭伯許子莒子盟于踐土〔僖公二十八年〕
同考試官教諭楊　批〔士生於理明詞暢是篇也簡〕
〔濮可以觀晚論策俱稱蓋麟經中之表表者宜登〕
===
考試官教諭劉　批〔斷制詳明可以群議〕
〔此冠士於房〕
考試官教授邢　批〔詞嚴義正之文得聖人予奪之〕
〔旨推於此本經允協輿論〕
外夷僭貳國而伯主帖之則背義者可譏外夷僭大
國而伯主拄之則從義者可予此桓文之恤鄭宋雖
同而鄭宋之待桓文則異也嗟夫春秋齊荊蠻屢為鄭
患公當我僖公之初會盟方睦而與師以侵鄭明年復舉兵
punctuated:
「楚人侵鄭〔僖公二年〕，楚人伐鄭〔僖公三年〕，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘〔僖公四年〕，鄭伯逃歸不盟〔僖公五年〕，楚人伐宋〔僖公十六年〕，楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋〔僖公二十七年〕，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕，公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、許子、莒子盟于踐土〔僖公二十八年〕。」

同考試官教諭楊　批：〔士生於理明詞暢。是篇也，簡濮可以觀晚，論策俱稱，蓋《麟經》中之表表者，宜登。〕

考試官教諭劉　批：〔斷制詳明，可以群議，此冠士於房。〕

考試官教授邢　批：〔詞嚴義正之文，得聖人予奪之旨。推於此本經，允協輿論。〕

外夷僭貳國而伯主帖之，則背義者可譏；外夷僭大國而伯主拄之，則從義者可予。此桓、文之恤鄭、宋雖同，而鄭、宋之待桓、文則異也。嗟夫！春秋齊荊蠻屢為鄭患。公當我僖公之初，會盟方睦，而與師以侵鄭；明年復舉兵
translation_en:
"Men of Chu invaded Zheng [2nd year of Duke Xi]; men of Chu attacked Zheng [3rd year of Duke Xi]; the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Baron of Cao to invade Cai; Cai collapsed in rout, whereupon they attacked Chu and halted at Xing [4th year of Duke Xi]; the Earl of Zheng fled home and did not take part in the covenant [5th year of Duke Xi]; men of Chu attacked Song [16th year of Duke Xi]; men of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song [27th year of Duke Xi]; the Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought with the men of Chu at Chengpu, and the army of Chu suffered a crushing defeat [28th year of Duke Xi]; the Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Xu, and the Viscount of Ju to make a covenant at Jiantu [28th year of Duke Xi]."

Associate Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: [This scholar's grasp of principle is clear and his diction fluent. In this essay, its conciseness and unadorned quality [?] allow one to observe its depth [?], and his discourses and policy essays are all well-matched. He is indeed an outstanding figure among specialists in the Unicorn Classic (Spring and Autumn Annals) and ought to be placed on the list of graduates.]

Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: [The judgments and assessments are detailed and clear, worthy of comparison [?] with the deliberations of the group; thus we place this scholar first in his examination ward.]

Examiner and Instructor Xing comments: [Writing of rigorous diction and upright principle, which captures the Sage's intent in bestowing praise and blame. Ranking him first in this Classic truly accords with public opinion.]

When outer barbarians encroach upon a wavering [?] state and the hegemon brings it peace, then the one that turns its back on righteousness deserves censure; when outer barbarians encroach upon a major state and the hegemon props it up, then the one that follows righteousness deserves praise. Thus, although Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin were alike in relieving Zheng and Song, the ways in which Zheng and Song treated Huan and Wen were different. Alas! In the Spring and Autumn period, the southern barbarian Chu repeatedly [?] proved a menace to Zheng. At the beginning of the reign of our Duke Xi, just when meetings and covenants were harmonious, Chu raised [?] an army to invade Zheng; the following year it again mobilized troops…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以伐鄭侵而又伐無非欲逞威而兼併其土地也其
時若無齊桓以攘之鄭之爲鄭不亦殆哉幸而齊桓
主伯合八國之師爲伐楚之舉奇兵侵蔡以剪其羽
翼正兵次陘以擣其腹心自是楚人不敢抗衡而鄭
國之患少息矣使鄭伯果能一心輔齊以尊王則與
後日宋公之從義者同一予鄭也不爾方首止之有
盟而逃歸之遽見不顧前日之德反效匹夫之行其
背義之罪烏可逃耶迨夫齊伯既往楚患尤甚至我
僖公之季今日既率師旅以伐宋明日復援諸侯以
===
圍宋伐而又圍無厭欲肆强以荼毒真人民也是時
若無晉文以挫之宋之爲宋不亦危哉幸而晉文繼
伯因宋人之告急爲城濮之大戰東征西伐而楚師
奔走政子西而楚兵潰自是外夷之威漸熄而宋國
之圍已解矣使宋公不能刻意從晉以奬王則與向
日鄭伯之背義者同一譏宋也不然遄踐土之有盟
即率先而往會不忘前日之恩同伸奬王之義其從
義之榮可勝紀耶吁齊救而鄭叛則鄭之不德也可
知晉救而宋從則宋之知義也可見鄭惟背義故□□
punctuated: 以伐鄭。侵而又伐，無非欲逞威而兼併其土地也。其時若無齊桓以攘之，鄭之爲鄭不亦殆哉！幸而齊桓主伯，合八國之師，爲伐楚之舉：奇兵侵蔡，以剪其羽翼；正兵次陘，以擣其腹心。自是楚人不敢抗衡，而鄭國之患少息矣。使鄭伯果能一心輔齊以尊王，則與後日宋公之從義者同一予鄭也。不爾，方首止之有盟，而逃歸之遽見；不顧前日之德，反效匹夫之行，其背義之罪烏可逃耶？迨夫齊伯既往，楚患尤甚。至我僖公之季，今日既率師旅以伐宋，明日復援諸侯以圍宋。伐而又圍，無厭欲肆强以荼毒真人民也。是時若無晉文以挫之，宋之爲宋不亦危哉！幸而晉文繼伯，因宋人之告急，爲城濮之大戰：東征西伐而楚師奔走，政子西而楚兵潰。自是外夷之威漸熄，而宋國之圍已解矣。使宋公不能刻意從晉以奬王，則與向日鄭伯之背義者同一譏宋也。不然，遄踐土之有盟，即率先而往會；不忘前日之恩，同伸奬王之義，其從義之榮可勝紀耶？吁！齊救而鄭叛，則鄭之不德也可知；晉救而宋從，則宋之知義也可見。鄭惟背義，故□□
translation_en: …to attack Zheng. Invading and then attacking again, they wanted nothing less than to flaunt their might and annex its territory. At that time, had there not been Duke Huan of Qi (Qi Huan) to repel them, would not Zheng's very existence as Zheng have been in grave peril? Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi assumed the hegemony and united the armies of eight states to launch a campaign against Chu: a surprise force invaded Cai to clip its wings, while the main army halted at Xing to strike at its heart. From then on, the people of Chu dared not contend as equals, and the troubles of the state of Zheng abated somewhat. Had the Earl of Zheng truly been able to assist Qi with a single mind in honoring the King, Zheng would have been granted the same praise as the Duke of Song later received for following righteousness. Instead, just as the covenant at Shouzhi was being made, he was suddenly seen fleeing home; disregarding the kindness of the previous day, he instead imitated the conduct of a petty man—how could he escape the guilt of betraying righteousness? By the time the hegemony of Qi had passed, the menace of Chu grew even worse. Toward the end of the reign of our Duke Xi, one day they led troops to attack Song, and the next day they again rallied the feudal lords to besiege Song. Attacking and then besieging, in their insatiable greed [?] they wished to unleash their brute force to torment its [reading 其 for 真] people. At that time, had there not been Duke Wen of Jin (Jin Wen) to foil them, would not Song's very existence as Song have been in danger? Fortunately, Duke Wen of Jin succeeded to the hegemony, and in response to the urgent plea of the people of Song, fought the great battle of Chengpu: campaigning east and west [?], the Chu army was put to flight, and by attacking [reading 攻 for 政] Zixi, the Chu troops were routed. From then on, the might of the foreign barbarians gradually subsided, and the siege of the state of Song was lifted. Had the Duke of Song not devoted himself to following Jin in supporting the Royal House, Song would have been subjected to the same censure as the Earl of Zheng earlier received for betraying righteousness. On the contrary, as soon as the covenant at Jiantu was held, he took the lead in going to attend the meeting; not forgetting the grace of the previous day, he joined in extending the righteousness of supporting the King—how could the glory of his following righteousness ever be fully recounted? Alas! Qi rescued Zheng and yet Zheng rebelled, from which Zheng's lack of virtue can be known; Jin rescued Song and Song followed, from which Song's understanding of righteousness can be seen. Because Zheng alone betrayed righteousness, therefore [□□]…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
此所以不數年而復有楚患宋惟輔晉不貳此所以
二十餘年而無楚患也歟讀是經者不可不知
〔公及齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯會王〕
世子于首止〔僖公五年〕〔公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛〕
侯鄭伯許男曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕〔公會齊侯于〕
夾谷　齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕叔孫州
仇帥師墮郈　季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費〔定〕
〔公十二年〕
周重
===
同考試官教諭楊　批〔題本平易場中得此要致〕
〔者衆是篇說出齊桓禮明上下聖人化行內外之〕
〔意詞理俱到有學之士也〕
考試官教諭翁　批〔有議論有發越足見作手〕
考試官教授鄧　批〔春秋以尊王室正王制爲可云此〕
〔作深合經旨允宜甲選〕
禮明於上下而王室尊化行於內外而王制正此齊
桓首止葵丘之會聖人歸田墮邑之事春秋備書以
致意焉嘅自東遷以來下陵上替王室不尊者也久矣
punctuated:
此所以不數年而復有楚患；宋惟輔晉不貳，此所以二十餘年而無楚患也歟！讀是經者不可不知。
〔公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會王〕世子于首止。〔僖公五年〕〔公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛〕侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕〔公會齊侯于〕夾谷，齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔定公十年〕叔孫州仇帥師墮郈，季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。〔定〕〔公十二年〕
周重
同考試官教諭楊　批：〔題本平易，場中得此要致〕〔者衆。是篇說出齊桓禮明上下、聖人化行內外之〕〔意，詞理俱到，有學之士也。〕
考試官教諭翁　批：〔有議論，有發越，足見作手。〕
考試官教授鄧　批：〔《春秋》以尊王室、正王制爲可云。此〕〔作深合經旨，允宜甲選。〕
禮明於上下而王室尊，化行於內外而王制正。此齊桓首止、葵丘之會，聖人歸田、墮邑之事，《春秋》備書以致意焉。嘅自東遷以來，下陵上替，王室不尊者也久矣。
translation_en:
…and for this reason, within a few years it again suffered from the menace of Chu; whereas Song steadfastly assisted Jin without duplicity, and is this not why for more than twenty years it was free from the menace of Chu? Those who read this Classic must not fail to understand this.

[The Duke, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao met with the Royal] Heir Apparent at Shouzhi [fifth year of Duke Xi]. [The Duke met with the Grand宰 and Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the] Marquis [of Wei], the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu [ninth year of Duke Xi]. [The Duke met with the Marquis of Qi at] Jiagu; the people of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin [tenth year of Duke Ding]. Shusun Zhouqiu led a force to raze the walls of Hou; Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led a force to raze the walls of Bi [twelfth year of Duke Ding].

By Zhou Zhong 周重

Associate Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: [The topic is inherently straightforward, and many in the examination hall grasped its essential point. This essay brings out the meaning of how Duke Huan of Qi clarified ritual propriety between superior and inferior, and how the Sage's moral transformation operated both externally and internally. Both its diction and its reasoning are thorough; he is a scholar of true learning.]

Examiner and Instructor Weng comments: [There is sound argument and spirited expression, which suffices to show a skilled hand.]

Examiner and Professor Deng comments: [The Spring and Autumn Annals takes honoring the royal house and rectifying the royal institutions as its central message [?]. This composition deeply accords with the purport of the Classic and truly deserves top selection.]

When ritual propriety is clarified between superior and inferior, the royal house is honored; when moral transformation operates both externally and internally, the royal institutions are rectified. Such were the assemblies of Duke Huan of Qi at Shouzhi and Kuiqiu, and the Sage's achievements in securing the return of the lands and the razing of the fortified towns, which the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded in full in order to convey its message. Alas, ever since the eastern relocation of the Zhou capital, inferiors had encroached upon superiors and superiors had fallen into decline, so that the royal house had gone unhonored for a long time…

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
于時扶持周室者得不有賴於山東之齊哉幸而齊
桓主伯廼心王室因世子者兒疑桓則大合諸侯于首
止而尊以殊會之禮因宰孔下臨桓則再合諸侯于
葵丘而待以同會之禮然世子儲君也以殊會而尊
之則禮明於上矣宰孔人臣也以同會而待之則禮
明於下矣夫以周室陵夷之秋齊桓能尊之如此可
謂支一木於大厦之將顛於□砥柱於頹波之既潰矣
桓伯之功何其偉歟君夫春秋之季內強外黃□□
不明也甚矣斯時與復周道者得不有望於東魯之
===
聖哉幸而聖人用魯其道得行相君夾谷發夷不譚
夏之言而有以感齊人之歸三田行乎季孫出家不
藏甲之語而有以感叔季之墮二邑然三田既歸則
大國服義而化行於外矣二邑既墮則大夫効順而化
行於內矣夫以王制僭亂之餘聖人能正之若此可
見變齊至魯之驗變魯至道之機矣聖人之化何其
神歟雖然伯者之功終不可與聖化同日而語矣蓋
伯者假乎仁義故今日首止雖能尊王而後日緣陵
尤不免專封焉若聖人則純乎王道推之無不準動
punctuated: 于時扶持周室者，得不有賴於山東之齊哉？幸而齊桓主伯，廼心王室：因世子者兒疑，桓則大合諸侯于首止，而尊以殊會之禮；因宰孔下臨，桓則再合諸侯于葵丘，而待以同會之禮。然世子，儲君也，以殊會而尊之，則禮明於上矣；宰孔，人臣也，以同會而待之，則禮明於下矣。夫以周室陵夷之秋，齊桓能尊之如此，可謂支一木於大厦之將顛，於□砥柱於頹波之既潰矣。桓伯之功，何其偉歟！君夫春秋之季，內強外黃，□□不明也甚矣。斯時與復周道者，得不有望於東魯之聖哉？幸而聖人用魯，其道得行：相君夾谷，發「夷不譚夏」之言，而有以感齊人之歸三田；行乎季孫，出「家不藏甲」之語，而有以感叔季之墮二邑。然三田既歸，則大國服義而化行於外矣；二邑既墮，則大夫効順而化行於內矣。夫以王制僭亂之餘，聖人能正之若此，可見變齊至魯之驗、變魯至道之機矣。聖人之化，何其神歟！雖然，伯者之功，終不可與聖化同日而語矣。蓋伯者假乎仁義，故今日首止雖能尊王，而後日緣陵尤不免專封焉；若聖人則純乎王道，推之無不準，動…
translation_en:
At that time, could the upholding of the House of Zhou not depend on Qi to the east of the mountains? Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi presided as hegemon, keeping his heart devoted to the royal house. Because the Royal Heir Apparent was subject to suspicion [兒疑 -> 見疑?], Huan grandly assembled the feudal lords at Shouzhi and honored him with the ritual of a separate meeting; because the Royal Aide Kong descended to attend, Huan once again assembled the feudal lords at Kuiqiu and treated him with the ritual of a joint meeting. Now, the Royal Heir Apparent is the crown prince; by honoring him with a separate meeting, ritual propriety was made clear toward superiors. The Royal Aide Kong is a subject; by treating him with a joint meeting, ritual propriety was made clear toward inferiors. Truly, in an autumn when the House of Zhou was in decline, that Duke Huan of Qi was able to honor it like this may be called propping up a great mansion with a single timber just as it is about to topple, and [standing like?] a pillar rock amidst collapsing waves after they have already burst through. How magnificent was the achievement of Hegemon Huan!

As for [君夫 -> 若夫] the late Spring and Autumn period, with powerful lineages within and [overbearing states? 外黃 -> 外橫] without, [the royal institutions? □□] were extreme in their obscurity. At such a time, could the revival [與復 -> 興復] of the Way of Zhou not look with hope to the Sage of eastern Lu? Fortunately, the Sage was employed in Lu, and his Way was able to be practiced: assisting his ruler at Jiagu, he uttered the words that "barbarians must not disrupt [譚 -> 亂] the Chinese states," and thereby moved the men of Qi to return the three tracts of land; acting through Jisun, he pronounced the dictum that "a grandee's household does not store armor," and thereby moved the Shusun and Jisun clans to dismantle their two walled cities. Now, once the three tracts of land were returned, a great state submitted to righteousness and moral transformation operated abroad; once the two cities were dismantled, the grandees rendered obedience and moral transformation operated at home. Truly, in the aftermath of usurpation and disorder in the royal institutions, that the Sage was able to rectify them like this reveals the verification of "transforming Qi until it reaches the level of Lu" and the pivot of "transforming Lu until it reaches the Way." How marvelous was the moral transformation of the Sage!

Even so, the achievements of a hegemon can never be spoken of on the same day as the transformative influence of a sage. For a hegemon merely borrows benevolence and righteousness; thus, although at Shouzhi today he could honor the King, later at Yuanling he still could not avoid arrogating the authority to enfeoff. As for the Sage, he is pure in the Kingly Way: wherever he extends it, it never fails to be the standard; whenever he sets it in motion, …

title: 天順三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之無不出向使□無女樂之受則必與周道於□□
矣惜乎不能必直遂也噫
禮記
天子之五官曰司徒司馬司空司士司寇典司
五衆
